easy.q: Which is the best way to find out whether a plant grows faster in sunlight?
o: Ask a friend which one they feel is right
Grow two similar plants, one in sunlight and one in shade, and compare them
Read only the name of the plant
Water the plant and wait for a feeling
easy.why: Science finds answers by testing and comparing, not by feelings.

easy.q: Which body part do you mainly use to observe the colour of a flower?
easy.why: We see colours with our eyes.

easy.q: Kavya notices that ice melts faster in the sun than in the shade. This first step of science is called
easy.why: Noticing something carefully is observation.

easy.q: Science is best described as
o: finding out about the world through observation, questions and evidence
easy.why: Science depends on evidence, and anyone can do it anywhere.

easy.q: Which question can science answer by testing?
o: Which colour is the most beautiful?
Does salt dissolve faster in hot water than in cold water?
Is it good to be lucky?
easy.why: Only a question that can be tested by an experiment is a scientific question.

easy.q: Meena wants to know if a magnet attracts a steel spoon. What should she do?
o: Think about it for a whole day
Ask the price of the spoon
Bring the magnet near the spoon and see what happens
easy.why: A simple test gives direct evidence.

medium.q: Ravi says, 'Heavy things always sink in water.' Which plan best checks his claim?
o: Ask five friends what they think
Put many heavy and light objects in water and note which sink
medium.why: A claim should be tested on many different cases.

medium.q: In a fair test, how many conditions should you change at one time?
medium.why: Changing only one thing lets you know what caused the result.

medium.q: Asha measures a bean seedling: 2 cm on day 5, 5 cm on day 10, 9 cm on day 15. Which conclusion is supported by this data?
o: The seedling grew taller at every measurement
The seedling will stop growing at 9 cm
Sunlight alone causes all the growth
medium.why: Only the first statement is shown by the numbers given.

medium.q: Which of these is an observation and not an opinion?
o: The candle flame is yellow at the top
medium.why: An observation reports what is seen; words like pretty or boring are opinions.

medium.q: Why do scientists write their observations in a notebook instead of trusting memory?
o: It makes the results come out right
Memory can fail, and others can check written records
medium.why: Records are reliable and can be checked.

medium.q: Two groups test the same thing and get different results. What should they do first?
o: Check how each test was done and repeat it
medium.why: Different results mean the methods must be examined and the test repeated.

hard.q: Priya says her garden plants grew taller because she sang to them. She sang only to the plants near the window. What is wrong with her conclusion?
o: She measured the height in inches, not centimetres
She sang for too few minutes to count as an experiment
Plants kept indoors cannot be used in experiments
Plants near the window also got more sunlight, so singing was not the only difference
hard.why: A fair test changes only one thing.

hard.q: Zoya tests whether sunlight helps bean seedlings grow. One pot is in sunlight, one is in a cupboard. Which things should be the SAME in both pots?
o: Type of soil, amount of water and size of the pot
Place where the pot is kept
Height of the seedlings at the end
hard.why: Everything except the thing being tested must be kept the same.

hard.q: Which of these is a hypothesis that can be tested by an experiment?
o: Which colour of cloth is the prettiest in sunlight?
Dark cloth gets warmer than white cloth when kept in sunlight
Everyone should wear light clothes in summer
Sunlight is the main source of heat on Earth
hard.why: A hypothesis is a prediction you can check by a fair experiment; the others are opinions or known facts.

hard.q: A shop claims its tonic makes children taller because one child grew after taking it. What would give better evidence?
o: Checking the same child again after a month
Giving it to many children and comparing them with a similar group that did not take it
hard.why: Good evidence needs many cases and a comparison group.

hard.q: A black cat crossed the road, and later Sonu failed a test. He says the cat caused it. What would a scientist say?
o: It is certain, because the test came after the cat
Science cannot study cats or tests
One event after another does not prove a cause; it must be tested on many cases
hard.why: Happening one after another is not the same as one causing the other.

hard.q: Rahul's experiment gave a result that disagreed with his hypothesis. What is the best response?
o: Accept the result honestly and revise the hypothesis
Change the hypothesis before looking at the result
Repeat until the result agrees and ignore the others
Report only the part of the result that agrees
hard.why: Science follows evidence, even when it is unexpected.

easy.q: The variety of living things found on Earth is called
easy.why: Biodiversity means the variety of life.

easy.q: A small plant with a soft, green stem is called a
easy.why: Herbs have soft green stems.

easy.q: Leaves with parallel veins are seen in
easy.why: Grass has parallel venation.

easy.q: Which of these is a tree?
easy.why: A tree is tall with a thick, woody trunk.

easy.q: A camel can live in the desert because it
o: stores fat in its hump and can go long without water
easy.why: Its body is adapted to the dry desert.

easy.q: Why do we group living things?
o: To study them easily by looking at their similarities and differences
easy.why: Grouping makes the huge variety easier to study.

medium.q: A fish has gills, fins and a streamlined body. These features are examples of
medium.why: Body features suited to a habitat are adaptations.

medium.q: A leaf has a middle line with many branching veins forming a net. This is called
medium.why: Net-like veins are reticulate.

medium.q: Which animal is matched correctly with its habitat?
medium.why: Polar bears live in the cold Arctic; the other pairs are mismatched.

medium.q: Maya finds a plant about 1.5 m tall, with many thin woody stems branching from near the ground. It is most likely a
medium.why: Shrubs are medium-sized with several woody branches from the base.

medium.q: Which feature helps a cactus save water?
o: Roots that stay out of the soil
Many open pores on wide leaves
Thick fleshy stem and spines instead of broad leaves
medium.why: Spines lose very little water.

medium.q: A plant with a taproot generally has leaves with which venation?
medium.why: Taproot plants usually have net-veined leaves.

hard.q: Which plant is correctly paired with its root system and leaf venation?
hard.why: Grass-like plants such as wheat have fibrous roots and parallel veins; mango and gram have taproots and net veins.

hard.q: A bird has webbed feet, a flat broad bill and waterproof feathers. Where does it most likely live, and why?
o: Dense forest, because webbed feet help grip branches
Ponds and lakes, because webbed feet help it swim
Grassland, because a flat bill helps cut grass
Mountain cliff, because waterproof feathers suit snow
hard.why: Webbed feet and waterproof feathers are adaptations to life in water.

hard.q: Which of these does NOT make its own food using chlorophyll, and so depends on other organisms for food?
hard.why: Mushrooms are fungi and have no chlorophyll.

hard.q: Which grouping is correct?
o: Aquatic: cactus, lotus; desert: water lily
Aquatic: cactus; desert: lotus, water lily
Aquatic: lotus, water lily; desert: cactus
hard.why: Lotus and water lily live in water; cactus lives in dry places.

hard.q: When a forest is cut down, many animals living there disappear mainly because
o: they lose the food and shelter the forest provided
they prefer to migrate to the sea
new animals replace them at once
they dislike sunlight in open places
hard.why: Habitat loss removes food and shelter.

hard.q: A watermelon plant has a weak stem that spreads along the ground. It is a
hard.why: Creepers have weak stems that spread on the ground; climbers climb on supports.

easy.q: Which nutrient mainly gives us energy?
easy.why: Rice and roti are rich in carbohydrates.

easy.q: Which nutrient helps build and repair the body?
easy.why: Proteins are body-building foods, found in dal and eggs.

easy.q: A lack of vitamin C can cause
easy.why: Vitamin C from citrus fruits prevents scurvy.

easy.q: Mindful eating means
o: eating slowly, paying attention to food and stopping when full
easy.why: It means being aware of what and how much you eat.

easy.q: Which food is the best source of protein?
easy.why: Pulses are rich in protein.

easy.q: A balanced diet contains
easy.why: The body needs many nutrients together.

medium.q: Lack of iodine in food can lead to
medium.why: Iodised salt prevents goitre.

medium.q: A child lacking vitamin D may develop
medium.why: Vitamin D is needed for strong bones.

medium.q: Why is fibre (roughage) in food important?
o: It gives a lot of energy
It helps digestion and prevents constipation
medium.why: Fibre helps food move through the gut.

medium.q: Which meal is the most balanced?
o: Roti, dal, vegetables, curd and a fruit
medium.why: It has carbohydrates, protein, vitamins, minerals and fibre.

medium.q: Anaemia is caused mainly by a lack of
medium.why: Iron makes haemoglobin in the blood.

medium.q: A packet's label lists sugar as the first ingredient. What does this suggest?
o: The packet contains more sugar than any other ingredient
medium.why: Ingredients are listed from the largest amount to the smallest.

hard.q: Ritu eats only rice, roti and potatoes every day, and often feels weak. Which pair of foods would best fill the gap in her diet?
hard.why: Her meals are all carbohydrate; dal and curd add protein.

hard.q: Which change makes a lunch of rice and potato curry more balanced?
o: Add dal and a green vegetable salad
hard.why: Dal adds protein; the salad adds vitamins and fibre.

hard.q: Which habit is NOT part of mindful eating?
o: Finishing a large packet of chips while watching television
hard.why: Distracted eating makes it easy to overeat.

hard.q: A boy cannot see well in dim light. Which pair of foods would help most?
hard.why: Vitamin A in these foods prevents night blindness.

hard.q: A 200 mL juice pack lists 18 g sugar. A 100 mL pack lists 10 g sugar. Which has more sugar per 100 mL?
o: The 200 mL pack, because 18 g is more than 10 g
The 100 mL pack (10 g per 100 mL)
Both have the same sugar per 100 mL
hard.why: 18 g in 200 mL is 9 g per 100 mL, less than 10 g.

hard.q: Which pair correctly matches a food to its main nutrient?
hard.why: Butter is rich in fats and lemon is rich in vitamin C.

easy.q: Which of these is attracted by a magnet?
easy.why: Iron is magnetic.

easy.q: The two ends of a bar magnet, where the force is strongest, are called
easy.why: Each magnet has a north and a south pole.

easy.q: When two like poles are brought near each other, they
easy.why: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.

easy.q: A freely hanging bar magnet comes to rest pointing roughly
easy.why: The Earth acts like a giant magnet.

easy.q: Which pair of materials are both magnetic?
easy.why: Iron, nickel and cobalt are magnetic materials.

easy.q: A magnetic compass is used to find
easy.why: The needle points north-south.

medium.q: The north pole of one magnet is brought near the south pole of another. What happens?
medium.why: Unlike poles attract.

medium.q: Which test best finds if a coin is magnetic?
o: Bring a magnet near and see if it is attracted
medium.why: Magnetic materials are attracted.

medium.q: Why does a compass needle always settle in one direction?
o: It is pulled by the Moon
It is heavier on one side
It is a small magnet lined up by the Earth's magnetism
medium.why: The Earth behaves like a large magnet.

medium.q: Which action can weaken a magnet?
o: Heating it or hitting it hard
Storing it in a dry box
Keeping unlike poles together with iron pieces
medium.why: Heat and hammering disturb the magnet.

medium.q: Why do some fridge doors have magnetic strips?
o: To keep the door shut by sticking to the iron body
medium.why: The magnet clings to the steel of the fridge.

medium.q: A mixture has iron filings and sand. How can you separate the iron filings quickly?
o: Move a magnet over the mixture
Sieve it with a cloth only
medium.why: Only the iron sticks to the magnet.

hard.q: A bar magnet is cut into two halves. What do you get?
o: One north-only and one south-only piece
Two smaller magnets, each with a north and south pole
One magnet and a piece of iron
hard.why: Every piece of a magnet has two poles.

hard.q: Both ends of a nail are attracted to a magnet. One end of a second object is repelled by the same magnet. The second object must be
hard.why: Only a magnet can repel; iron is only attracted.

hard.q: The ends of two bar magnets are marked A and B. End A attracts the north pole of a compass needle. So A is a
hard.why: A south pole attracts a north pole.

hard.q: A bag holds a steel pin, a copper wire and a plastic clip. A magnet is brought near the bag. Which is attracted?
o: the steel pin and the copper wire
hard.why: Steel contains iron; copper and plastic are non-magnetic.

hard.q: Rohan's compass needle points in a wrong direction near a loudspeaker. The best reason is
o: the Earth stops being a magnet
a magnet inside the speaker disturbs the needle
the plastic of the compass melts
hard.why: A nearby magnet can overpower the Earth's weak field.

hard.q: Bar magnets are stored in pairs with unlike poles together and soft iron pieces at the ends. Why?
o: To make them stronger than when new
To stop rust forming on the poles
To keep dust away from the iron
To stop them from losing their magnetism
hard.why: The keepers help them stay magnetised.

easy.q: What is the SI unit of length?
easy.why: The SI unit of length is the metre.

easy.q: How many metres are there in 1 kilometre?
A train moving on a straight track shows
easy.why: Motion along a straight line is linear.

easy.q: A child on a swing moves to and fro again and again. This is
easy.why: Motion that repeats after equal time is periodic.

easy.q: Which of these is NOT a standard unit of length?
easy.why: A handspan changes from person to person.

easy.q: To measure a pencil with a ruler, how should you place it?
o: Any mark at one end, and look from the side
Zero mark in the middle of the pencil
Zero mark at one end of the pencil, and look straight down at the other end
Hold the ruler loosely and estimate
easy.why: Start from zero and read with the eye directly above the mark.

medium.q: A road is 3.5 km long. How many metres is this?
A ribbon is 2.4 m long. Its length in centimetres is
One end of a pencil is at the 2.0 cm mark of a ruler and the other end at 11.5 cm. Its length is
A person sitting in a moving bus is at rest with respect to
medium.why: Rest or motion depends on the reference point.

medium.q: What is the best way to measure the length of the curved edge of a leaf?
o: Place a ruler straight across the curve
Lay a thread along the edge, then measure the thread with a ruler
Press a measuring tape flat on the leaf
medium.why: A thread bends along the curve and then can be straightened.

medium.q: Sunil starts a measurement from the 2 cm mark of a ruler because its end is broken. The line ends at the 17 cm mark. Its length is

hard.q: Riya walks 1.2 km to school and 1.2 km back, five days a week. How many metres does she walk in a week?
A thread laid along a winding road on a map is 45 cm long. The map scale is 1 cm = 2 km. The real road length is
Which set correctly matches each object with its motion?
o: Spinning top - linear; swinging pendulum - rotational; bullet train - periodic
Spinning top - rotational; swinging pendulum - periodic; bullet train on straight track - linear
Spinning top - periodic; swinging pendulum - linear; bullet train - rotational
Spinning top - linear; swinging pendulum - periodic; bullet train - rotational
hard.why: A top spins about an axis, a pendulum repeats to and fro, a train goes in a line.

hard.q: A man stands on a platform while a train passes. A passenger in the train looks at the man. Which statement is correct?
o: Only the train is moving, whoever looks
The man is at rest in every sense
Each is moving with respect to the other, so motion depends on the reference point
The passenger is at rest with respect to the platform
hard.why: The same object can be at rest or moving depending on the reference point.

hard.q: A rope 2 m 35 cm long is cut into pieces of 5 cm each. How many pieces are there?
A tape has its first 2 cm broken off. Aman puts the start of the object at the 2 cm mark but reads the far end, 62 cm, as the length. The true length is
hard.why: True length = 62 - 2 = 60 cm.

easy.q: Which material lets light pass through clearly?
easy.why: Glass is transparent.

easy.q: A material that dissolves in water is called
easy.why: Soluble means it dissolves.

easy.q: The shine of a metal surface is called
easy.why: Lustre means shininess.

easy.q: Which of these is translucent?
easy.why: Translucent materials let some light through but not a clear view.

easy.q: Which of these sinks in water?
easy.why: Iron is denser than water.

easy.q: Why are cooking pans made of metal?
o: Metals are good conductors of heat
easy.why: Metals pass heat quickly to the food.

medium.q: Which group has only opaque materials?
medium.why: Glass, air and butter paper let some light through.

medium.q: What do sugar and salt have in common?
o: Both are attracted by a magnet
medium.why: Both are soluble.

medium.q: Why is a raincoat made of plastic?
o: Plastic does not let water pass through
medium.why: Plastic is waterproof.

medium.q: Why are electric wires covered with plastic or rubber?
o: They do not conduct electricity, so they protect us from shocks
medium.why: Plastic and rubber are insulators.

medium.q: A cloth soaks up spilled water but a plastic sheet does not. This is because cloth
o: is insoluble so water runs off it
absorbs water, while plastic does not
medium.why: Cloth has tiny gaps that take in water.

medium.q: Ritu wants an ice-cream box to stay cold on a long journey. Which material is best?
medium.why: Thermocol is a poor conductor of heat.

hard.q: Material X is hard, shiny, sinks in water and is attracted by a magnet. X is most likely

hard.q: A torch is held behind three sheets. Through A the bulb is clearly seen, through B only a blurred glow, through C nothing. Which is correct?
o: A translucent, B transparent, C opaque
A transparent, B translucent, C opaque
A opaque, B translucent, C transparent
A transparent, B opaque, C translucent
hard.why: Clear view means transparent; blurred means translucent; none means opaque.

hard.q: Which statement is correct?
o: Salt is insoluble in water because it seems to vanish
Rubber is a good conductor of electricity
Materials that do not allow light to pass are opaque, for example wood

hard.q: Which material is best for the handle of a hot steel pan, and why?
o: Copper, because it conducts heat well and cooks faster
Aluminium, because it is light and shiny
Wood, because it is a poor conductor of heat
hard.why: A handle should not pass heat to the hand.

hard.q: Which set contains only things that float in water?
o: cork, empty plastic bottle, dry leaf
empty plastic bottle, stone, wooden spoon
hard.why: Iron, stone and glass sink.

hard.q: Glass breaks easily, yet it is used for windows. Why?
o: It is a good conductor of heat
It is transparent, so it lets light in while keeping wind and rain out
It is opaque so it gives privacy
hard.why: Usefulness depends on the property needed.

easy.q: Which instrument measures temperature?
easy.why: A thermometer measures how hot or cold something is.

easy.q: The normal temperature of a healthy person is about
easy.why: 37 °C is normal body temperature.

easy.q: Pure water boils at about
easy.why: At normal pressure water boils at 100 °C.

easy.q: Water freezes at
easy.why: Freezing point of water is 0 °C.

easy.q: The usual range of a clinical thermometer is
easy.why: It is made for the human body range.

easy.q: Which thermometer should be used to measure the temperature of boiling water?
easy.why: Its range goes up to 110 °C.

medium.q: Why should we not use our hand to judge temperature?
o: Our feeling of hot or cold depends on what the hand touched before
medium.why: Touch is not reliable for measuring temperature.

medium.q: Before using a clinical thermometer, one should
o: shake it so the mercury falls below 35 °C
medium.why: The mercury must start below the expected reading.

medium.q: A clinical thermometer reads 39 °C. This means the person
medium.why: 39 °C is above the normal 37 °C.

medium.q: While reading a laboratory thermometer in a beaker of water, the bulb should
o: touch the bottom of the beaker
rest against the side of the beaker
be inside the water without touching the bottom or sides
medium.why: The container bottom may be hotter than the water.

medium.q: Water at 5 °C is mixed with water at 45 °C. The mixture's temperature will be most likely
medium.why: Heat flows from hot to cold until they are equal.

medium.q: Why are digital thermometers preferred to mercury ones for fever?
o: Mercury is poisonous and glass can break
medium.why: A broken mercury thermometer is dangerous.

hard.q: A metal spoon at 80 °C is dropped into water at 30 °C. What happens?
o: The water becomes hotter than the spoon
The spoon cools and the water warms until both are at the same temperature
hard.why: Heat flows from the hotter to the colder object.

hard.q: A steel spoon feels colder than a wooden spoon in the same room. Why?
o: Steel is at a lower temperature
Wood is warmer than the room
Steel takes heat from the hand faster, though both are at room temperature
hard.why: Feeling cold is about heat leaving the hand, not actual temperature.

hard.q: A student reads a laboratory thermometer while its bulb touches the hot bottom of the beaker. The reading will be
hard.why: The bottom is hotter than the water.

hard.q: A clinical thermometer shows 38.5 °C. Without shaking it, it is placed in a healthy person with 37 °C. What does it show?
hard.why: The mercury does not fall on its own.

hard.q: Equal amounts of water at 10 °C and 70 °C are mixed. The temperature will be closest to
hard.why: The mixture settles midway between the two.

hard.q: Between the 30 °C and 40 °C marks of a thermometer there are 10 small divisions. The mercury stops at the 7th division after 30. The reading is
hard.why: 7 divisions of 1 °C each past 30 gives 37 °C.

easy.q: Water vapour is water in the ___ state.
easy.why: Vapour is the gas form.

easy.q: Ice changing to water is called
easy.why: Solid to liquid is melting.

easy.q: Water changing to ice is called
easy.why: Liquid to solid is freezing.

easy.q: Water drops form on the outside of a glass of cold water because

easy.why: Cold surfaces cool the vapour in air into drops.

easy.q: Water slowly turning into vapour from its surface at any temperature is called
easy.why: That is evaporation.

easy.q: On which day do wet clothes dry fastest?
easy.why: Heat and moving air speed up evaporation.

medium.q: Which form of water has its own fixed shape?
medium.why: Solids have a fixed shape.

medium.q: Wet clothes dry faster when spread out than when in a heap because
o: more surface is open to air
medium.why: A bigger exposed surface lets more water evaporate.

medium.q: Clouds form when
o: water vapour rises, cools and condenses into tiny droplets
medium.why: Condensation makes clouds.

medium.q: We feel cool when sweat dries from our skin because
o: evaporation takes heat from the body
medium.why: Evaporating water takes heat from the skin.

medium.q: Ice floats on water because ice is
o: lighter than the same amount of water
medium.why: Ice is less dense than water.

medium.q: A full closed glass bottle of water cracks in the freezer because
o: water shrinks and pulls the glass
medium.why: Ice takes more space than water.

hard.q: Which gives the order of changes when steam becomes water and then ice?
hard.why: Gas to liquid is condensation; liquid to solid is freezing.

hard.q: Three plates hold equal water: A in the sun, B in shade, C in the sun with a fan blowing. Which dries first and why?
o: B, because shade keeps water in
All dry at the same time
C, because heat and moving air both speed up evaporation
hard.why: Two helping factors act on C.

hard.q: Dew forms on grass on a cool morning because
o: water vapour in the air cools and condenses on the grass

hard.q: A student says water leaks through a steel tumbler of ice water. Which observation shows the drops come from air?
o: Drops appear on a warm dry tumbler
Drops also form outside when the tumbler is sealed with a lid and has no holes
The tumbler is made of steel
hard.why: A sealed tumbler with no leak still gets drops, so they come from air.

hard.q: Clothes dry more slowly in winter mainly because
hard.why: Evaporation is slower when it is cold.

hard.q: How is boiling different from evaporation?
o: Boiling happens only from the surface; evaporation throughout
Evaporation needs a fixed temperature; boiling does not
Evaporation happens at any temperature from the surface; boiling happens at a fixed temperature through the liquid
hard.why: Boiling bubbles form inside the liquid at the boiling point.

easy.q: Separating stones from rice by picking them out is called
easy.why: Handpicking is used when the pieces are large enough to see.

easy.q: Separating light husk from heavy grain using wind is called
easy.why: Wind blows away the lighter husk.

easy.q: Tea leaves are separated from tea by
easy.why: A strainer filters out the leaves.

easy.q: Salt is obtained from sea water by
easy.why: Water leaves as vapour, salt remains.

easy.q: Iron filings can be separated from sand by using
easy.why: Only iron is attracted.

easy.q: Separating grains from the stalks is called
easy.why: Threshing beats grain loose from stalks.

medium.q: In muddy water the mud settles and the clear water is poured off. The two steps are
medium.why: Settling is sedimentation; pouring off is decantation.

medium.q: What gives dry salt from a mixture of salt, sand and water?
medium.why: Filter out sand first, then evaporate the water.

medium.q: Which mixture can be separated by sieving?
o: wheat flour and lumps of bran
medium.why: Sieves separate by particle size.

medium.q: Filter paper separates sand from water because
o: its tiny holes let water through but not sand
medium.why: Filtration works by hole size.

medium.q: Butter is separated from curd by
medium.why: Churning separates fat from the liquid.

medium.q: Why can't filter paper separate salt dissolved in water?
o: Filter paper dissolves in salt water
Water cannot pass through wet paper
Dissolved salt passes through with the water
medium.why: Dissolved particles are too small to be caught.

hard.q: A mixture has iron filings, salt and sand. Which order separates all three?
o: Add water and filter, then magnet, then sieve
Evaporate first, then magnet, then filter
Filter first, then magnet, then winnow
Magnet, then add water and filter, then evaporate the filtrate
hard.why: Magnet removes iron; water dissolves salt; filter removes sand; evaporation gives salt.

hard.q: Tiny stones are about the same size as rice grains. Which method works best to remove them?
o: Handpicking, since a sieve cannot tell similar sizes apart
hard.why: Sieving needs a size difference.

hard.q: A farmer has wheat grains, chaff and small stones after threshing. Which steps suit best?
o: Winnowing to remove chaff, then handpicking or sieving to remove stones
hard.why: Wind removes light chaff; stones are removed by size or by hand.

hard.q: Oil floats on water in a jar. How can they be separated?
o: Let it settle and pour off the oil layer, or use a separating funnel
hard.why: Oil and water do not mix; filter paper lets both pass.

hard.q: A tea strainer removes tea leaves but not sugar because
o: the holes are too small for leaves
sugar dissolves and is smaller than the holes
hard.why: Dissolved particles pass through.

hard.q: Salt water is boiled in a pot with a lid, and drops collect on the lid. These drops are
hard.why: Salt stays behind when water turns to steam.

easy.q: Which of these is a living thing?
easy.why: A tree grows, breathes and reproduces.

easy.q: Living things need food mainly to get
easy.why: Food gives energy and growth material.

easy.q: Which gas do living things take in for respiration?
easy.why: Respiration uses oxygen.

easy.q: A touch-me-not plant folds its leaves when touched. This shows
easy.why: Living things respond to changes around them.

easy.q: Which is the correct order in a frog's life?
easy.why: The frog goes through these stages in order.

easy.q: A seed needs which of these to germinate?
easy.why: These three are needed for sprouting.

medium.q: Removal of waste products from the body is called
medium.why: Excretion removes wastes.

medium.q: Which of these does a toy car NOT do, though a puppy does?
medium.why: Only living things grow by themselves.

medium.q: The seed coat
medium.why: The seed coat guards the embryo.

medium.q: A tadpole breathes through gills. An adult frog breathes mainly through
medium.why: The frog's breathing organs change as it grows.

medium.q: Which pair of animals both lay eggs?
medium.why: Cow, cat, dog, rabbit, bat and whale give birth to young.

medium.q: Frog eggs have no hard shell yet survive because they
o: are laid in water inside a jelly-like layer
medium.why: The jelly layer protects and keeps them moist.

hard.q: A toy robot moves, makes sounds and uses batteries. Which living characteristics does it still lack?
hard.why: A robot cannot grow or reproduce.

hard.q: A chemical that kills algae is sprayed in a pond, and mosquito larvae there also die. Why?
o: Larvae need the chemical to live
The larvae feed on algae and lose their food
hard.why: Removing food kills the animals that feed on it.

hard.q: Which is the correct order of a mosquito's life cycle?
hard.why: Mosquitoes go egg, larva, pupa, adult.

hard.q: Birds eating grains suddenly fly off. This is best explained as
o: a response to a stimulus (sensing danger) that helps survival
hard.why: Living things respond to danger.

hard.q: Grain stored in a damp bag starts sprouting. Why, and how to avoid it?
o: Moisture lets seeds germinate; store grain dry
Light makes grain grow; store in sunlight
Cold causes sprouting; store warm and wet
Air stops sprouting; seal wet grain
hard.why: Seeds sprout when they get water.

hard.q: A student says a dry seed is non-living because it shows no signs. A correct reply is
o: It is non-living until it flowers
It is living but resting; with water, air and warmth it can germinate
It is living only when dry
hard.why: A seed stays alive in a resting state.

easy.q: Which of these is a natural resource?
easy.why: Water comes from nature.

easy.q: Which of these is a renewable resource?
easy.why: Sunlight is available again and again.

easy.q: Coal is a
easy.why: Coal took millions of years to form.

easy.q: Which fuel is commonly used in a scooter?
easy.why: Scooters run on petrol.

easy.q: The three Rs of conservation are
easy.why: These three save resources.

easy.q: Soil is formed by
o: slow breaking of rocks over a long time
easy.why: Rock weathering makes soil over thousands of years.

medium.q: Which group has only non-renewable resources?
medium.why: Wind, water and sunlight are renewable.

medium.q: Why should we save water?
o: Fresh water that is fit to use is limited
medium.why: Only a small share of water is usable.

medium.q: Which habit conserves resources?
o: Using a new plastic bag each time
Using a cloth bag again and again
medium.why: Reusing cuts waste.

medium.q: Burning fossil fuels mainly pollutes air by releasing
medium.why: Fumes harm air quality.

medium.q: It is difficult to regrow forests because
o: trees take many years to grow, and a forest also needs animals and soil
medium.why: A forest is a whole community that takes long to rebuild.

medium.q: Which resource can be renewed if we plant new ones as we cut?
medium.why: Planting new trees replaces those cut.

hard.q: A town of 2000 people uses 100 L of water per person daily. Water-saving reduces use by 20 per cent. How much water is saved per day?
hard.why: Total = 200000 L; 20 per cent of that is 40000 L.

hard.q: A family uses solar panels for electricity, a gas stove for cooking and a windmill to pump well water. How many renewable sources do they use?
hard.why: Solar and wind are renewable; cooking gas is not.

hard.q: Which statement about fossil fuels is correct?
o: They form in a few years under soil
They can be made from water in a factory
They are found only in forests
They formed over millions of years from dead plants and animals, so they cannot be replaced quickly
hard.why: Fossil fuels are non-renewable.

hard.q: A school collects old newspapers so they can be made into new paper. Which of the three Rs is this?
hard.why: Turning waste into new material is recycling.

hard.q: Rainwater harvesting helps mainly by
o: storing rain for later use and recharging groundwater
hard.why: It saves rainwater for use.

hard.q: Which is a correct view of renewable resources?
o: They can still run short if used faster than they are replaced
hard.why: Renewable does not mean unlimited.

easy.why: The Sun makes its own light.

easy.q: Which planet is nearest to the Sun?

easy.q: The natural satellite of the Earth is the
easy.why: A satellite goes around a planet.

easy.q: How many planets are in our Solar System?
easy.why: There are eight planets.

easy.q: In which direction does the Pole Star lie?
easy.why: The Pole Star lies almost due north.

medium.q: A group of stars that makes an imaginary pattern is a
medium.why: Patterns of stars are constellations.

medium.q: The galaxy we live in is called the
medium.why: Our Solar System is in the Milky Way.

medium.q: Day and night happen because
o: the Earth goes round the Sun
the Sun moves round the Earth
the Earth rotates on its axis
medium.why: Rotation turns places toward or away from the Sun.

medium.q: The Earth takes about how long to go once around the Sun?
medium.why: That is one year.

medium.q: Which is an artificial satellite?
medium.why: INSAT is made by people.

medium.q: Which is the brightest star in the night sky?
medium.why: Mars is a planet; Pole Star is much dimmer than Sirius.

hard.q: Which list gives planets in increasing distance from the Sun?

hard.q: Stars are huge but look like tiny dots because
o: they are made only of gas
they are extremely far from us
hard.why: Distance makes them look small.

hard.q: The Moon goes through all its phases in about

o: A planet makes its own light while a star reflects

easy.q: Choose the correct form: Meena ___ a letter every week.
easy.why: Habit with singular subject: writes.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: He ___ for an hour now.
easy.why: 'For an hour now' needs present perfect continuous.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: We ___ cricket yesterday.
easy.why: Yesterday needs simple past.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: She ___ to Delhi next month.
easy.why: Next month is future.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: I ___ my lunch already.
easy.why: Already + I: have finished.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: Look! It ___.
easy.why: 'Look!' points to what is happening now.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: When I reached, the film ___.
medium.why: Past perfect for the earlier action.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: At 9 p.m. yesterday, I ___ dinner.
medium.why: Past continuous for an action in progress at a past time.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: They ___ here since 2015.
medium.why: 'Since' + a point in time: present perfect.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius.
medium.why: A scientific fact uses simple present.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: By next June, he ___ here for ten years.
medium.why: Future perfect shows completion by a future time.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: Why ___ you late yesterday?
medium.why: Yesterday needs past: were.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: She has been living here since 2020.
She has lived here from 2020 since.
hard.why: 'Since' needs a perfect tense.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: The bell rang before the teacher had entered.
The bell has rung before the teacher entered.
The bell had rung before the teacher entered.
The bell had rung before the teacher enters.
hard.why: The earlier action takes past perfect, the later action takes simple past.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: I wish I know the answer.
I wish I knew the answer.
I wish I will know the answer.
I wish I am knowing the answer.
hard.why: 'Wish' about the present takes the past form.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: I have not seen her since Monday.
I did not see her since Monday.
I have not seen her for Monday.
I am not seeing her since Monday.
hard.why: 'Since' needs present perfect.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: As soon as he will arrive, I will call you.
As soon as he arrived, I will call you.
As soon as he arriving, I call you.
As soon as he arrives, I will call you.
hard.why: In time clauses about the future we use present, not 'will'.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: He always complains about the noise since a week.
He is always complaining about the noise.
hard.why: The continuous with 'always' shows an annoying habit; other options are ungrammatical.

easy.q: Choose the verb: The flowers ___ fresh.
easy.why: Plural flowers: are.

easy.q: Choose the verb: My parents ___ at home.
easy.why: Plural subject.

easy.q: Choose the verb: Sheela ___ a good singer.
easy.why: Singular subject: is.

easy.q: Choose the verb: Gold ___ a precious metal.
easy.why: Gold is singular.

easy.q: Choose the verb: Every boy ___ present today.
easy.why: Every takes a singular verb.

easy.q: Choose the verb: Tom and Jerry ___ friends.
easy.why: Joined by 'and': plural.

medium.q: Choose the verb: The team ___ practising on the ground.
medium.why: The team acts as one unit.

medium.q: Choose the verb: Physics ___ difficult for some.
medium.why: Subjects ending in -ics are singular.

medium.q: Choose the verb: Neither Raj nor his friends ___ late.
medium.why: The verb agrees with the nearer subject, friends.

medium.q: Choose the verb: The principal and teacher ___ coming. (one person)
medium.why: One person with two roles takes a singular verb.

medium.q: Choose the verb: The scissors ___ on the table.
medium.why: Scissors takes a plural verb.

medium.q: Choose the verb: Many a student ___ failed this exam.
medium.why: Many a is followed by a singular noun and verb.

hard.q: Choose the verb: Not only the teacher but also the students ___ present.
hard.why: The verb agrees with the nearer subject.

hard.q: Choose the verb: One of the best players ___ injured.
hard.why: The subject is 'One'.

hard.q: Choose the verb: The quality of the mangoes ___ poor.
hard.why: The subject is 'quality', not 'mangoes'.

hard.q: Choose the verb: Fifty kilometres ___ a long distance to walk.
hard.why: A distance as a whole is singular.

hard.q: Choose the verb: Each of the girls ___ given a prize.
hard.why: Each is singular.

hard.q: Choose the verb: Half of the cake ___ eaten, and half of the biscuits ___ eaten too.
hard.why: The verb agrees with the noun after 'of': cake (singular), biscuits (plural).

easy.q: Choose the modal: ___ I come in, sir? (asking permission)
easy.why: 'May' is used to ask for permission.

easy.q: Choose the modal: Birds ___ fly. (ability)
easy.why: Can shows ability.

easy.q: Choose the modal: You ___ wear a helmet. (rule)
easy.why: Must shows obligation.

easy.q: Choose the word: I need ___ water. (a small quantity)
easy.why: Uncountable water: a little.

easy.q: Choose the word: She has ___ friends. (a large number)
easy.why: Countable plural: many.

easy.q: Choose the word: ___ girl in the class got a prize. (all of them, one by one)
easy.why: Every + singular noun.

medium.q: Choose the modal: He ___ be at home; his lights are on. (probably)
medium.why: Must can express strong probability.

medium.q: Choose the modal: ___ you help me, please? (polite request)
medium.why: Could is a polite request.

medium.q: Choose the modal: You ___ to respect your elders.
medium.why: Ought to shows duty.

medium.q: Choose the word: He gave me ___ advice. (not a number)
medium.why: Advice is uncountable.

medium.q: Choose the word: There were ___ people at the fair, so we left early. (too many)
medium.why: People are countable.

medium.q: Choose the word: ___ of the two roads leads to the village.
medium.why: Either means one of two.

hard.q: Which sentence shows a past habit?
o: We would play in the fields every evening.
We will play in the fields every evening.
We must play in the fields every evening.
We can play in the fields every evening.
hard.why: 'Would' can show past habit.

hard.q: Which sentence shows no need?
hard.why: Needn't means it is not necessary.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: She can't have see the message.
She cannot have seen the message.
She cannot has seen the message.
She can not saw the message.
hard.why: Modal + have + past participle.

hard.q: Which sentence uses the quantifier correctly?
o: Fewer students came than we expected.
Less students came than we expected.
Few students came than we expected.
Lesser students came than we expected.
hard.why: Use fewer with countable nouns.

hard.q: Which sentence shows prohibition?
hard.why: Mustn't = it is forbidden.

hard.q: Which sentence uses 'much' correctly?
hard.why: Time (meaning duration) is uncountable.

easy.q: Change to passive: Ravi writes a letter.
o: A letter was written by Ravi.
A letter is written by Ravi.
easy.why: Simple present passive: is/are + past participle.

easy.q: Which sentence is passive?
o: The window was broken by the ball.
easy.why: The window receives the action.

easy.q: Change to passive: The cat drank the milk.
o: The milk is drunk by the cat.
The milk was drank by the cat.
The milk was drunk by the cat.
easy.why: Simple past passive: was/were + participle.

easy.q: Change to passive: They will build a bridge.
o: A bridge is built by them.
A bridge was built by them.
A bridge will be built by them.
A bridge will built by them.
easy.why: Future passive: will be + participle.

easy.q: Which sentence is active?
o: The wall was painted by Anu.
easy.why: The subject Anu does the action.

easy.q: Change to passive: She sings a song.
o: A song was sung by her.
A song is sing by her.
A song is sung by her.
easy.why: Present passive uses is + participle.

medium.q: Change to passive: The students are cleaning the room.
o: The room is being cleaned by the students.
The room is cleaned by the students.
The room was being cleaned by the students.
The room has been cleaned by the students.
medium.why: Present continuous passive: is being + participle.

medium.q: Change to passive: The teacher was praising the boy.
o: The boy is being praised by the teacher.
The boy was praised by the teacher.
The boy was being praised by the teacher.
The boy has been praised by the teacher.
medium.why: Past continuous passive: was being + participle.

medium.q: Change to passive: Mohan has completed the project.
o: The project is completed by Mohan.
The project has been completed by Mohan.
The project was completed by Mohan.
The project had been completed by Mohan.
medium.why: Present perfect passive: has been + participle.

medium.q: Change to passive: Did Rani break the glass?

easy.q: Meena wants to know if a claim in science is true. What is the best thing to do?
o: Ask the loudest person in the class
Test it with an experiment and note the results
Read it again and again until it feels true
Accept it because it is in an old book
easy.why: Science checks ideas by observing and testing, not by who says them.

easy.q: After rain, Arjun asks why the puddle in his lane vanished by evening. This habit of asking questions is called
easy.why: Curiosity, asking why and how, is where science begins.

easy.q: Which of these will make a bulb glow when joined in a circuit with a cell and wires?
easy.why: Iron is a conductor of electricity; wood, rubber and plastic are insulators.

easy.q: Which of these changes cannot be reversed?
easy.why: Burning makes new substances such as ash, so the paper cannot be got back.

easy.why: A sundial reads time from the position of a shadow cast by the Sun.

medium.why: Metals like steel and iron conduct electricity; the eraser and plastic comb do not.

medium.q: Ravi says, "Science is only memorising facts from books." Which reply is best?
o: He is right, since all science is already known
Science is only done by adults in labs
Science also means asking questions and testing ideas by observing and experimenting
medium.why: Science grows through questions, observation and experiments, not just facts.

medium.q: Ice cream melting on a hot day and a cake baking in an oven are both changes. Which statement is correct?
o: Melting can be undone by cooling, but baking a cake cannot be undone
Baking can be undone by cooling the cake
medium.why: Cooling makes the melted ice cream solid again; a baked cake has new substances and cannot return to batter.

medium.q: The length of your shadow changes through the day. What can this help early people do?
o: Roughly tell the time of day
medium.why: As the Sun moves across the sky, shadow length and direction change in a regular way.

medium.q: A student sorts copper wire, chalk, aluminium foil and glass. Which two will conduct electricity?
medium.why: Copper and aluminium are metals and conduct electricity; chalk and glass do not.

medium.q: An experiment gives a result different from your guess. What is the best scientific response?
o: Change the result to match your guess
Check the method, repeat the test and accept what the evidence shows
medium.why: Evidence decides what is true; a guess that fails is still useful learning.

hard.q: A student finds that a graphite pencil lead lets a bulb glow, but wood does not. Which conclusion is correct?
o: Some non-metals, such as graphite, can conduct electricity
Wood is a better conductor than graphite
hard.why: Graphite is a non-metal that conducts, so conductors are not always metals.

hard.q: Sugar is heated in a pan. It melts, turns brown and smells burnt. On cooling it forms a hard black lump. Which conclusion is correct?
o: It is only melting, so sugar can be got back
The colour change is the only change
A new substance has formed, so the change cannot be reversed
hard.why: Browning and the burnt smell show a new substance, so this change is irreversible.

hard.q: Early people noticed that the Moon's shape repeats in about 29 to 30 days. How could this help them?
o: They could stop the Moon changing
They could count months and plan festivals and farming
They could make the Moon brighter
hard.why: A regular pattern in the sky works as a natural calendar.

hard.q: Sita wants to test whether a wider dish makes water dry faster. Which set-up is a fair test?
o: Same amount of water in a wide and a narrow dish, kept in the same place
A wide dish in the sun and a narrow dish in the shade
More water in the wide dish and less in the narrow dish
Wide dish near a fan and narrow dish in a cupboard
hard.why: A fair test changes only one thing; everything else must stay the same.

hard.q: Kabir throws a thick paper plane and a thin one and says thicker paper flies farther. The thick plane was also thrown harder. What is wrong?

He should not have thrown the thin plane
hard.why: Both paper thickness and throwing force differed, so we cannot tell which one caused the result.

hard.q: A battery runs down in a toy car. Which explanation is best?

Chemicals inside have been used up and cannot be restored by us simply
hard.why: The chemical change inside a cell uses up its materials, so it is not simply reversible.

medium.why: A switch closes or opens the gap in the circuit.

medium.q: How should two cells be joined to make a battery in a torch?
o: Positive terminal of one to negative terminal of the other
medium.why: In a battery, cells are joined one after the other with unlike terminals touching.

medium.q: Neha leaves the plastic covering on the wire ends that touch the cell. The cell and lamp are fine, but the lamp does not glow. Why?
o: Plastic is an insulator and blocks the current
Wires need no covering to glow
medium.why: Current cannot pass through the plastic, so the circuit is not complete.

medium.q: A lamp, cell and switch are connected, the switch is on and the cell is good, but the lamp does not glow. What is a likely cause?
o: The wire is made of copper
medium.why: A broken filament means the circuit is open at the lamp.

medium.q: An LED does not glow when connected to a cell, but glows when the connections to the cell are swapped. Why?
o: An LED works only when connected the correct way round
medium.why: An LED allows current in one direction only.

hard.q: Two lamps are joined one after the other in a single loop with a cell. One filament breaks. What happens to the other lamp?
o: It also goes off because the loop is broken
hard.why: In a single loop, a break anywhere stops the current everywhere.

hard.q: A cell, a lamp and two switches S1 and S2 are all joined one after another in one loop. When will the lamp glow?
o: Only when both switches are closed
hard.why: Both switches must be closed to complete the loop.

hard.q: A student's circuit does not work. Which is NOT a likely cause?
o: A wire end is not touching a terminal
The glass of the lamp is transparent
hard.why: A transparent bulb is normal and does not stop the current.

hard.q: A cell is joined to lamp A with its own switch and to lamp B with its own switch, so that each lamp has a separate path. Only A's switch is closed. What happens?
o: A glows and B stays off
B glows and A stays off
hard.why: Each lamp has its own path, so closing one switch lights only that lamp.

hard.q: What is the best material choice for an electric switch?
o: Plastic contacts inside and a metal cover outside
Rubber contacts and a wooden cover
Metal contacts and a metal cover
Metal contacts inside and a plastic cover outside
hard.why: Metal lets current pass in the circuit, and plastic protects the user.

hard.q: A student places a steel spoon, a rubber band, a pencil lead, chalk and a plastic pen cap one at a time in a gap in a circuit. Which pair makes the lamp glow?
hard.why: Steel and graphite conduct electricity; rubber, chalk and plastic do not.

easy.q: The property that lets metals be beaten into thin sheets is called
easy.why: Malleable metals can be hammered into sheets, like aluminium foil.

easy.q: Which property allows copper to be drawn into thin wires?
easy.why: Ductile materials can be stretched into wires.

easy.q: A school bell is made of metal because metals
o: produce a ringing sound when struck
easy.why: This ringing property is called sonority.

easy.q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
easy.why: Mercury is the only common metal that is liquid at room temperature.

easy.q: The brown flaky layer on an iron gate left in rain is called
easy.why: Iron reacts with air and moisture to form rust.

easy.q: Which non-metal is used to purify drinking water?
easy.why: Chlorine kills germs in water.

medium.q: Which cheap metal is rolled into thin foldable sheets to wrap food?
medium.why: Aluminium is malleable, light and cheap.

medium.q: The handle of a cooking pan is made of plastic because plastic
o: is a good conductor of heat
is a poor conductor of heat
medium.why: A poor conductor keeps the handle from getting hot.

medium.q: Why are gold and silver good for making ornaments?
o: They shine, can be shaped easily and do not rust quickly
medium.why: Lustre, malleability and corrosion resistance make them suitable.

medium.q: Magnesium burns in air to form a white powder. Its solution in water will turn
medium.why: Metal oxides are generally basic.

medium.q: Sulfur burns to form a gas. When it dissolves in water, the solution
medium.why: Non-metal oxides are generally acidic.

medium.q: Which iron nail will rust fastest after a week?
o: One kept in tap water open to air
One in dry air with a drying agent
medium.why: Rusting needs both air and moisture.

hard.q: Nail A is coated with oil, nail B is in water and nail C is in vinegar, all in the open. Which will rust least?
o: A, because oil keeps out air and water
hard.why: Oil blocks air and water.

hard.q: Why does an ironsmith heat iron red-hot before hammering it?
o: Heat makes iron softer, so it is easier to shape
Heat stops iron being a metal
hard.why: Hot iron is more malleable.

hard.q: Why does painting an iron gate prevent rusting?
o: The paint changes iron into copper
The paint separates the iron from air and moisture
The paint removes oxygen from air
hard.why: Rusting needs air and moisture.

hard.q: Why are aluminium wires used in overhead power lines?
o: It is a good conductor, light and can be drawn into wires
hard.why: Good conduction, low weight and ductility make aluminium suitable.

hard.q: A student hits a lump of coal and a copper piece with a hammer. The coal breaks, the copper flattens. Conclusion?
o: Coal is brittle and copper is malleable
hard.why: Non-metals like coal are brittle; metals are malleable.

hard.q: X is shiny, can be drawn into wires and rings when struck. Y is dull and crumbles on hitting. Z is a shiny liquid. Which are metals?
hard.why: Shine, ductility and sonority are metal properties, and mercury is a liquid metal.

easy.q: Melting of ice is a
easy.why: No new substance forms when ice melts.

easy.q: Rusting of an iron gate is a
easy.why: Rust is a new substance.

easy.q: Which is a chemical change?
easy.why: Burning makes ash and gases.

easy.q: Lime water turns milky when which gas passes through?
easy.why: Carbon dioxide reacts with lime water.

easy.q: Which does NOT form a new substance?
easy.why: Dissolving is physical.

easy.q: Burning a substance in air with heat and light is called
easy.why: Combustion is burning.

medium.q: Milk turns to curd. This is a
o: chemical change, as new substances form
medium.why: Curd cannot become milk.

medium.q: Which pair has two physical changes?
o: Dissolving salt in water and freezing water
medium.why: Dissolving and freezing give no new substance; rusting, burning, curdling and baking do.

medium.q: Burning magnesium ribbon gives a white powder. Why is it chemical?
o: A new substance, a white powder, forms
medium.why: The white powder is magnesium oxide, a new substance, so the change is chemical.

medium.q: Vinegar is added to baking soda. A gas forms that turns lime water milky. The gas is
medium.why: Baking soda and vinegar react to give carbon dioxide, which turns lime water milky.

medium.q: Candle wax near the flame melts and hardens again. This is
medium.why: Only the state changes between solid and liquid; no new substance forms.

medium.q: Which can be reversed?
medium.why: Freezing is a change of state and can be undone by warming; the others make new substances.

hard.q: Of boiling water, rusting, baking bread and crushing chalk, how many are chemical?
hard.why: Rusting and baking make new substances; boiling and crushing do not.

hard.q: A candle burns. Which statement is correct?
o: Wax melting is physical, wick and vapour burning is chemical
hard.why: The melting of wax is physical, while burning of the wick and wax vapour is chemical.

hard.q: Rocks crack from heating and cooling, while acid rain slowly dissolves limestone. These are
hard.why: Cracking is physical; dissolving by acid is chemical.

hard.q: Vegetable peels become compost in a pit. This is
o: a chemical change that cannot be reversed
hard.why: Rotting makes new substances, so the change is chemical and not reversible.

hard.q: Which mixture will turn lime water milky?
hard.why: Only vinegar with baking soda gives carbon dioxide, which turns lime water milky.

hard.q: Why can a boiled egg not become raw again?
o: Heat caused a chemical change forming new substances
hard.why: Heat changes the egg's substances permanently, so it cannot be raw again.

easy.q: The bump in a boy's throat appears because of growth of the
easy.why: The voice box grows and the voice deepens.

easy.q: Chemicals that regulate growth in the body are called
easy.why: Hormones are chemical messengers that control growth and changes.

easy.q: The monthly discharge of blood in girls is called
easy.why: Menstruation is the monthly discharge of blood in girls during reproductive maturity.

easy.q: Pimples appear in adolescence mainly because
easy.why: Hormones make oil glands more active, which can block skin pores.

easy.q: The stage when the body becomes able to reproduce is
easy.why: Puberty is when the body becomes able to reproduce.

easy.q: Which should teenagers stay away from?
easy.why: Tobacco harms health and can cause addiction.

medium.q: Which change occurs in both boys and girls?
medium.why: Hair under the arms grows in both boys and girls; the other changes are specific to one.

medium.q: Which meal is best for a growing teenager?
medium.why: Growing teenagers need all nutrients, which a balanced meal provides.

medium.q: Which is a good hygiene habit during periods?
o: Change pads regularly and wash hands
medium.why: Regular changing and washing hands prevents infection.

medium.q: A boy's voice becomes deep as his
medium.why: The growing voice box deepens a boy's voice.

medium.q: A friend sends hurtful messages online. What should you do?
medium.why: Cyberbullying is harmful, and a trusted adult can help stop it.

medium.q: Priya feels happy then irritable in a day. This is
medium.why: Hormonal changes in the teenage years cause mood swings.

hard.q: A girl has a swelling in the neck. A doctor suspects lack of
hard.why: Lack of iodine can enlarge the thyroid gland in the neck, which needs a doctor's advice.

hard.q: Shalu says adolescence brings only physical changes. A better statement is
o: Emotional and social changes also occur
hard.why: Adolescence brings physical, emotional and social changes.

hard.q: Raju says trying tobacco once is harmless as he can quit anytime. Why wrong?
hard.why: Harmful substances can lead to addiction, so even one try is risky.

hard.q: Which statement about adolescence is incorrect?
o: It is a stage of growth
It starts at the same age in everyone
hard.why: Adolescence starts at different ages for different people.

hard.q: Asha's height shot up but her classmate Rani has not grown. This shows
hard.why: Adolescent growth starts at different ages in different people, which is normal.

hard.q: Friends press Dev to try a harmful substance. Best response?
o: Say no firmly and tell a trusted adult
hard.why: Saying no and telling an adult protects you from addiction.

easy.q: A steel spoon kept in hot tea becomes hot at the other end. Heat travels in the spoon by
easy.why: In solids heat passes from particle to particle without the material moving, which is conduction.

easy.q: Smoke from a chimney goes up because
o: hot air is lighter and rises
easy.why: Warm air is lighter and rises; this movement is convection.

easy.q: Heat from the Sun reaches us mainly by
easy.why: Radiation needs no medium, so it crosses empty space from the Sun.

easy.q: Which of these is a poor conductor of heat?
easy.why: Wood is a poor conductor; metals are good conductors.

easy.q: Water vapour changing to tiny droplets that form clouds is called
easy.why: Cooling vapour condenses into droplets that form clouds.

easy.q: Which clothes are most suitable in summer?
easy.why: Light colours absorb less heat from sunlight than dark colours.

medium.q: On a sunny afternoon at a seaside town, the breeze blows
o: from the land to the sea
from the sea to the land
medium.why: Land warms faster in the day; warm air over land rises and cooler air from the sea flows in.

medium.q: Woollen clothes keep us warm in winter because wool
medium.why: Wool traps air, which is a poor conductor, so body heat does not escape.

medium.q: When water is heated in a pan on a stove, hot water at the bottom moves up. This is
medium.why: Heated water rises and cooler water sinks, setting up convection currents.

medium.q: Why are hollow bricks used in the outer walls in hot places?
o: Air trapped inside slows heat entering
Air inside is a good conductor
medium.why: Air trapped in the hollows is a poor conductor, so less heat enters.

medium.q: Water from rain seeps fastest into
medium.why: Sand has larger gaps between grains, so water seeps through quickly.

medium.q: Water leaving leaves as vapour is called
medium.why: Transpiration is loss of water vapour from leaves.

hard.q: Where is a smoke detector best fitted in a room?
hard.why: Hot smoke rises, so a detector near the ceiling senses it first.

hard.q: An incense stick points downward. The smoke from its burning tip will
hard.why: Hot smoke is lighter than surrounding air, so it rises whichever way the stick points.

hard.q: A glass of lassi is placed inside a larger glass, leaving an air gap. Compared with a single glass, it
o: stays cool longer because the air gap is a poor conductor
hard.why: The air gap is a poor conductor, so heat enters the lassi slowly.

hard.q: At night in a coastal town, the breeze blows
o: from the sea to the land
from the land to the sea
hard.why: At night land cools faster than sea; warm air rises over the sea and cooler land air moves in to replace it.

hard.q: A city with concrete roads floods more than a village with soil. Why?
o: Concrete lets little rainwater seep in
hard.why: Concrete lets very little water seep in, so rainwater runs off and floods roads.

hard.q: Which pair is correctly matched?
o: Hot ladle handle: conduction; warmth felt from soup surface: radiation
Hot ladle handle: radiation; warmth felt from soup surface: conduction
hard.why: Heat moves along the metal handle by conduction and across air from the soup surface by radiation.

easy.q: The SI unit of time is the
easy.why: The second is the SI unit.

easy.q: Speed is calculated as
easy.why: Speed = distance / time.

easy.q: The time a pendulum takes for one complete to-and-fro swing is its
easy.why: Time period is time for one oscillation.

easy.q: The SI unit of speed is
easy.why: Distance in metres over time in seconds.

easy.q: An object moving in a straight line covering equal distances in equal times shows
easy.why: Uniform means constant speed.

easy.q: Which device records the distance travelled by a vehicle?
easy.why: An odometer counts distance.

medium.q: A car covers 150 km in 3 hours. Its speed is
A bus must cover 240 km at 60 km/h. The time taken is
A train runs at 20 m/s. In km/h this is
A cyclist rides at 6 m/s for 5 minutes. The distance covered is

Anu runs 100 m in 14 s and Bina runs 100 m in 12.5 s. Who is faster?
medium.why: Bina takes less time for the same distance: 100/12.5 = 8 m/s against about 7.1 m/s for Anu.

hard.q: A car runs at 90 km/h. Its speed in m/s is
A toy covers 5 m, 5 m, 5 m and 8 m in four successive seconds. Which is correct?
o: Its motion is non-uniform because the last distance differs
hard.why: Equal distances in equal times are needed for uniform motion; the last second differs.

hard.q: A bus travels 60 km in the first hour and 40 km in the next 2 hours. Its average speed is
hard.why: Average speed = total distance / total time = 100 km / 3 h = 33.3 km/h.

hard.q: A train goes at 54 km/h and a cyclist at 16 m/s. Which is faster?

easy.q: Saliva in the mouth begins the digestion of
easy.why: Saliva has an enzyme that acts on starch.

easy.q: The longest part of our digestive system is the
easy.why: The small intestine is about 6 metres long.

easy.q: Cows chewing food again after swallowing it is called
easy.why: The food brought back is called cud.

easy.q: The tiny air sacs in lungs where gases are exchanged are called
easy.why: Gas exchange occurs in alveoli.

easy.q: The gas that turns lime water milky is present in larger amount in
easy.why: Exhaled air has more CO2.

easy.q: Most water is absorbed from undigested food in the
easy.why: The large intestine absorbs water.

medium.q: When we breathe in, the diaphragm
o: moves up and chest becomes smaller
moves down and chest space increases
medium.why: Downward diaphragm increases chest volume.

medium.q: Blood carries digested food and oxygen to
medium.why: Blood carries food and oxygen to every cell of the body.

medium.q: Fish breathe using their
medium.why: Gills take oxygen from water.

medium.q: Which statement shows the difference between breathing and respiration?
o: Breathing moves air in and out; respiration releases energy from food in cells
medium.why: Breathing is the movement of air; respiration is the chemical release of energy in cells.

medium.q: Chewing a piece of chapati for a long time makes it taste sweet because
medium.why: Saliva contains an enzyme that breaks starch into sugar, which tastes sweet.

medium.q: An earthworm breathes through its
medium.why: Moist skin allows gas exchange.

hard.q: Birds have no teeth. Which organ grinds their food?
hard.why: Gizzard grinds with swallowed stones.

hard.q: After running, we breathe faster because
o: muscle cells need more oxygen to release energy
hard.why: Working muscles need more energy, so cells need more oxygen and we breathe faster.

hard.q: A frog's tadpole breathes with gills. The adult frog uses
hard.why: A tadpole breathes with gills in water; the adult frog breathes with lungs and through its moist skin.

hard.q: Why do cows chew cud?
o: Grass is tough, so partly digested food is chewed again
hard.why: Grass is tough, so a cow chews the partly digested cud again to digest it fully.

hard.q: A frog kept in a dry place has trouble because
o: its skin must stay moist to take in oxygen
hard.why: A frog takes in oxygen through its skin, which works only when the skin is moist.

hard.q: A student blows through a straw into lime water for a while and it turns milky. This shows
hard.why: Carbon dioxide turns lime water milky, so our breath must contain it.

easy.q: The process by which green plants make their own food using sunlight is called
easy.why: Plants combine carbon dioxide and water using sunlight to make food.

easy.q: Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?
easy.why: Carbon dioxide enters leaves and is used to make food.

easy.q: Which gas is released by plants during photosynthesis?
easy.why: Oxygen is a by-product of making food.

easy.q: The green pigment that traps sunlight in leaves is
easy.why: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy for photosynthesis.

easy.q: The tiny openings on the surface of leaves are called
easy.why: Gases and water vapour pass through stomata.

easy.q: Xylem vessels carry
o: water and minerals from roots to leaves
easy.why: Xylem carries water and minerals upward.

medium.q: Which part of a plant absorbs water and minerals from the soil?
medium.why: Roots take water and minerals from the soil.

medium.q: Phloem carries
o: food made in the leaves to other parts
medium.why: Phloem moves prepared food to all parts of the plant.

medium.q: A leaf kept in sunlight is boiled in alcohol and tested with iodine. A blue-black colour shows
medium.why: Iodine turns blue-black with starch, a product of photosynthesis.

medium.q: Which statement about plant respiration is correct?
o: Plants take in oxygen and give out carbon dioxide, day and night
Plants take in carbon dioxide only
medium.why: All living cells respire all the time.

medium.q: A potted plant is kept in complete darkness for 36 hours and a leaf is tested with iodine. The leaf
medium.why: In darkness there is no photosynthesis, so no starch is stored.

medium.q: A variegated leaf has green and white patches. After sunlight and an iodine test, which patches turn blue-black?
medium.why: Chlorophyll is needed for photosynthesis, so only green patches make starch.

hard.q: Which pair correctly gives the inputs of photosynthesis?
o: Carbon dioxide and water, with sunlight
hard.why: Plants use carbon dioxide, water and light to make food.

hard.q: Water rises from roots to the leaves of a tall tree mainly because
o: water evaporating from leaves pulls more water up through xylem
hard.why: Loss of water from leaves pulls water up.

hard.q: A polythene bag is tied over a leafy branch in sunshine. Droplets collect inside after a few hours because
o: the leaves lose water vapour through stomata
hard.why: Water vapour from leaves condenses on the cool bag.

hard.q: In bright sunlight, a plant's net gas exchange shows more oxygen released than used. Why?
o: Photosynthesis makes more oxygen than respiration uses
hard.why: Photosynthesis happens only in light, while respiration is continuous.

hard.q: A water plant in a jar gives off many bubbles in sunlight but few in shade. The bubbles are mostly
hard.why: More light means more photosynthesis, so more oxygen.

hard.q: A ring of bark is removed from a stem. Over days, the stem swells just above the ring because
o: food from leaves piles up where phloem is cut
hard.why: The phloem carrying food downward is blocked.

easy.q: An object that gives out its own light is called
easy.why: Luminous objects such as the Sun make their own light.

easy.q: We see the Moon because it
easy.why: The Moon does not make light; it reflects sunlight.

easy.q: Light travels in
easy.why: Light travels in straight lines, which is why shadows have sharp edges.

easy.q: Which material is opaque?
easy.why: Wood blocks light; clear glass, air and clean water let it pass.

easy.q: Frosted glass lets some light through but we cannot see clearly. It is
easy.why: Frosted glass lets light through but scatters it, so it is translucent.

easy.q: In a plane mirror, the left-right swap in the image is called
easy.why: A plane mirror swaps left and right, which is called lateral inversion.

medium.q: Which three things are needed to form a shadow?
o: Source of light, opaque object and screen
medium.why: A shadow forms when an opaque object blocks light.

medium.q: A periscope uses
o: two plane mirrors fixed at 45 degrees
medium.why: Two mirrors at 45 degrees turn light twice, letting you see over obstacles.

medium.q: A ray of light falls on a plane mirror at 40 degrees to the normal. The reflected ray makes with the normal an angle of
medium.why: The angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, so it is 40 degrees.

medium.q: The word AMBULANCE is written reversed on its front so that
o: it reads correctly in a driver's mirror
medium.why: The reversed word looks correct in the rear-view mirror of the driver ahead because of lateral inversion.

medium.q: The image formed by a pinhole camera is
medium.why: Rays from the top of an object pass the hole and reach the bottom of the screen, giving an inverted image.

medium.q: A torch is moved closer to a book on a table in a dark room. The book's shadow on the wall
medium.why: A source nearer the object blocks more light angles, so a bigger shadow forms.

hard.q: Between a lamp and a wall, a student places cardboard, wax paper and clear glass one at a time. The shadows are
hard.why: Opaque cardboard gives a dark shadow, wax paper a faint one, and clear glass almost none.

hard.q: In a periscope, the two mirrors are placed
o: parallel to each other, each at 45 degrees to the tube
hard.why: Mirrors parallel at 45 degrees turn the light twice so you see over a wall.

hard.q: We cannot see the shadow of a bird flying very high because
o: the shadow falls far away and becomes faint and spread out
hard.why: The shadow falls very far from the bird, so it is faint and spread out.

hard.q: The pinhole of a pinhole camera is made larger. The image becomes
hard.why: A bigger hole lets more light in, but rays spread, so the image is brighter yet blurred.

hard.q: Sunlight through tree leaves makes round bright patches on the ground because
o: small gaps work like pinholes forming round images of the Sun
hard.why: Each small gap acts as a pinhole and makes a round image of the Sun.

hard.q: A boy's shadow is longer at 4 pm than at noon because
o: the Sun is lower in the sky
hard.why: When the Sun is lower in the sky, shadows are longer.

easy.q: Day and night happen because the Earth
o: moves around the Sun in a day
moves closer to and away from the Sun
easy.why: As Earth spins, the half facing the Sun has day while the other half has night.

easy.q: The Earth completes one rotation in about
easy.why: Earth takes about 24 hours for one rotation, which makes one day and night.

easy.q: The Earth completes one revolution around the Sun in about
easy.why: The Earth takes about 365 days.

easy.q: The path of the Earth around the Sun is called its
easy.why: Earth's fixed path around the Sun is called its orbit.

easy.q: A solar eclipse happens when the
o: Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth
Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon
Sun comes between the Earth and the Moon
easy.why: The Moon passes between the Sun and Earth and blocks sunlight.

easy.q: A lunar eclipse happens when the
o: Moon is between the Sun and the Earth
Earth is between the Sun and the Moon
Sun is between the Earth and the Moon
Moon is farthest from the Earth
easy.why: Earth's shadow falls on the Moon when Earth lies between the Sun and Moon.

medium.q: Seasons change mainly because
o: Earth's axis is tilted as it goes around the Sun
Earth moves nearer to the Sun in summer
the Sun moves up and down
medium.why: The tilt changes how much sunlight each hemisphere gets during the year.

medium.q: The Sun seems to rise in the east because
o: the Sun really moves around the Earth
Earth rotates from west to east
the Earth goes around the Sun in a day
medium.why: Earth spins from west to east, so the Sun only appears to move from east to west.

medium.q: A leap year has an extra day because
o: Earth spins slower every fourth year
Earth takes about 365 1/4 days to go around the Sun
medium.why: The extra quarter days add up to one day every four years, added as 29 February.

medium.q: It is safe to watch a lunar eclipse with the eyes but not a solar eclipse because
o: the Moon is too hot to look at
a lunar eclipse is much brighter
a lunar eclipse happens only in the day
the Sun's light can damage the eyes even when it is partly hidden
medium.why: Looking at the Sun can damage the eyes, while the eclipsed Moon is not harmful to view.

medium.q: The stars seem to move across the night sky because
o: stars revolve around Earth every night
medium.why: Earth's spin makes stars appear to drift across the sky.

medium.q: Different stars are seen in different months because
o: stars move to new places each month
the Sun moves across the stars
medium.why: As Earth goes around the Sun, the night side faces different stars in different months.

hard.q: Which pairing is right?
o: Solar eclipse on new moon day; lunar eclipse on full moon day
Solar on full moon; lunar on new moon
hard.why: A solar eclipse needs the Moon between Sun and Earth (new moon); a lunar eclipse needs Earth between (full moon).

hard.q: If Earth's axis were not tilted, then
o: there would be no day and night
it would be summer everywhere all year
winter would last longer in India
hard.why: Without the tilt, sunlight would fall the same way all year, so there would be no seasons.

hard.q: A total solar eclipse is seen only from a narrow strip of Earth because
o: the Moon is larger than Earth
the Moon's dark shadow on Earth is small
eclipses happen only at the poles
hard.why: The Moon's darkest shadow is a small spot on Earth, so only a narrow strip sees totality.

hard.q: The smaller Moon can fully cover the Sun because
o: the Moon is larger than the Sun
the Sun is dimmer than the Moon
the Moon is much closer to Earth than the Sun is
the Moon is made of a dark material
hard.why: The Moon is much closer to us than the Sun, so it appears about the same size and can cover it.

hard.q: In June, days in the northern hemisphere are longer because
o: Earth is nearer to the Sun in June
the northern hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun
the Sun moves around the Earth
the Moon pulls sunlight to India
hard.why: The northern hemisphere tilted towards the Sun gets more hours of daylight.

hard.q: When it is summer in India (northern hemisphere) the southern hemisphere
o: also has summer, getting the same light
has winter because it is tilted away from the Sun
hard.why: When the northern hemisphere tilts towards the Sun, the southern hemisphere tilts away and has winter.
