easy.why: Past continuous interrupted by a past event.

easy.q: Choose the past participle of 'take'.
easy.why: Take - took - taken.

easy.q: Choose the past participle of 'write'.
easy.why: Write - wrote - written.

easy.q: Choose the correct form: By next year, I ___ school.
easy.why: Future perfect with 'by next year'.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: How long ___ you ___ here?
medium.why: Present perfect continuous for an action still going on.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: After she ___ the letter, she cried.
medium.why: Past perfect with 'after' for the first action.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: He ___ the door before the thief entered.
medium.why: Past perfect for the earlier action.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: If I had money, I ___ a car.
medium.why: Second conditional: would + base verb.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: If it rains, we ___ indoors.
medium.why: First conditional: present in if, will in result.

medium.q: Choose the correct form: I ___ the news when you called.
medium.why: An action in progress was interrupted.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: If she had studied harder, she would have passed.
If she studied harder, she would have passed yesterday.
If she had studied harder, she will pass.
If she has studied, she would have passed.
hard.why: Third conditional: had + participle; would have + participle.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: No sooner he had left than it started to rain.
No sooner had he left then it started to rain.
No sooner had he left than it started to rain.
No sooner he left when it started to rain.
hard.why: 'No sooner had ... than'.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: I have been waiting since morning.
I was waiting since morning now.
hard.why: 'Since' with an action still going needs the perfect continuous.

hard.q: Which sentence uses the verb form correctly?
o: The glass was broken by the child.
The glass was broke by the child.
The glass was breaked by the child.
The glass has broke by the child.
hard.why: Passive uses the past participle: broken.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: She said she has finished the work yesterday.
She says she had finished work tomorrow.
She said she will finished the work.
She said she had finished the work.
hard.why: Past reporting verb, past perfect for an earlier action.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: I wish I studied more last year.
I wish I had studied more.
I wish I have studied more.
I wish I would studied more.
hard.why: A wish about the past uses past perfect.

easy.q: Choose the verb: The children ___ playing in the garden.
easy.why: Plural children: are.

easy.q: Choose the verb: Mohit and his sister ___ here.
easy.why: Two subjects joined by and.

easy.q: Choose the verb: Nobody ___ the answer.
easy.why: Nobody is singular.

easy.q: Choose the verb: The pair of shoes ___ new.
easy.why: The subject is 'pair'.

easy.q: Choose the verb: The class ___ a test today. (acting as one unit)
easy.why: The class as a unit takes a singular verb.

easy.q: Choose the verb: Two kilos of sugar ___ enough.
easy.why: A quantity as a whole is singular.

medium.q: Choose the verb: Neither the boys nor the girl ___ ready.
medium.why: Verb agrees with the nearer subject: girl.

medium.q: Choose the verb: The number of players ___ eleven.
medium.why: 'The number of' is singular.

medium.q: Choose the verb: The poet and writer ___ honoured. (one person)
medium.why: One person: singular.

medium.q: Choose the verb: Economics ___ taught in Class 11.
medium.why: Subjects ending in -ics are singular.

medium.q: Choose the verb: A number of guests ___ arrived.
medium.why: 'A number of' means many: plural.

medium.q: Choose the verb: Each of the cars ___ a number plate.
medium.why: Each is singular.

hard.q: Choose the verb: Not only the captain but also the players ___ tired.
hard.why: Agrees with the nearer subject, players.

hard.q: Choose the verb: One of the books I bought ___ torn.
hard.why: The subject is 'one'.

hard.q: Choose the verb: The principal, with all his teachers, ___ attending the event.
hard.why: With does not make the subject plural.

hard.q: Choose the verb: Cattle ___ grazing in the field.
hard.why: Cattle is a plural noun.

hard.q: Choose the verb: Either of the two answers ___ correct.
hard.why: Either is singular.

hard.q: Choose the verb: There ___ many reasons for his absence.
hard.why: The real subject 'reasons' is plural.

easy.q: Change to passive: Rita bakes cakes.

easy.q: Change to passive: Dad will paint the gate.
o: The gate was painted by Dad.
The gate will paint by Dad.
The gate will be painted by Dad.
The gate is painted by Dad.
easy.why: Simple future: will be + participle.

easy.q: Change to passive: The boys broke the window.
o: The window is broken by the boys.
The window was broken by the boys.
The window broke by the boys.
The window was breaking by the boys.
easy.why: Simple past: was + participle.

easy.q: Change to passive: She writes a diary.
o: A diary is written by her.
A diary was written by her.
A diary is writing by her.
easy.why: Simple present passive.

easy.q: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
o: The cake was eaten by the guests.
easy.why: The cake receives the action.

easy.q: Change to passive: Priya opened the gift.
o: The gift is opened by Priya.
The gift was opened by Priya.
The gift was open by Priya.
easy.why: Simple past passive.

medium.q: Change to passive: The cook is preparing dinner.
o: Dinner is prepared by the cook.
Dinner was being prepared by the cook.
Dinner is being prepared by the cook.
Dinner has been prepared by the cook.
medium.why: Present continuous passive: is being + participle.

medium.q: Change to passive: They had finished the game.
o: The game had been finished by them.
The game has been finished by them.
The game was finished by them.
The game had finished by them.
medium.why: Past perfect passive.

medium.q: Change to passive: He has solved the puzzle.
o: The puzzle is solved by him.
The puzzle was solved by him.
The puzzle had been solved by him.
The puzzle has been solved by him.
medium.why: Present perfect passive.

medium.q: Change to passive: Who has broken the glass?
o: Who has the glass been broken?
By whom the glass was broken?
By whom has the glass been broken?
medium.why: Present perfect interrogative passive.

medium.q: Change to passive: You should obey the rules.
o: The rules should obey by you.
The rules should be obeyed by you.
The rules should have obeyed by you.
medium.why: Modal passive: should be + participle.

medium.q: Change to passive: Does she sing the song?
o: Does the song sung by her?
Is the song sing by her?
Was the song sung by her?
Is the song sung by her?
medium.why: Simple present question passive.

hard.q: Change to passive: Open the window.
hard.why: An imperative becomes 'Let ... be + participle'.

hard.q: Which sentence has the correct passive?
o: I taught English by my aunt.
English was taught me by my aunt was.
I was taught English by my aunt.
I am teaching English by my aunt.
hard.why: With two objects, 'I was taught' is natural.

hard.q: Change to passive: People believe that he is rich.
o: He is believing to be rich.
He is believed to be rich.
It is believe that he is rich.
hard.why: Impersonal passive with infinitive.

hard.q: Change to passive: She is going to write a report.
o: A report is going to be written by her.
A report is going to write by her.
A report was going to be written by her.
A report will write by her.
hard.why: Be going to: is going to be + participle.

hard.q: Which sentence cannot be turned into the passive?
hard.why: Sleep is intransitive; it takes no object.

hard.q: Change to passive: They are laughing at him.
o: He is laughed at by them.
He is being laughed at by them.
He was being laughed at by them.
He is laughing at by them.
hard.why: The preposition stays after the verb.

easy.q: Change to reported speech: He said, "I am happy."
o: He said that I am happy.
He said that he is happy.
He said that he was happy.
He told that he was happy.
easy.why: Present becomes past in reporting; I becomes he.

easy.q: Change to reported speech: Ravi said, "I will come."
o: Ravi said that he would come.
Ravi said that he will come.
Ravi said that I would come.
easy.why: Will becomes would.

easy.q: Change to reported speech: She said, "I like tea."
o: She said that she likes tea.
She said that she had liked tea.
She said that she liked tea.
easy.why: Simple present becomes simple past.

easy.q: Change 'here' in reported speech:
easy.why: Here becomes there.

easy.q: Change 'today' in reported speech after a past reporting verb:
easy.why: Today becomes that day.

easy.q: Change 'now' in reported speech:
easy.why: Now becomes then.

medium.q: Change to reported speech: He said, "I am reading a book."
o: He said that he was reading a book.
He said that he is reading a book.
He said that he read a book.
He said that I was reading a book.
medium.why: Present continuous becomes past continuous.

medium.q: Change to reported speech: He said to me, "Where do you live?"
o: He asked me where do I live.
He said me where I lived.
He asked me where I lived.
He asked me that where I lived.
medium.why: A question becomes a statement order with 'asked'.

medium.q: Change to reported speech: She said, "I have finished."
o: She said that she has finished.
She said that she had finished.
She said that I had finished.
medium.why: Present perfect becomes past perfect.

medium.q: Change to reported speech: The teacher said, "Sit down."
o: The teacher told them to sit down.
The teacher said them to sit down.
The teacher told that sit down.
medium.why: A command uses 'told ... to'.

medium.q: Change to reported speech: She said to him, "Do you know the way?"
o: She asked him do he know the way.
She said him if he knew the way.
She asked him that he knew the way.
She asked him if he knew the way.
medium.why: Yes/no question uses if or whether.

medium.q: Change to reported speech: He said to us, "Please help me."
o: He requested us to help him.
He said that please help him.
medium.why: Please shows a request.

hard.q: Change to reported speech: She said, "I saw him yesterday."
o: She said that she saw him yesterday.
She said that she has seen him the previous day.
She said that she had seen him the day before.
She said that I had seen him the day before.
hard.why: Yesterday becomes the day before; simple past becomes past perfect.

hard.q: Change to reported speech: Mother said, "The sun rises in the east."
o: Mother said that the sun rises in the east.
Mother said that the sun rose in the east not.
Mother said that the sun had risen.
Mother said the sun will rise.
hard.why: A universal truth keeps its tense.

hard.q: Change to reported speech: He said, "I will come tomorrow."
o: He said that he will come tomorrow.
He said that he came tomorrow.
He said that I would come the next day.
He said that he would come the next day.
hard.why: Tomorrow becomes the next day.

hard.q: Change to reported speech: He said, "What a lovely day!"
o: He asked what a lovely day.
He said what a lovely day.
He exclaimed that it was a lovely day.
He exclaimed what a lovely day was.
hard.why: An exclamation uses exclaimed (with joy).

hard.q: Change to reported speech: "Let us go to the park," said Rita.
o: Rita ordered that they go to the park.
Rita suggested that they go to the park.
Rita said that let us go to the park.
Rita asked what they go to the park.
hard.why: 'Let us' is a suggestion.

hard.q: Change to reported speech: The boy said, "Alas! I have failed."
o: The boy said alas that he failed.
The boy said with joy that he had failed.
The boy exclaimed that I had failed.
The boy exclaimed with sorrow that he had failed.
hard.why: Alas shows sorrow.

easy.q: Choose the relative pronoun: The man ___ lives next door is a doctor.
easy.why: Use who for a person as subject.

easy.q: Choose the conjunction: I will go ___ you come.
easy.why: If shows a condition.

easy.q: Choose the relative pronoun: This is the book ___ I read.
easy.why: That refers to a thing.

easy.q: Choose the conjunction: Wash your hands ___ you eat.
easy.why: Before shows time order.

easy.q: Choose the conjunction: He is poor ___ honest.
easy.why: But shows contrast.

easy.q: Choose the conjunction: Stay here ___ I return.
easy.why: Until marks the time limit.

medium.why: Whose shows possession.

medium.q: Choose the conjunction: ___ it rained, the match went on.
medium.why: Although shows contrast.

medium.q: Choose the word: This is the house ___ I was born.
medium.why: Where refers to a place.

medium.q: Which is the subordinate clause? 'He stayed home because he was ill.'
medium.why: It depends on the main clause.

medium.q: Choose the conjunction: Hurry up, ___ we will be late.
medium.why: Otherwise shows the other result.

medium.why: It can stand alone.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: If I were rich, I would travel the world.
If I was rich, I will travel the world.
If I am rich, I would travel the world.
If I were rich, I will travel the world.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: Not only he sang, but he also danced.
Not only did he sang, but also danced he.
Not only did he sing, but he also danced.
Not only he did sing, but danced.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: Unless you don't work hard, you will fail.
Unless you work hard, you will fail.
Unless you will work hard, you fail.
Unless you worked hard, you will fail.
hard.why: Unless already carries the negative idea.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: This is the boy whom I met yesterday.
This is the boy whom met me yesterday.
This is the boy which I met yesterday.
This is the boy whose I met yesterday.

hard.q: Which sentence has a noun clause?
o: The girl who sang is my sister.
I know that she is honest.
hard.why: 'that she is honest' is the object of know.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: Hardly she had left when the phone rang.
Hardly had she left when the phone rang.
Hardly had she left than the phone rang.
Hardly she left when the phone rang.
hard.why: 'Hardly had ... when'.

easy.q: Choose the word: The cat jumped ___ the table.

o: I like apples oranges, and bananas
I like, apples oranges and bananas.

easy.q: Which of these numbers cannot be a perfect square?
easy.why: A perfect square never ends in 2, 3, 7 or 8, and 2038 ends in 8.

easy.q: What is the cube root of 2744?
What is the value of 35 squared?
easy.why: 35^2 = 3 x 4 x 100 + 25 = 1225 (n5 squared ends in 25).

easy.q: What is the smallest number by which 12 must be multiplied to get a perfect square?
easy.why: 12 = 2 x 2 x 3, and the lone 3 needs a partner, so multiply by 3 to get 36.

easy.q: How many whole numbers lie strictly between 12^2 and 13^2?
easy.why: Between n^2 and (n+1)^2 there are 2n numbers, so 2 x 12 = 24.

easy.q: What is the last digit of 27 cubed?
easy.why: Only the last digit matters: 7 x 7 x 7 = 343 ends in 3.

medium.q: What is the sum of the first 15 odd numbers?
medium.why: The sum of the first n odd numbers is n^2, so 15^2 = 225.

medium.q: What is the cube root of 17576?
What is the smallest perfect square divisible by 6, 8 and 10?
medium.why: LCM = 120 = 2^3 x 3 x 5. Make every power even: 2^4 x 3^2 x 5^2 = 3600.

medium.q: What is the smallest number by which 252 must be multiplied to get a perfect square?
medium.why: 252 = 2^2 x 3^2 x 7. Only the 7 is unpaired.

medium.q: A square floor measures 30 tiles by 30 tiles. How many tiles are in the single outer border row?
medium.why: Border = 30^2 - 28^2 = 900 - 784 = 116. Counting 4 x 30 double-counts the 4 corners.

medium.q: What is 10 cubed minus 9 cubed?

hard.q: How many perfect squares lie between 200 and 1000?
hard.why: 15^2 = 225 is the first and 31^2 = 961 the last. Count = 31 - 15 + 1 = 17.

hard.q: A four-digit perfect cube ends in 8. What is its cube root?
hard.why: A cube ending in 8 has a root ending in 2. 12^3 = 1728 has 4 digits; 22^3 = 10648 has 5.

hard.q: 5 x 6 x 7 x 8 + 1 is the square of which number?
hard.why: 1680 + 1 = 1681 = 41 x 41. Product of 4 consecutive numbers plus 1 is a square.

hard.q: What is the smallest number greater than 1 that is both a perfect square and a perfect cube?
hard.why: It needs every prime power divisible by 6. The smallest is 2^6 = 64.

hard.q: How many two-digit numbers have a square ending in the digit 9?
hard.why: The number must end in 3 or 7: 9 tens digits x 2 endings = 18.
The sum of the first n cubes is (1+2+...+n)^2 = 55^2 = 3025.

easy.q: What is 2^5 x 2^3 written as a single power of 2?
easy.why: Same base: add the exponents, 5 + 3 = 8.

easy.q: What is the value of 10^-2?
easy.topic: Powers of ten and negative exponents

easy.q: How is 45,000 written in scientific notation?
easy.why: Move the decimal 4 places to get a number between 1 and 10: 4.5 x 10^4.

easy.q: What is the value of (-3)^4?
easy.why: An even power of a negative number is positive: 3 x 3 x 3 x 3 = 81.

easy.q: What is 5^6 divided by 5^2?
easy.why: Same base: subtract exponents, 6 - 2 = 4.

easy.q: What is 7^0 + 3^0?
easy.why: Any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1, so 1 + 1 = 2.
easy.topic: Powers of ten and negative exponents

medium.q: Simplify (3^2)^4.
medium.why: Power of a power: multiply exponents, 2 x 4 = 8.

medium.q: What is the value of (1/2)^-3?
medium.why: A negative exponent flips the fraction: (2/1)^3 = 8.
medium.topic: Powers of ten and negative exponents

medium.q: What is (6.2 x 10^5) x (3 x 10^2) in scientific notation?
What is 2^6 x 5^6?
medium.why: Same exponent: (2 x 5)^6 = 10^6.

medium.q: Simplify 10^-3 x 10^5 divided by 10^-1.
medium.topic: Powers of ten and negative exponents

medium.q: Light travels 3 x 10^5 km every second. How far does it travel in 5 x 10^2 seconds?

hard.q: Which is correct?
o: It cannot be decided without a calculator

hard.q: Earth's mass is about 6 x 10^24 kg and the Moon's about 7.35 x 10^22 kg. Earth is about how many times heavier?
Simplify (4^3 x 8^2) / 2^5.
A code has 3 letters (A to Z) followed by 2 digits (0 to 9). How many codes are possible?
3^n + 3^n + 3^n equals which of these?
hard.why: Three copies of 3^n is 3 x 3^n = 3^(n+1).
1/2 + 1/3 = 5/6, and the negative power flips it to 6/5.
hard.topic: Powers of ten and negative exponents

easy.q: What number does the Roman numeral XLIV stand for?
easy.why: XL = 40 and IV = 4, so 44.

easy.q: Which Roman numeral stands for 90?
easy.why: XC means 100 - 10 = 90. XL is 40 and CX is 110.

easy.q: Which feature makes the Hindu-Arabic system better than Roman numerals for big numbers?
o: Place value and a symbol for zero
It has no fixed order of digits
easy.why: The position of a digit gives its value, with 0 holding empty places.

What is the binary number 1011 in decimal?
What is decimal 9 in binary?

medium.q: In Egyptian numerals, the symbol for 10 appears 3 times and the symbol for 1 appears 4 times. What number is it?
medium.why: 3 tens + 4 ones = 34.

medium.q: What number is the Roman numeral MCMXCIV?
What is XXIX + XIV written in Roman numerals?
What is decimal 25 in binary?
What is the largest decimal value of a 3-digit base-8 number?
medium.why: The largest 3-digit base-8 number is 777 (base 8) = 7 × 64 + 7 × 8 + 7 = 511.

medium.q: In base 5, what is 4 x 3?
medium.why: 4 x 3 = 12 decimal = 2 x 5 + 2, written 22.

hard.q: In which base does the numeral 100 stand for decimal 49?
hard.why: In base b, 100 means b^2. So b^2 = 49 and b = 7.

What is the binary sum 1101 + 1011?
What is the binary product 101 x 11?
How many numbers can be written with exactly 5 binary digits (first digit 1)?
hard.why: They run from 10000 (16) to 11111 (31): 16 numbers.

easy.q: A quadrilateral has all four sides equal but its angles are not right angles. What is it?
easy.why: Equal sides without right angles describes a rhombus.

easy.q: What is the sum of the four angles of any quadrilateral?
easy.why: A diagonal splits it into 2 triangles of 180 degrees each.

easy.q: Which is always true for the diagonals of a rectangle?
o: They do not bisect each other
They are equal and bisect each other
easy.why: Rectangle diagonals are equal and bisect each other. Perpendicular diagonals belong to a rhombus.

easy.q: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 80, 100 and 90 degrees. What is the fourth?

easy.q: One angle of a parallelogram is 70 degrees. What is an adjacent angle?
easy.why: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram add to 180 degrees.

medium.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are in the ratio 1:2:3:4. What is the largest angle?

medium.q: Which statement is true?
medium.why: A square has four equal sides, so it is a rhombus, but not the other way round.

medium.q: A rectangle has perimeter 36 cm and its length is twice its breadth. What is the breadth?
medium.why: 2(2b + b) = 36 gives b = 6.

medium.q: In a parallelogram one angle is three times its adjacent angle. What is the smallest angle?

medium.q: A rhombus has side 8 cm and one angle of 60 degrees. What is its shorter diagonal?
medium.why: The shorter diagonal makes an equilateral triangle with two sides, so it is 8.

hard.q: What is the angle between the bisectors of two adjacent angles of a parallelogram?
hard.why: Half of 180 is 90, so in the triangle formed the third angle is 90.

hard.q: A rhombus has perimeter 52 cm and one diagonal of 24 cm. What is the other diagonal?
hard.why: Side 13, half-diagonal 12, so other half = square root of 169 - 144 = 5; the diagonal is 10.

hard.q: A parallelogram has equal diagonals. What must it be?
hard.why: A parallelogram with equal diagonals has right angles, so it is a rectangle.

hard.q: In rectangle ABCD the diagonals meet at O and angle AOB = 64 degrees. What is angle OAB?

hard.q: The angles of a quadrilateral are x, x+10, x+20 and x+30 degrees. What is the largest angle?

hard.q: What shape do you get by joining the midpoints of the sides of a rectangle that is not a square?

easy.q: The sum of three odd numbers is always...

easy.q: Which of these numbers is divisible by 9?

easy.q: What is the remainder when 47 is divided by 5?
Which of these numbers is divisible by 6?
easy.why: 4236 is even and its digit sum 15 is a multiple of 3.

easy.q: 23 leaves remainder 3 and 34 leaves remainder 4 when divided by 5. What remainder does 23 + 34 leave?

easy.q: What is the digital root of 4567?

medium.q: What is the smallest 3-digit number divisible by both 4 and 9?
medium.why: Multiples of 36: 36, 72, 108.

medium.q: What is the smallest number greater than 10 that leaves remainder 2 on division by both 3 and 4?
medium.why: Numbers are 12k + 2: 2, 14, 26...

medium.q: The sum of four consecutive whole numbers leaves what remainder when divided by 4?
medium.why: n + (n+1) + (n+2) + (n+3) = 4n + 6, which leaves remainder 2.

medium.q: For which digit A is 6A8 (a three-digit number 6 hundreds, A tens, 8 units) divisible by 9?
medium.why: 6 + A + 8 = 14 + A must be 18, so A = 4. Check: 648 = 9 x 72.

medium.q: n x n + n is always...
medium.why: n(n+1) is a product of consecutive numbers, so one factor is even.

medium.q: What remainder does 123 x 456 leave when divided by 5?
medium.why: 123 leaves 3 and 456 leaves 1, so the product leaves 3 x 1 = 3.

hard.q: The greatest number that always divides the product of any three consecutive whole numbers is...
hard.why: Among three consecutive numbers there is a multiple of 2 and of 3, but not always of 4 or 9.

hard.q: What is the smallest number greater than 1 that leaves remainder 1 on division by 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6?
What is the smallest number that leaves remainder 4 on division by 9 and remainder 5 on division by 7?
The difference between a two-digit number and its reversal is always divisible by...
hard.why: (10a + b) - (10b + a) = 9(a - b). For 63 - 36 = 27, not divisible by 18.

hard.q: What is the largest 4-digit number divisible by 18?
A two-digit number has digit sum 11. Reversing its digits increases it by 27. What is the number?
hard.why: 9(b - a) = 27 gives b - a = 3, and a + b = 11 gives a = 4, b = 7.

easy.q: What is 5(x + 4) after expansion?
easy.why: Multiply 5 with each term inside: 5x + 20.

easy.q: What is the expansion of (x + 3)^2?
easy.why: (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2, so the middle term is 6x.

easy.q: What is 12 x 99 worked out as 12 x 100 - 12?
Simplify 2x(x + 5) - 3x.
What is the expansion of (x - 4)^2?
What is 23 x 11?
easy.why: Put 2 + 3 = 5 between the digits 2 and 3: 253.

medium.q: What is 98 squared?
Step n of a tile pattern uses n^2 + 3n + 2 tiles. How many tiles are in step 5?
What is 103 x 97?
What is the expansion of (2x + 3y)^2?
medium.why: The middle term is 2 x 2x x 3y = 12xy; it cannot be dropped.

medium.q: What is 15 squared minus 7 squared?
If x + 1/x = 5, what is x^2 + 1/x^2?
medium.why: Square both sides: x^2 + 2 + 1/x^2 = 25, so the sum is 23.

hard.q: What is 998 squared?

hard.why: 36 - 1 = 35, which equals 4ab = 4 x 3.5 x 2.5.

hard.q: Which expression equals 2(a^2 + b^2)?
hard.why: The cross terms 2ab and -2ab cancel, leaving 2a^2 + 2b^2.

hard.q: If a + b = 10 and ab = 21, what is a^2 + b^2?

A rectangle has sides (3x + 2) and (2x - 1). What is its area?

easy.q: What is 24:36 in simplest form?
easy.why: Divide both by 12.

easy.q: Which ratio is equal to 3:5?
easy.why: Multiply both terms by 3.

easy.q: What is the ratio of 40 minutes to 2 hours?
easy.why: 2 hours = 120 minutes, and 40:120 = 1:3.
easy.topic: Dividing in a ratio and mixtures

easy.q: On a map 1 cm stands for 5 km. How far apart are two towns that are 7 cm apart on the map?

medium.q: Rs 1,200 is shared by A, B and C in the ratio 2:3:5. What does C get?
medium.why: One part = 1200 / 10 = 120; C gets 5 parts.

medium.q: A car travels 150 km in 3 hours. How far does it go in 5 hours at the same speed?

medium.why: Numbers are 48 and 36.

medium.q: Which is the better buy: 250 g for Rs 45 or 400 g for Rs 68?

hard.why: 15 parathas need 600 / 8 x 15 = 1125 g.

hard.q: A father and son have ages in the ratio 7:2, and the father is 35 years older. In how many years will the ratio be 2:1?

hard.q: A:B = 2:3 and B:C = 4:5. What is A:C?

medium.why: Pay Rs 120 for goods worth Rs 160, saving Rs 40, which is 25%.

easy.q: Which pair of quantities varies inversely?

Distance and time at constant speed

easy.q: Why should a student note down observations while doing an experiment?
o: So the teacher need not check it
So the results can be checked and compared later
easy.why: Written records let you check, compare and repeat the work; memory can fail.

easy.q: In a fair test, how many conditions should you change at one time?
easy.why: Changing one condition at a time shows which condition caused the result.

easy.q: Which of these is a question that science can test?
o: Which colour is the most beautiful?
Does a plant grow taller in sunlight than in shade?
Which song is nicest to hear?
easy.why: Science can answer questions that can be tested by observation or measurement; opinions of beauty cannot be measured.

easy.q: Sunita compares how fast sugar dissolves in 100 mL of cold water and 100 mL of hot water, using one spoon of the same sugar. What is the variable she changes?
easy.why: Only the water temperature differs; everything else is kept the same.

easy.q: Which of the following is an observation and not an opinion?
o: The paper turned brown after 10 minutes in the sun
The sun is unfair to paper
easy.why: An observation is what you can see, measure or record, without adding personal judgement.

easy.q: Which statement best describes how science grows?
o: Once written in a book, ideas never change
New evidence can improve or change earlier explanations
Only one scientist decides what is true
easy.why: Science is self-correcting: new observations can refine or replace old ideas.

medium.q: Rahul tests which paper plane flies farthest. He uses A4 paper for plane P and a thicker chart paper for plane Q, and throws P gently and Q hard. Which statement is correct?
o: The test is fair because two planes are used
The test is fair because he threw both
The test is unfair only because the planes are of the same shape
The test is unfair because paper type and throwing force both differ
medium.why: Two conditions changed together, so a difference in distance cannot be linked to one cause.

medium.q: Arrange these steps of an investigation in the correct order: (1) draw a conclusion, (2) ask a question, (3) do the experiment and record results, (4) make a hypothesis.
medium.why: We ask a question, propose a hypothesis, test and record, and then conclude.

medium.q: Priya wants to know if the amount of oil affects how much a puri puffs. Which of these should she keep the same?
o: Dough, thickness, flame and frying time
medium.why: All factors except the one being tested must be controlled.

medium.q: Four students recorded the temperature of cooling tea every 2 minutes. Which record is best?
o: A single reading at the end
A table showing time and temperature with units
A drawing of the cup only
medium.why: Repeated, measured values with units make a clear and checkable record.

medium.q: After testing, Ravi's result does not match his hypothesis. What is the best thing for him to do?
o: Accept the result and revise the hypothesis
Change the result to match his hypothesis
medium.why: A good scientist follows the evidence even when it disagrees with the hypothesis.

medium.q: Meera tests how the height of a ramp changes the distance a toy car rolls. Which two quantities should she measure?
o: Colour of car and ramp height
Mass of ramp and time of day
Distance rolled and the colour of floor
medium.why: She changes ramp height and measures the distance the car rolls in response.

hard.q: Ravi tests whether salt dissolves faster in hot water. He puts 1 spoon of fine salt in 100 mL hot water and 1 spoon of coarse salt in 100 mL cold water. Why can he not conclude anything about temperature?
o: Both temperature and grain size changed
The volume of water was different
Salt does not dissolve in cold water
hard.why: With two variables changed, a faster result could be due to either temperature or grain size.

hard.q: A student claims that plants kept in a cupboard grow slower than those in the window, so sunlight makes them grow faster. The cupboard is also cooler. What is the weakness in her claim?
o: Plants never grow in a cupboard
Temperature also differs, so sunlight alone is not shown to be the cause
hard.why: A second difference (temperature) could also explain the result, so she cannot be sure about sunlight.

hard.q: Over 5 days, a bean seedling grows 2 cm, 4 cm, 6 cm, 8 cm and 40 cm. What is the most sensible action?
o: Write that the seedling grew by magic
Recheck the 40 cm reading, since it breaks the pattern
Average only the last two readings
hard.why: A reading far from the pattern is possibly a recording or measuring error and should be rechecked.

hard.q: Two groups did the same experiment on boiling time of water at the same flame. Group A got 6 min, Group B got 9 min. Which is the most likely reason?
o: Water boils differently for each group
Group B used a bad clock only
The volume of water or the flame size was not the same
hard.why: Unless amount of water and heat are controlled, results differ even for the same procedure.

hard.q: To find out whether the number of turns of a coil changes the number of paper clips an electromagnet lifts, Gita uses 20 turns with a thin wire and a 1.5 V cell, and 40 turns with a thick wire and a 3 V cell. What should she do?
o: Use the same wire and the same cell, changing only the turns
Keep the coils different so results are more interesting
hard.why: Only the number of turns should change; wire and cell must stay the same.

hard.q: A hypothesis says: "Heavier stones fall faster." An experiment shows a 100 g stone and a 500 g stone reaching the ground together when dropped from the same height. Which conclusion is best?
o: The hypothesis is not supported by this evidence
The experiment is invalid because the stones are heavy
hard.why: Experiments can show a hypothesis is not supported; here the weights did not change the fall time.

easy.q: Which instrument do we need to see most microorganisms?
easy.why: Microorganisms are too small for the naked eye, so a microscope is used.

easy.q: Which microorganism makes dough rise when added to flour for bhature?
easy.why: Yeast ferments sugar and releases carbon dioxide, which makes the dough rise.

easy.q: Which of these is a fungus?
easy.why: Moulds and yeast are fungi; Lactobacillus and Rhizobium are bacteria; Amoeba is a protozoan.

easy.q: Rhizobium bacteria live in the root nodules of which crop?
easy.why: Rhizobium fixes atmospheric nitrogen in the roots of legumes such as chana, moong and peas.

easy.q: Which gas turns lime water milky?
easy.why: Carbon dioxide reacts with lime water to form a white, milky solid.

easy.q: Which place helps mould grow fastest on bread?
easy.why: Microbes grow best with warmth and moisture.

medium.q: Why do we keep cooked dal in a refrigerator?
o: Low temperature slows down growth of microbes
medium.why: Low temperature slows microbial growth and delays spoilage.

medium.q: A balloon is tied over a bottle with yeast, sugar and warm water. After a day the balloon is inflated. The gas inside is mainly
medium.why: Yeast ferments sugar and gives off carbon dioxide.

medium.q: A farmer grows moong and does not add nitrogen fertiliser, but a neighbour growing maize does. Why?
o: Moong does not need any nutrients
Maize bacteria fix nitrogen in leaves
Moong has Rhizobium in its root nodules that fixes nitrogen
Moong takes nitrogen only from rain
medium.why: Legume roots host nitrogen-fixing bacteria; maize cannot use air nitrogen.

medium.q: Which pair is correctly matched?
medium.why: Yeast is a fungus; Amoeba is a protozoan; Lactobacillus and Rhizobium are bacteria.

medium.q: Bread slice X is kept in a closed box in the kitchen; slice Y is kept in a fridge. After 3 days only X has mould. Which factor best explains it?
o: Closed box lets in more light
medium.why: Mould spores grow quickly at room temperature but slowly in the cold.

medium.q: A virus differs from bacteria in that it
o: Multiplies only inside a living host cell
medium.why: Viruses cannot reproduce on their own; they need a host cell.

hard.q: A compost heap is turned and sprinkled with water weekly, yet decomposes slowly in winter. The most likely reason is
hard.why: Microbial activity falls in the cold, even when air and moisture are available.

hard.q: Lime water is placed in a test tube connected to a flask of sugar and yeast. After 4 hours it turns milky. A student repeats the setup without yeast. What will she find and why?
o: It turns milkier because sugar gives carbon dioxide
It becomes blue as sugar rises
It stays clear because no carbon dioxide is made without yeast
It turns milky because air alone makes CO2
hard.why: Without yeast there is no fermentation, so no carbon dioxide reaches the lime water.

hard.q: To test whether moisture is needed for mould growth, which set-up is best?
o: A damp slice in a fridge and a dry slice in sunlight
Two damp slices at different temperatures
Two identical slices, one damp and one dry, kept at the same temperature
hard.why: Only moisture should differ; temperature and bread type stay equal.

hard.q: Which statement about microorganisms is correct?
o: Some are useful and some cause disease
All can be seen without a microscope
hard.why: Microbes include helpful ones (curd, bread, antibiotics) and harmful pathogens.

hard.q: Yeast is added to two flasks of sugar solution. Flask P is kept at 35 degrees C and flask Q at 5 degrees C. After 3 hours, which observation is most likely?
o: More bubbles in Q because cold makes yeast faster
More bubbles in P because yeast is more active when warm
No bubbles in P because heat kills yeast at 35 degrees C
hard.why: Yeast ferments faster at a warm, moderate temperature; at 5 degrees C it is slow.

hard.q: Fresh milk boiled and sealed in a clean airtight bottle stays unspoilt for many days, while open milk spoils in a day. Which reasoning is best?
o: Boiling kills most microbes and sealing keeps new ones out
hard.why: Heat kills microbes and the closed bottle prevents new ones from entering.

easy.q: Which of these diseases spreads from one person to another?
easy.why: Cholera is communicable; the others do not spread person to person.

easy.q: The best way to prevent many stomach infections is to
o: Wash hands with soap before eating
easy.why: Handwashing removes germs before they enter the mouth.

easy.q: Which pair contains only non-communicable diseases?
easy.why: Diabetes and asthma do not spread from person to person.

easy.q: Malaria is spread by
easy.why: Anopheles females carry the malaria parasite.

easy.q: Antibiotics work against
easy.why: Antibiotics are medicines that kill bacteria and do not act on viruses.

easy.q: Why should stagnant water be removed near homes?
easy.why: Mosquitoes lay eggs in standing water.

medium.q: Which pair of diseases mainly spreads through contaminated water?
medium.why: Cholera and typhoid spread through food or water carrying germs from excreta.

medium.q: Rohit has a viral cold and asks the chemist for antibiotics. A good reply is that
o: Antibiotics do not work against viruses and may cause resistance
Antibiotics work faster on viruses than bacteria
medium.why: Antibiotics act on bacteria; unnecessary use helps resistant bacteria develop.

medium.q: A family returns from a trip to a mosquito-prone area and a child develops fever with chills. What is the most sensible step?
o: Hide from people for a year
Visit a doctor for tests and treatment
medium.why: Fever after exposure could be malaria; diagnosis and proper treatment matter.

medium.q: A classmate says diabetes spreads by sharing food. Which reply is correct?
o: Diabetes is non-communicable, so it does not spread that way
medium.why: Diabetes is related to the body's sugar control, not germs.

medium.q: Why is it important to finish a full antibiotic course prescribed by a doctor?
o: Stopping early can leave some bacteria that may become resistant
medium.why: Surviving bacteria after incomplete treatment may develop resistance.

medium.q: Which set of habits best reduces dengue spread?
o: Empty coolers weekly, use nets and repellents
medium.why: Dengue mosquitoes breed in clean standing water, so removing it plus personal protection helps.

hard.q: In a town, dengue cases were 20 in April, 35 in June, 150 in August, 210 in September and 60 in November. Which explanation best fits the pattern?
o: Dengue is caused by cold winds
Monsoon rain increases standing water and mosquito breeding
hard.why: Rain collects in containers, so mosquitoes breed and cases rise after the monsoon.

hard.q: A person gets chicken pox once but gets cold many times. Why can colds recur?
o: Many different cold viruses exist and they change
hard.why: Immune memory works against a specific germ; many varieties cause common colds.

hard.q: Which advice does NOT help prevent a non-communicable disease?
o: Take antibiotics regularly to stay healthy
hard.why: Antibiotics act on bacteria and do not prevent lifestyle diseases.

hard.q: A village well gets sewage seepage and many people suffer vomiting and diarrhoea. Which step is best for the community?
o: Chlorinate the water and stop sewage entering the well
hard.why: Disinfecting water and sealing the contamination source breaks the disease cycle.

hard.q: Two children are given the same vaccine. Child P is later exposed to the germ and recovers in 2 days; Child Q, unvaccinated, is ill for 10 days. The best explanation is
o: P has more antibiotics in blood
Q has no white blood cells at all
The memory cells in P responded faster
hard.why: A vaccinated child has memory cells that respond quickly.

hard.q: Which pair of examples is correctly classed?
hard.why: Measles spreads by a virus; asthma is not infectious.

easy.q: A current-carrying wire placed near a compass needle will
easy.why: Electric current produces a magnetic field that deflects a compass.

easy.q: Which appliance works mainly on the heating effect of current?
easy.why: An electric iron has a heating element; a bell works on the magnetic effect.

easy.q: A cell converts
easy.why: A cell stores chemicals that react to produce an electric current.

easy.q: Heating wires in toasters are made of nichrome because it
o: Has high resistance and does not oxidise easily when hot
easy.why: Nichrome gets very hot and resists burning in air.

easy.q: An electromagnet is made by passing current through a coil wound on
easy.why: Iron strengthens the magnetic field of the coil and loses it when current stops.

easy.q: Which will heat up faster for the same current and material?
o: A thick nichrome wire of equal length
easy.why: A thinner wire has higher resistance, so more heat is produced.

medium.q: A coil with 20 turns picks up 6 pins. Which change would most likely make it pick up more?
o: Increase the turns and use the same cell
medium.why: More turns and a stronger current increase the magnetism.

medium.q: In a lemon cell, a copper strip and a zinc strip are pushed into a lemon. The lemon juice acts as
medium.why: The juice carries ions between the metals, completing the circuit inside the cell.

medium.q: If the battery connections of a wire near a compass are reversed, the needle deflection will
medium.why: Reversing current reverses the direction of the magnetic field.

medium.q: Which change makes a compass placed near a straight current-carrying wire deflect more?
o: Using a larger current in the wire
medium.why: A stronger current produces a stronger magnetic field; reversing it only reverses the direction of deflection.

medium.q: Four cups hold: tap water with salt, pure water, sugar solution and plain oil. A cell is dipped into each in turn. Which makes a bulb glow?
medium.why: Salt gives ions that conduct; sugar solution, pure water and oil do not conduct well.

medium.q: Which of the following does an electric bell use?
medium.why: An electromagnet pulls the hammer repeatedly to ring the bell.

hard.q: Meena's electromagnet lifted 10 pins when connected to a fresh cell. After an hour, it lifts 2 pins though the wire is still warm. The best explanation is
o: The cell is running down so current is weaker
hard.why: A weaker current gives a weaker magnetic effect while some heating remains.

hard.q: A circuit is made with a cell, an LED and two metal strips dipped in a glass. The LED glows when the glass has lemon juice but not with sugar solution. A student says sugar cannot be an electrolyte because it is sweet. What is the correct reasoning?
o: Sugar dissolves as molecules, not ions, so it does not conduct
Juice is a conductor only in dark
hard.why: Conduction in solutions needs charged ions; sugar does not form ions.

hard.q: Two nichrome wires, X and Y, are of the same thickness. X is 20 cm long and Y is 40 cm. Connected one by one to the same cell, which statement is most likely?
o: X has more resistance than Y
Y has more resistance and shows less current
Both have exactly the same resistance
hard.why: A longer wire has greater resistance, so less current flows.

hard.q: A coil without an iron core deflects a compass by 10 degrees. When an iron nail is placed inside, the deflection
hard.why: Soft iron inside the coil strengthens the magnetic field.

hard.q: A bulb is in series with a thin nichrome wire and a cell, and glows dimly. The nichrome wire is replaced by a copper wire of the same length and thickness. The bulb will now glow
o: More dimly, since copper has higher resistance
Equally, since both wires carry current
Not at all, since copper is an insulator
More brightly, since copper has much lower resistance
hard.why: Less resistance in the circuit lets a larger current flow through the bulb.

hard.q: The heating effect makes a fuse useful. Which fuse wire is suited to a 5 A circuit?
o: A wire that melts at a little above 5 A
A wire that melts at 0.1 A
A wire that melts at 100 A
hard.why: A fuse should melt only when the current becomes dangerously more than the rated value.

easy.q: Friction acts
o: In the same direction as motion
Opposite to the direction of motion
easy.why: Friction opposes relative motion between surfaces.

easy.q: Mass of an object is measured in
easy.why: Mass is measured in kg; weight (a force) is measured in newtons.

easy.q: Which surface produces the most friction?
easy.why: Rougher surfaces have more interlocking and so more friction.

easy.q: A plastic comb rubbed on dry hair attracts small paper bits because
easy.why: Rubbing charges the comb, which attracts light paper pieces.

easy.q: An iron nail sinks in water because its
o: Weight is greater than the upward buoyant force
easy.why: If weight is more than buoyancy, the object sinks.

easy.q: The force with which Earth pulls an object is called
easy.why: Weight is the gravitational pull on an object.

medium.q: Why do we sprinkle sand on a wet slippery road?
medium.why: Sand makes the surface rough and increases grip.

medium.q: An astronaut weighs 600 N on Earth. On the Moon, where gravity is about 1/6 of Earth's, her weight will be about
medium.why: 600 / 6 = 100 N. Mass stays the same; weight changes.

medium.q: Which of these does NOT need contact between objects?
o: A magnet attracting an iron nail
medium.why: A magnetic force can act across a gap.

medium.q: A wooden block of 100 cm cubic volume floats in water but a steel ball of the same weight sinks. Why?
o: Steel ball has smaller volume so less water is displaced
medium.why: Buoyancy depends on displaced water volume; the larger block displaces more.

medium.q: A box needs 50 N to start moving on a floor and 40 N to keep it moving. Which statement is correct?
o: Friction is zero when the box moves
Starting friction is greater than moving friction
medium.why: It takes more force to start motion than to continue it.

medium.q: Two balloons rubbed on hair are brought close. They
medium.why: Like charges repel; both balloons carry the same kind of charge.

hard.q: A 12 kg bag on the Moon (gravity about 1/6 of Earth's, taking Earth's g as 10 N/kg) has weight
hard.why: On the Moon g = 10/6; weight = 12 x 10/6 = 20 N. The mass is still 12 kg.

hard.q: A student pushes a heavy almirah and it does not move even though she pushes with 200 N. What can be said about the friction force?
o: It is also 200 N, balancing her push
It is more than 200 N and acts forward
hard.why: For no motion, forces balance: static friction equals the push.

hard.q: Two blocks of equal volume are held fully under water. Block P has mass 200 g and block Q has mass 400 g. Which statement about the buoyant force is correct?
o: It is greater on Q because Q is heavier
It is greater on P because P is lighter
It is the same on both because they displace equal volumes
hard.why: Buoyant force equals the weight of water displaced, which depends only on the volume under water.

hard.q: A satellite moves around Earth in a circle at constant speed. Which statement is correct?
o: No force acts since its speed is constant
The force acts only when it speeds up
Force acts only along its direction of motion
A force (gravity) acts on it because its direction keeps changing
hard.why: Force is needed to change direction as well as speed; gravity pulls the satellite toward Earth.

hard.q: A spring balance shows 49 N for an object on Earth taking g = 9.8 m/s squared. Its mass is
hard.why: Mass = weight / g = 49 / 9.8 = 5 kg.

hard.q: A girl pulls a sled with 30 N to the right and her brother pulls with 45 N to the left. Which is the net force?
hard.why: Opposite forces subtract: 45 - 30 = 15 N toward the larger force.

easy.q: Pressure is defined as
easy.why: Pressure = force / area.

easy.q: A force of 200 N acts on an area of 4 square metres. The pressure is
easy.why: 200 / 4 = 50 N per square metre = 50 Pa.

easy.q: Air moves from
o: Cold place to cold place only
easy.why: Wind is air flowing from a region of higher pressure to lower pressure.

easy.q: Why does a sharp knife cut better than a blunt one?
o: Larger edge area gives larger pressure
It has less friction in air
Smaller edge area gives larger pressure
easy.why: For the same force, a smaller area gives more pressure.

easy.q: The calm, clear centre of a cyclone is called the
easy.why: The eye has light winds and clear sky.

easy.q: During a thunderstorm, which place is safest?
o: Inside a closed building or car
On a hilltop holding a metal rod
easy.why: Closed buildings and vehicles protect from lightning; tall objects attract it.

medium.q: A 60 kg boy has two feet each 150 cm squared on the floor. Taking g = 10 N/kg, his pressure on the floor is
medium.why: Force 600 N; area 300 cm squared = 0.03 m squared; 600/0.03 = 20,000 Pa.

medium.q: Water is poured to the same height in three vessels with bases of different areas. The pressure at the bottom of each is
medium.why: Liquid pressure depends on height (depth), not on base area.

medium.q: On a hot afternoon at the seashore, the land warms more than the sea. The wind blows
medium.why: Air above hot land rises, lowering pressure, so cooler sea air moves in.

medium.q: A brick (20 cm x 10 cm x 5 cm, weight 20 N) is placed on its largest face. Its pressure on the table is
medium.why: Largest face 20 x 10 = 200 cm squared = 0.02 m squared; 20/0.02 = 1,000 Pa.

medium.q: Why are dams made thicker at the bottom?
o: Pressure of water increases with depth
Water is lighter at the bottom
Less water is at the bottom
medium.why: Greater pressure at depth needs a stronger and thicker wall.

medium.q: A hole is made at different heights in a tall bottle. Water squirts farthest from
medium.why: Pressure is greatest at the lowest point, so water leaves with the greatest speed.

hard.q: A tractor weighing 40,000 N has 4 wheels, each in contact with 0.2 square metres of ground. A trolley weighing 20,000 N has 4 wheels each touching 0.05 square metres. The pressure of the trolley on the ground is how many times that of the tractor?
hard.why: Tractor: 40,000 / 0.8 = 50,000 Pa. Trolley: 20,000 / 0.2 = 100,000 Pa. The ratio is 2.

hard.q: The depth of water in a tank is doubled. The pressure at the bottom becomes
hard.why: Pressure is proportional to depth.

hard.q: Which sequence describes how a thunderstorm cloud causes lightning?
o: Charges separate in the cloud and a discharge jumps between cloud and ground
Clouds bump to make sparks of fire
hard.why: Ice and water droplets in the cloud separate positive and negative charges, causing discharge.

hard.q: A 50 N force is applied by a thumb on a drawing pin head of area 1 cm squared. The sharp tip has area 0.01 cm squared. The pressure on the board from the tip compared with the thumb is
hard.why: Force is transmitted equally; pressure is inversely proportional to area, so 1/0.01 = 100 times.

hard.q: Why does the wind speed rise near the centre of a cyclone (eye wall)?
o: The eye wall has high pressure
Pressure drops steeply toward the centre so air rushes in
hard.why: A large pressure difference over a short distance causes strong winds.

hard.q: A bottle with holes 10 cm and 20 cm below the water surface is filled. Which statement is correct when the water level is kept the same?
o: No water comes out of the lower hole
Water from the lower hole comes out faster and reaches farther
hard.why: Pressure grows with depth, so the lower hole squirts faster.

easy.q: Matter is made up of
easy.why: All matter is made of tiny particles.

easy.q: In which state of matter are particles packed very closely in fixed positions?
easy.why: Solid particles vibrate around fixed places.

easy.q: The smell of food cooking in the kitchen reaches you in the next room by
easy.why: Particles of food vapour spread through air by random motion.

easy.q: Ice turning into water is called
easy.why: Solid to liquid is melting.

easy.q: Which state of matter has no fixed shape and no fixed volume?
easy.why: Gases fill the container they are in.

easy.q: Water vapour on a cold glass turning into drops is
easy.why: Gas to liquid is condensation.

medium.q: During boiling of water at 100 degrees C, the particles
o: Gain enough energy to separate and become vapour
medium.why: Heat energy overcomes the attraction between the particles.

medium.q: Why does perfume spread faster in a room than a drop of honey spreads in a cup of water?
o: Gas particles are far apart and move freely
medium.why: Particles in gases move quickly with weak attraction.

medium.q: Camphor kept in an open dish slowly disappears. This is called
medium.why: A solid changes directly to gas without becoming liquid.

medium.q: Sugar placed in tea dissolves faster when the tea is hot because
o: Particles move faster at higher temperature
medium.why: Faster particle motion mixes the particles more rapidly.

medium.q: When ice is heated from -5 degrees C, which sequence is correct?
medium.why: Ice warms to 0 degrees C, melts, water warms to 100 degrees C, then boils.

medium.q: A drop of dye is placed in a glass of water without stirring. After some time the colour is uniform. This shows
o: Particles of liquid are in constant motion
Dye weighs the same as water
medium.why: Random motion of particles leads to mixing.

hard.q: Which statement explains why a solid keeps its shape but a liquid does not?
o: Solid particles do not move at all
Solid particles are held by stronger attractions in fixed positions
hard.why: Stronger attraction in solids locks particles in place, while liquid particles slide.

hard.q: A beaker of water at 25 degrees C is placed on a heater with a thermometer. At 100 degrees C, the temperature stops rising even though heating continues. Why?
o: The heat is used to separate particles into vapour
hard.why: During boiling the energy changes the state, not the temperature.

hard.q: Two identical glasses hold water at 20 degrees C and 60 degrees C. A drop of ink is added to each. Which statement is correct?
o: Colour spreads faster in the hot water
Colour spreads faster in the cold water
It does not spread in the hot water
hard.why: Particles in hot water move faster.

hard.q: Fine sand pours like a liquid, yet is a solid. Which explanation is correct?
o: Sand grains melt as they pour
Each grain is a solid and grains slide over each other
Sand turns to liquid when poured
hard.why: Each grain is solid; the pile behaves like a liquid because the grains move over one another.

hard.q: A student heats naphthalene balls in a covered dish and sees white crystals on the cold lid. Which describes what happened?
o: Sublimation of the solid followed by deposition on the lid
hard.why: Solid goes to gas on heating, then gas goes to solid on the cold lid.

hard.q: 50 mL of alcohol is mixed with 50 mL of water and the total volume is a little less than 100 mL. The best explanation is
o: Alcohol particles fill spaces between water particles
hard.why: Particles of one liquid fit into gaps among the particles of the other.

easy.q: Which of these is an element?
easy.why: Iron has only one kind of atom; the others are compounds.

easy.q: Which of these is a mixture?
easy.why: Air is made of nitrogen, oxygen and other gases that are only mixed.

easy.q: A compound is formed when
o: Elements combine chemically in a fixed ratio
easy.why: Compounds have fixed composition and new properties.

easy.q: Common salt (sodium chloride) is
easy.why: It is made of sodium and chlorine joined chemically.

easy.q: When a magnesium ribbon burns, the white powder formed is
easy.why: Magnesium combines with oxygen to form magnesium oxide.

easy.q: Which method separates iron filings from sand?
easy.why: Iron is attracted by a magnet; sand is not.

medium.q: Iron and sulfur are mixed and a magnet is passed over them. The iron sticks to it. After the mixture is heated strongly, the product is not attracted by the magnet. This shows
medium.why: Heating made iron sulfide with properties unlike the iron or sulfur.

medium.q: Which list has only compounds?
medium.why: Each of these is made of two or more elements chemically combined.

medium.q: In a mixture of sand and sugar, which statement is true?
medium.why: Components of a mixture are not chemically changed.

medium.q: Zinc is added to dilute hydrochloric acid and bubbles appear. The gas is most likely
medium.why: Metal plus acid gives a salt and hydrogen gas.

medium.q: Water differs from hydrogen and oxygen in properties because
o: Hydrogen and oxygen are mixed in it
A compound has properties different from its elements
medium.why: Chemical combination creates a new substance.

medium.q: Which pair shows a chemical change?
o: Melting of ice and boiling water
Burning of wood and rusting of iron
medium.why: Burning and rusting produce new substances.

hard.q: A substance X, when heated, gives two different gases and a solid, each of which cannot be split further. What is X?
hard.why: Splitting into simpler substances shows it is a compound.

hard.q: Iron filings and sulfur are mixed (sample P). Part of it is heated strongly to give a dark solid (sample Q). Which observation would show that Q is a compound and not just a mixture?
o: A magnet does not pull out iron from Q
Q can be crushed into powder
Q weighs about the same as P
hard.why: Iron in a mixture is pulled out by a magnet. If it is not, it has chemically joined with sulfur.

hard.q: Which statement is correct about air and carbon dioxide?
o: Air is a mixture, carbon dioxide is a compound
Air is a compound, carbon dioxide is an element
hard.why: Air has gases mixed without a fixed ratio; CO2 is carbon and oxygen chemically combined.

hard.q: When 24 g of magnesium burns completely it forms 40 g of magnesium oxide. The mass of oxygen that combined is
hard.why: Oxygen mass = 40 - 24 = 16 g.

hard.q: Which pair is correctly matched?
hard.why: Sodium is an element; sodium chloride is a compound.

hard.q: A metal piece X placed in dilute acid gives no bubbles but placed in oxygen on heating gains mass. Which conclusion is best?
o: X reacts with oxygen to form a compound heavier than the metal
X does not react with anything
hard.why: The gain in mass comes from oxygen combining with the metal.

easy.q: Density is
easy.why: Density = mass / volume.

easy.q: A solution that cannot dissolve any more solute at that temperature is
easy.why: Saturated means the maximum amount is already dissolved.

easy.q: A block has mass 80 g and volume 20 cubic cm. Its density is
An object floats in water if its density is
easy.why: Objects less dense than the liquid float.

easy.q: In a solution of sugar in water, sugar is the
easy.why: The dissolved substance is the solute.

easy.q: Which will sink in water?
easy.why: Iron is denser than water.

medium.q: A cube of side 2 cm has a mass of 40 g. Its density is
medium.why: Volume = 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 cubic cm; 40/8 = 5.

medium.q: At room temperature, 36 g of salt dissolves in 100 g of water to make a saturated solution. If 50 g is added to 100 g of water, how much remains undissolved?
medium.why: 50 - 36 = 14 g stays undissolved.

medium.q: A measuring cylinder shows 40 mL. After dropping in a stone it shows 52 mL. The volume of the stone is
medium.why: 52 - 40 = 12 mL = 12 cubic cm.

medium.q: What would increase the amount of sugar that dissolves in 100 mL of water?
medium.why: Solubility of most solids increases with temperature.

medium.q: A tank is 50 cm long, 20 cm wide and 10 cm deep. How many litres of water can it hold?
A saturated sugar solution made hot is cooled slowly. What happens?
o: Some sugar may settle as crystals
medium.why: Solubility decreases when cooled, so extra solute crystallises.

hard.q: A solid has mass 270 g and a volume of 100 cubic cm. The liquid density is 1.2 g per cubic cm. Will the solid float?
o: No, solid density 2.7 is more than 1.2
No, mass is the same as volume
hard.why: 2.7 g per cubic cm is greater than 1.2, so it sinks.

hard.q: A measuring cylinder holds 50 mL of water. A metal ball of mass 156 g is lowered in and the level reads 70 mL. The density of the metal is
hard.why: Volume = 20 cubic cm; 156/20 = 7.8.

hard.q: At 30 degrees C, 100 g of water dissolves at most 40 g of a salt. Ananya adds 70 g of the salt to 200 g of water at 30 degrees C and stirs well. How much salt stays undissolved?
hard.why: 200 g of water can dissolve 80 g, which is more than 70 g, so everything dissolves.

hard.q: Salt water has more density than fresh water. A boat sailing from a river into the sea will
hard.why: A denser liquid gives more buoyant force for a smaller submerged volume.

hard.q: A mixture of two liquids has a mass of 55 g in a volume of 50 cubic cm. If it were purely water (1 g per cubic cm), mass would be 50 g. What can be concluded?
o: The mixture is denser than water
The mixture is less dense than water
hard.why: 55/50 = 1.1, denser than water.

hard.q: A hollow steel ball weighs 400 g and has outer volume 600 cubic cm. Steel is 8 g per cubic cm. Why does it float in water?
o: Its average density (about 0.67 g per cubic cm) is less than 1
hard.why: Average density = 400/600 = 0.67, so it floats.

easy.q: A ray of light falls on a mirror along the normal. The angle of reflection is
easy.why: The angle of incidence is 0, so the angle of reflection is also 0.

easy.q: The angle of incidence is 30 degrees. The angle of reflection is
easy.why: By the law of reflection, the two angles are equal.

easy.q: The mirror used in a vehicle to see traffic behind is
easy.why: A convex mirror gives a wide field of view.

easy.q: A magnifying glass is a
easy.why: A convex lens enlarges objects held close to it.

easy.q: Bending of light as it passes from air into water is called
easy.why: Light changes direction at the boundary of two transparent media.

easy.q: Which surface gives a clear image like a mirror?
easy.why: Regular reflection from a smooth surface forms a clear image.

medium.q: A ray strikes a plane mirror making an angle of 25 degrees with the mirror surface. The angle of reflection is
medium.why: Angle of incidence = 90 - 25 = 65 degrees, so reflection = 65.

medium.q: A girl stands 2 m from a plane mirror. Her image appears to be at a distance from her of
medium.why: The image is as far behind the mirror as she is in front, so 2 + 2 = 4 m.

medium.q: A convex mirror always forms an image that is
medium.why: For a convex mirror, images are virtual, upright and diminished.

medium.q: A coin in an empty bowl is just out of sight. Water is poured in and the coin comes into view. This is due to
medium.why: Light from the coin bends at the water surface and reaches the eyes.

medium.q: The word AMBULANCE is written laterally inverted in front of a vehicle so that
o: It reads correctly in the rear view mirror
medium.why: A plane mirror reverses left and right.

medium.q: Which mirror can form a real image on a screen?
medium.why: A concave mirror can form real images when the object is far enough.

hard.q: A ray of light hits a mirror at 20 degrees from the normal. The angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray is
hard.why: The two angles to the normal are 20 each, so total 40.

hard.q: Two plane mirrors are placed at right angles. A ray hits the first at 30 degrees to its surface. After the second reflection it is
o: At 60 degrees to the incident ray
Parallel to the incident ray but opposite in direction
hard.why: For perpendicular mirrors, the final ray is antiparallel to the original ray.

hard.q: A person walks towards a large plane mirror at 1.5 m per second. Her image approaches her at a relative speed of
hard.why: The image also approaches the mirror at 1.5 m per second, so relative speed is 3 m per second.

hard.q: A fish in a pond appears to be
o: Closer to the surface than it really is
Larger but at the true depth
hard.why: Refraction bends rays away from the normal, so the apparent depth is less.

hard.q: Which statement about a convex lens in sunlight is correct?
o: It spreads sunlight so paper cools
It can focus light to a bright point and set paper alight
hard.why: A convex lens converges parallel rays to a focus.

hard.q: The angle between the incident and reflected rays is 80 degrees. The mirror is rotated so that the angle of incidence increases by 15 degrees. The new angle between incident and reflected rays is
hard.why: Original angle of incidence is 40 degrees; new is 55; total = 2 x 55 = 110.

easy.q: The Moon takes about how many days to go from one full Moon to the next?
easy.why: A lunar month is about 29.5 days.

easy.q: The Moon shines because it
easy.why: The Moon is not luminous.

easy.q: A year is based on the
o: Revolution of Earth around the Sun
easy.why: One revolution of Earth around the Sun is a year.

easy.q: The day on which we cannot see the Moon is called
easy.why: On the New Moon the lit side faces away from Earth.

easy.q: A day is based on the
o: Rotation of Earth on its axis
easy.why: One rotation of Earth is a day.

easy.q: A leap year has
easy.why: February has 29 days in a leap year.

medium.q: At sunset, a full Moon is seen
medium.why: A full Moon is opposite the Sun, so rises as the Sun sets.

medium.q: A lunar month is about 29.5 days. How many days are in 12 lunar months?
At which phase is the Moon seen overhead at midnight?
medium.why: The full Moon is opposite the Sun and is highest around midnight.

medium.q: Which natural cycle is used for a month in a lunar calendar?
medium.why: A lunar month is from one New Moon to the next.

medium.q: Which of these is true for a waning Moon?
o: The lit part is getting smaller each night
medium.why: Waning means decreasing.

medium.q: The Moon rises about 50 minutes later each day. If it rises at 6:00 pm on a full Moon day, about when will it rise two days later?
medium.why: 2 x 50 = 100 minutes after 6:00 pm gives 7:40 pm.

hard.q: A lunar year is about 354 days and a solar year about 365 days. After 3 years, how many days behind is the lunar calendar?
A student sees a crescent Moon in the west just after sunset. Which is correct?
hard.why: A waxing crescent is seen in the evening sky near the west.

hard.q: Which year is a leap year?
hard.why: Years divisible by 4 are leap years, except century years not divisible by 400. 2028 is.

hard.q: If the Moon rises at about 6 pm, which phase is it?
hard.why: The full Moon rises when the Sun sets.

hard.q: A geostationary satellite stays above the same point on Earth because
o: It is held by a string
It takes 24 hours for one orbit, equal to the rotation period of Earth
hard.why: Its orbital period matches the rotation of Earth.

hard.q: Under the Gregorian calendar, 1900 was not a leap year even though it is divisible by 4. Why?
o: Century years must be divisible by 400
hard.why: Century years are leap only if divisible by 400; 1900 is not, 2000 is.

easy.q: Plants are called producers because they
o: Make their own food by photosynthesis
easy.why: Producers make food using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide.

easy.q: Which of these is a non-living (abiotic) part of a pond ecosystem?
easy.why: Sunlight, water and temperature are abiotic.

easy.q: In the food chain grass -> grasshopper -> frog -> snake, the frog is a
easy.why: The frog eats grasshoppers and is eaten by the snake.

easy.q: Which organisms break down dead plants and animals?
easy.why: Decomposers return nutrients to the soil.

easy.q: A food chain always begins with a
easy.why: Producers capture the energy from sunlight.

easy.q: A herbivore eats
easy.why: Herbivores are plant eaters.

medium.q: In a pond, small fish eat algae and big fish eat small fish. If the big fish are removed, small fish will
medium.why: Fewer predators let prey populations grow.

medium.q: A dead leaf on the forest floor gets covered by fungus and later turns into humus. This shows
o: Decomposers recycling nutrients to the soil
medium.why: Fungus breaks down the leaf and returns minerals.

medium.q: Which is a correct set of an ecosystem's components?
o: Producers, consumers, decomposers and abiotic factors
medium.why: An ecosystem includes living things and their physical surroundings.

medium.q: Sprays of strong pesticides in a garden reduce butterflies because
o: They kill insects including useful ones and reduce their food plants
medium.why: Pesticides harm non-target insects and disturb the food web.

medium.q: A food web differs from a food chain because it
medium.why: Many organisms eat or are eaten by more than one species.

medium.q: Which activity best returns nutrients to farm soil?
medium.why: Compost provides humus and minerals.

hard.q: In a field, grass is eaten by rabbits and grasshoppers; frogs eat grasshoppers; snakes eat frogs and rabbits. If frogs disappear, which is the likely effect on the snake population?
o: Snakes grow in numbers with nothing changed
Snakes eat more rabbits so rabbit numbers fall while grasshoppers rise
hard.why: Snakes depend more on rabbits and grasshoppers lose a predator.

hard.q: If a forest had no fungi or bacteria, which would occur first?
o: Dead leaves and wood would pile up and nutrients would be locked
hard.why: Without decomposers, nutrient cycling stops.

hard.q: A village builds a dam and floods a wetland. Which long-term effect on the food web is most likely?
o: Loss of habitat reduces birds and fish that depend on it
hard.why: Destroying a habitat removes species and breaks food links.

hard.q: Which statement about energy in a food chain is correct?
o: Energy decreases at each step as it moves from one level to the next
Energy is the same at every level
hard.why: Much energy is lost as heat, so fewer organisms can be supported at higher levels.

hard.q: A disease sharply reduces the number of hares in a forest where foxes feed on hares and mice. Which is the most likely result in the short term?
o: Foxes eat more mice and mice numbers fall
hard.why: Predators switch to other prey, reducing it.

hard.q: Two compost pits are filled with equal wet kitchen waste. Pit A is covered and turned weekly; Pit B is sealed with no air. After a month, A has turned dark and crumbly, while B smells bad. Why?
o: Decomposers in A had air and worked well while B lacked oxygen
hard.why: Aerobic decomposition with air is quick and odourless; the sealed pit rots differently.

easy.q: Which gas in Earth's air do living things need for breathing?
easy.why: Most organisms use oxygen for respiration.

easy.q: Which is NOT needed for life as we know it?
easy.why: Life needs water, air and moderate temperature.

easy.q: Which gas increases global warming when released in large amounts?
easy.why: CO2 traps heat in the atmosphere.

easy.q: Which plant grows from a part of its stem?
easy.why: Sugarcane stem cuttings grow into new plants.

easy.q: Which layer of air protects us from harmful ultraviolet rays?
easy.why: The ozone layer absorbs UV from the Sun.

easy.q: In humans, fertilisation takes place
easy.why: Human fertilisation is internal.

medium.q: The Moon has no atmosphere. As a result, daytime temperatures are
o: Very high and nights very cold
medium.why: No air to trap or spread heat.

medium.q: Which pair gives examples of vegetative propagation?
medium.why: New plants grow from non-seed parts.

medium.q: A village sees hotter summers and sudden heavy rain. One adaptation that helps farmers is
o: Growing drought-resistant crops and storing rainwater
medium.why: Adaptation reduces the harm of changes.

medium.q: A planet has half the size of Earth but the same density. Compared with Earth it will probably
o: Hold less atmosphere due to weaker gravity
medium.why: Smaller mass means weaker gravity.

medium.q: Why do children differ from their parents?
o: Genetic material from both parents is combined
medium.why: Sexual reproduction mixes the traits of both parents.

medium.q: Cutting forests changes the local climate because trees
o: Release water vapour and give shade
medium.why: Fewer trees mean less transpiration and more heat.

hard.q: Which is NOT evidence that Earth is warming?
hard.why: Hot deserts have always been hot; the others are measurements of change.

hard.q: If Earth lost its magnetic field, which problem would be most serious?
o: Charged particles from the Sun would reach the surface
hard.why: The magnetic field deflects solar wind and cosmic radiation.

hard.q: Which pair correctly distinguishes weather and climate?
o: Weather is for one year; climate for one hour
Weather is the day-to-day state of the atmosphere; climate is the average over many years
hard.why: Climate is the long-term pattern of weather.

hard.q: Without an atmosphere, Earth's surface would most likely
o: Have extreme temperature swings and no liquid water
hard.why: No air means no heat retention or water cycle.

hard.q: Which statement about asexual reproduction is correct?
o: The offspring is genetically almost identical to the parent
hard.why: One parent produces similar offspring.

hard.q: A tree is planted for every 100 kg of CO2 a family emits. Which statement is most accurate?
o: Trees remove all pollution at once
Trees absorb CO2 and can partly offset emissions over time
hard.why: Photosynthesis takes in CO2 but slowly.
