easy.q: She ___ to school by bus every day.
easy.why: A daily habit uses the present simple, and a singular subject takes goes.

easy.q: They ___ football in the park every Sunday.
easy.why: A habit with a plural subject takes the base form of the verb.

easy.q: Passengers ___ wear a seat belt; it is the law.
easy.why: Must shows a rule or obligation.

easy.q: Look! The baby ___ at the picture.
easy.why: Look! shows the action is happening now, so we use the present continuous.

easy.q: We ___ our cousins in Pune last summer.
easy.why: Last summer is a finished past time, so the simple past is used.

easy.q: You ___ cross the road when the signal is red. It is dangerous.
easy.why: Must not shows a strong prohibition.

medium.q: By the time Dad came home, we ___ dinner.
medium.why: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect.

medium.q: I ___ in this school since 2022.
medium.why: Since with a starting point takes the present perfect.

medium.q: By the time we reached the station, the train ___.
medium.why: The train left before we arrived, so the earlier action takes the past perfect.

medium.q: This time next week, we ___ on a beach in Goa.
medium.why: This time next week points to an action in progress in the future, so we use the future continuous.

medium.q: Ravi ___ his homework since four o'clock and is still at it.
medium.why: Since with an action still going on needs the present perfect continuous.

medium.q: She ___ be at home; her car is outside.
medium.why: Must shows a strong guess based on evidence.

hard.q: If it ___ tomorrow, we will cancel the picnic.
hard.why: In a real future condition the if-clause takes the simple present.

hard.q: If I ___ you, I would apologise to her.
hard.why: An imaginary present situation takes were in the if-clause.

hard.q: If he had left earlier, he ___ the train.
hard.why: A past unreal condition takes would have plus the past participle.

hard.q: I would have called you if I ___ your number.
hard.why: A third conditional (unreal past) pairs would have with the past perfect in the if clause.

hard.q: She said she ___ the project by Friday.
hard.why: After a past verb, will changes to would.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: By next March, Meera has taught here for ten years.
By next March, Meera will have taught here for ten years.
By next March, Meera will teach here for ten years.
By next March, Meera would taught here for ten years.
hard.why: By a future time with a completed span takes the future perfect.

easy.q: The teacher, along with her students, ___ going to the museum.
easy.why: Along with does not make the subject plural. The subject is the teacher.

easy.q: Each of the boys ___ a prize.
easy.why: Each is singular, so it takes has.

easy.q: She drank ___ water and felt better.
easy.why: Water is uncountable, so a little is used; a few and many are for countable nouns.

easy.q: Mathematics ___ my favourite subject.
easy.why: Names of subjects ending in s are singular.

easy.q: There ___ two apples left in the basket.
easy.why: The real subject apples is plural, so use are.

easy.q: He is ___ honest boy.
easy.why: Honest starts with a vowel sound, so we use an.

medium.q: Either Priya or her brothers ___ coming.
medium.why: With either-or the verb agrees with the nearer subject, brothers.

medium.q: Each of the players ___ given a medal.
medium.why: Each is singular.

medium.q: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ aware of the change.
medium.why: With neither...nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject, students, which is plural.

medium.q: Ten kilometres ___ a long distance to walk.
medium.why: A distance seen as one amount takes a singular verb.

medium.q: He has ___ friends in the new city, so he often feels lonely.
medium.why: Few means hardly any and carries a negative sense; a few would mean some.

medium.q: The news of the floods ___ shocking.
medium.why: News is an uncountable noun that takes a singular verb.

hard.q: The principal as well as the teachers ___ present at the function.
hard.why: As well as does not change the subject. The subject is the principal.

hard.q: Two-thirds of the pizza ___ eaten, and two-thirds of the guests ___ gone.
hard.why: With a fraction the verb agrees with the noun after of: pizza is singular and guests is plural.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: Fifty rupees are too much for this pen.
Fifty rupee is too much for this pen.
Fifty rupees is too much for this pen.
Fifty rupees were too much for this pen now.
hard.why: A sum of money is treated as one amount.

hard.q: The number of stray dogs in our colony ___ risen, while a number of residents ___ complained.
hard.why: The number of takes a singular verb; a number of means several and takes a plural verb.

hard.q: Neither the manager nor the clerks ___ able to find the file.
hard.why: With neither-nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject, clerks.

hard.q: Bread and butter ___ my usual breakfast.
hard.why: Bread and butter is thought of as one dish, so the verb is singular.

easy.q: He said, "I am tired." He said that he ___ tired.
easy.why: The present tense moves back to the past in reported speech.

easy.q: Tom said, "I can drive." Tom said that he ___ drive.
easy.why: Can changes to could in reported speech.

easy.q: She said to me, "Close the door." She ___ me to close the door.
easy.why: A command is reported with told or asked plus to.

easy.q: He said to me, "Open the window." He ___ me to open the window.
easy.why: A command is reported with told plus the person plus to.

easy.q: He said, "I live here." He said that he lived ___.
easy.why: Here changes to there in reported speech.

easy.q: Father said, "I am going to Delhi today." Father said that he was going to Delhi ___.
easy.why: Today becomes that day.

medium.q: "Where do you live?" asked Sam. Sam asked me where ___.
medium.why: A reported question uses statement order and shifts to the past.

medium.q: Mohit said to Sunil, "Will you help me?" Mohit asked Sunil ___.
medium.why: A yes-no question uses if with statement order and will changes to would.

medium.q: Rohan said, "I will meet you tomorrow." Rohan said that he would meet me ___.
medium.why: Tomorrow becomes the next day in reported speech.

medium.q: The mother said to her son, "Please sit down." The mother ___ her son to sit down.
medium.why: Please marks a request, so requested is the best reporting verb.

medium.q: The teacher asked, "Have you finished the exercise?" The teacher asked whether I ___ the exercise.
medium.why: A yes-no question is reported with whether or if, and the present perfect becomes the past perfect.

medium.q: She said, "What a beautiful garden!" She ___ that it was a beautiful garden.
medium.why: An exclamation is reported with exclaimed.

hard.q: Rani said, "I saw him yesterday." Rani said that she had seen him ___.
hard.why: Yesterday becomes the day before and saw becomes had seen.

hard.q: He said to me, "Why did you not come to the party last night?" He asked me why I ___ to the party the night before.
hard.why: Past simple changes to past perfect and last night becomes the night before.

hard.q: The teacher said, "The earth moves around the sun." The teacher said that the earth ___ around the sun.
hard.why: A universal truth stays in the simple present.

hard.q: She said, "I have been waiting here since morning." She said that she ___ there since morning.
hard.why: The present perfect continuous changes to the past perfect continuous.

hard.q: Neha said to Kavya, "May God bless you!" Neha ___ that God might bless her.
hard.why: A blessing or wish is reported with prayed or wished, and may changes to might.

hard.q: "Let's go for a walk," said Kabir. Which is the correct report?
o: Kabir said to go for a walk.
Kabir suggested going for a walk.
Kabir ordered us going for a walk.
Kabir asked that let us go for a walk.
hard.why: Let's is a suggestion, reported with suggested.

easy.q: Which is the passive of "She sings a song."?
o: A song was sung by her.
A song is sung by her.
A song is singing by her.
easy.why: The simple present passive is is or are plus the past participle.

easy.q: Passive of "The cook prepares dinner."
o: Dinner was prepared by the cook.
Dinner is prepared by the cook.
Dinner is preparing by the cook.
easy.why: Present simple becomes is or are plus the past participle.

easy.q: The letter ___ yesterday.
easy.why: Yesterday needs the past passive, was written.

easy.q: The window ___ by the boy yesterday.
easy.why: Yesterday needs the simple past passive, was plus the past participle.

easy.q: In "The boy who won the race is my cousin", the clause "who won the race" is a(n)
easy.why: It describes the noun boy, so it is an adjective clause.

easy.q: In "I will go home when the bell rings", the clause "when the bell rings" is an
easy.why: It tells when the action happens, so it is an adverb clause.

medium.q: Which is the passive of "The students have finished the project."?
o: The project has been finished by the students.
The project is finished by the students.
The project had been finished by the students.
The project was finished by the students.
medium.why: The present perfect passive is has or have been plus the past participle.

medium.q: Which is the passive of "Who broke the glass?"?
o: By whom the glass was broken?
By whom was the glass broken?
By whom is the glass broken?
medium.why: The simple past question becomes By whom was ... broken?

medium.q: Passive of "They are repairing the road."
o: The road is being repaired by them.
The road is repaired by them.
The road was being repaired by them.
The road has been repaired by them.
medium.why: Present continuous becomes is or are being plus the past participle.

medium.q: In "I know that he is honest", the clause "that he is honest" is a
medium.why: It is the object of know, so it works as a noun.

medium.q: In "I know where he lives", the clause "where he lives" is a
medium.why: It is the object of the verb know, so it is a noun clause.

medium.q: In "She was late because the bus broke down", the clause "because the bus broke down" is an
medium.why: Because gives the reason, so it is an adverb clause of reason.

hard.q: Which is the passive of "You must not touch the wire."?
o: The wire must be not touched.
The wire must not be touched.
The wire is not must touched.
hard.why: A modal passive is modal plus be plus the past participle, and not follows the modal.

hard.q: In "What he said was true", the clause "What he said" is
o: a noun clause used as the subject
hard.why: It works as the subject of was, so it is a noun clause.

hard.q: Which is the passive of "Someone has stolen my bicycle."?
hard.why: The present perfect passive is has been plus the past participle, and the doer is dropped.

hard.q: Which sentence has an adverb clause of reason?
o: The match that was cancelled was ours.
I wonder whether the match will be held.
Because it rained, the match was cancelled.
He told me that the match was cancelled.
hard.why: Because it rained tells why the match was cancelled.

hard.q: Which sentence has an adjective clause?
o: I stayed home because it rained.
The man whose car was stolen called the police.
He asked if I was ready.
hard.why: Whose car was stolen describes the man.

hard.q: Passive of "Who wrote this poem?"
o: By whom is this poem written?
Who has this poem been written?
By whom this poem was written?
By whom was this poem written?
hard.why: The simple past becomes was plus the past participle, and who becomes by whom.

easy.q: She is afraid ___ dogs.
easy.why: Afraid is followed by of.

easy.q: "Break a leg!" said before a performance means
easy.why: It is a theatre idiom wishing good luck.

easy.q: He is fond ___ mangoes.
easy.why: Fond is followed by of.

easy.q: He apologised ___ being late.
easy.why: We apologise for something.

easy.q: "A huge crowd gathered at the gate." Huge means
easy.why: Huge means very big.

easy.q: Which word means the same as "rapid"?
easy.why: Rapid means quick or fast.

medium.q: In "Each of the boys have a book", which word needs correcting?
medium.why: Each is singular, so the verb should be has.

medium.q: The meeting was called off ___ heavy rain.
medium.why: Because of is followed by a noun phrase.

medium.q: In "Neither of the two answers are correct", the word that needs correcting is
medium.why: Neither takes a singular verb, so are should be is.

medium.q: "Losing the match was a blessing in disguise" means
o: something good that seemed bad at first
medium.why: A blessing in disguise is a good thing that first looks bad.

medium.q: "The shopkeeper's lenient attitude let students return goods without fuss." Lenient means
medium.why: Lenient describes someone who is gentle and not strict with rules.

medium.q: She is allergic ___ peanuts.
medium.why: Allergic is followed by to.

hard.q: Which is the corrected version of "She don't like to eats spicy food."?
o: She don't like to eat spicy food.
She doesn't like to eat spicy food.
She doesn't like to eats spicy food.
She not like eating spicy food.
hard.why: Doesn't goes with she, and the verb after to stays in the base form.

hard.q: He is senior ___ me by two years.
hard.why: Senior, junior and prefer take to.

hard.q: "After months of delay, she decided to bite the bullet and confront the problem." Bite the bullet means
hard.why: It means to face something unpleasant with courage.

hard.q: ___ she was ill, she attended the rehearsal.
hard.why: The two parts contrast, so a concession word is needed.

hard.q: She worked hard; ___, she failed.
hard.why: However shows contrast.

hard.q: "He let the cat out of the bag at the party." This means he
hard.why: To let the cat out of the bag is to give away a secret by accident.

easy.q:
Passage: Rani's grandmother kept a small tin box under her bed. Every evening, after the lamps were lit, she took out one old photograph and told a story about it. The children never tired of the stories, though they had heard most of them twice. When she fell ill, they quietly began telling the stories to her instead.

Where did the grandmother keep the tin box?
easy.why: The first sentence says it was under her bed.

easy.q:
Passage: The mobile library van reached the village of Dhanora every Thursday. Children ran after it, shouting the name of the driver, Raju bhaiya. Last month, the panchayat decided to stop the service because few adults borrowed books. But when Raju bhaiya showed that fifty-two children had borrowed books that month, the panchayat reconsidered. The van still comes on Thursdays, and now it carries picture books in Marathi as well.

How often does the van visit Dhanora?
easy.why: The passage says the van reached the village every Thursday.

easy.q:
Passage: Rani's grandmother kept a small tin box under her bed. Every evening, after the lamps were lit, she took out one old photograph and told a story about it. The children never tired of the stories, though they had heard most of them twice. When she fell ill, they quietly began telling the stories to her instead.

What did the grandmother do every evening?
o: Lit all the lamps in the village
Told a story about an old photograph
easy.why: After the lamps were lit she took out one photograph and told a story.

easy.q:
Passage: The mobile library van reached the village of Dhanora every Thursday. Children ran after it, shouting the name of the driver, Raju bhaiya. Last month, the panchayat decided to stop the service because few adults borrowed books. But when Raju bhaiya showed that fifty-two children had borrowed books that month, the panchayat reconsidered. The van still comes on Thursdays, and now it carries picture books in Marathi as well.

Why did the panchayat first decide to stop the service?
easy.why: The panchayat acted because few adults borrowed books.

easy.q:
Passage: Honeybees communicate through dance. When a worker bee finds flowers rich in nectar, she returns to the hive and performs a "waggle dance". The angle of her dance shows the direction of the flowers relative to the sun, and the length of the waggle shows how far they are. Other workers watch closely and then fly out to the spot. Scientists once believed only humans could pass on such detailed directions.

What is the bee's dance called?
easy.why: The passage names it the waggle dance.

easy.q:
Passage: Honeybees communicate through dance. When a worker bee finds flowers rich in nectar, she returns to the hive and performs a "waggle dance". The angle of her dance shows the direction of the flowers relative to the sun, and the length of the waggle shows how far they are. Other workers watch closely and then fly out to the spot. Scientists once believed only humans could pass on such detailed directions.

According to the passage, what does the length of the waggle show?
o: Which direction the sun is in
easy.why: The length of the waggle shows the distance.

medium.q:
Passage: The mobile library van reached the village of Dhanora every Thursday. Children ran after it, shouting the name of the driver, Raju bhaiya. Last month, the panchayat decided to stop the service because few adults borrowed books. But when Raju bhaiya showed that fifty-two children had borrowed books that month, the panchayat reconsidered. The van still comes on Thursdays, and now it carries picture books in Marathi as well.

What made the panchayat change its mind?
o: The number of children borrowing books
medium.why: Raju bhaiya showed that fifty-two children had borrowed books.

medium.q:
Passage: The mobile library van reached the village of Dhanora every Thursday. Children ran after it, shouting the name of the driver, Raju bhaiya. Last month, the panchayat decided to stop the service because few adults borrowed books. But when Raju bhaiya showed that fifty-two children had borrowed books that month, the panchayat reconsidered. The van still comes on Thursdays, and now it carries picture books in Marathi as well.

The word "reconsidered" means
medium.why: Re- means again, so reconsidered means thought about it again.

medium.q:
Passage: Rani's grandmother kept a small tin box under her bed. Every evening, after the lamps were lit, she took out one old photograph and told a story about it. The children never tired of the stories, though they had heard most of them twice. When she fell ill, they quietly began telling the stories to her instead.

Why did the children tell the stories to her when she was ill?
o: To repay her care and comfort her
Because they had forgotten the photographs
Because they were bored of listening
Because she asked them to leave
medium.why: The children gave back the comfort she had always given them.

medium.q:
Passage: Honeybees communicate through dance. When a worker bee finds flowers rich in nectar, she returns to the hive and performs a "waggle dance". The angle of her dance shows the direction of the flowers relative to the sun, and the length of the waggle shows how far they are. Other workers watch closely and then fly out to the spot. Scientists once believed only humans could pass on such detailed directions.

What does the angle of the dance tell other bees?
o: The direction of the flowers compared with the sun
medium.why: The passage says the angle shows direction relative to the sun.

medium.q:
Passage: The village of Kharsi had one well, and it was running dry. Instead of blaming the weather, Meena called a meeting. "Every roof here can catch rain," she said. Within a year forty rooftops fed pipes into pits near the well, and by the next monsoon the well was full again.

What does the passage suggest about Meena?
o: She is afraid of the weather
She is practical and takes the lead
medium.why: She skipped blaming and acted with a workable plan.

medium.q:
Passage: Honeybees communicate through dance. When a worker bee finds flowers rich in nectar, she returns to the hive and performs a "waggle dance". The angle of her dance shows the direction of the flowers relative to the sun, and the length of the waggle shows how far they are. Other workers watch closely and then fly out to the spot. Scientists once believed only humans could pass on such detailed directions.

In the passage, "communicate" means
medium.why: The bees pass on information about the flowers.

The van still comes on Thursdays, and now it carries picture books in Marathi as well.

Which can be inferred from the passage?
o: The panchayat first judged the service only by adult borrowers
Raju bhaiya wants to leave the village
Children are not interested in books
All the books are in English
hard.why: The decision to stop was based on adults alone, and changed when children's use was shown.

hard.q:
Passage: The mobile library van reached the village of Dhanora every Thursday. Children ran after it, shouting the name of the driver, Raju bhaiya. Last month, the panchayat decided to stop the service because few adults borrowed books. But when Raju bhaiya showed that fifty-two children had borrowed books that month, the panchayat reconsidered. The van still comes on Thursdays, and now it carries picture books in Marathi as well.

The last sentence suggests that the service
o: is changing to suit the village
hard.why: Adding picture books in Marathi shows it adapts to local needs.

The angle of her dance shows the direction of the flowers relative to the sun, and the length of the waggle shows how far they are. Other workers watch closely and then fly out to the spot. Scientists once believed only humans could pass on such detailed directions.

The words "once believed" suggest that scientists now
o: know animals can also give detailed directions
hard.why: Once believed points to an old idea that has since changed.

hard.q:
Passage: The village of Kharsi had one well, and it was running dry. Instead of blaming the weather, Meena called a meeting. "Every roof here can catch rain," she said. Within a year forty rooftops fed pipes into pits near the well, and by the next monsoon the well was full again.

Which statement is NOT supported by the passage?
hard.why: The passage says the village had one well.

hard.q:
Passage: Honeybees communicate through dance. When a worker bee finds flowers rich in nectar, she returns to the hive and performs a "waggle dance". The angle of her dance shows the direction of the flowers relative to the sun, and the length of the waggle shows how far they are. Other workers watch closely and then fly out to the spot. Scientists once believed only humans could pass on such detailed directions.

Which is the best title for the passage?
hard.why: The passage is about how a dance tells direction and distance.

hard.q:
Passage: Arjun looked at the clock, then at the empty chair beside him, and finally put the second cup of tea back on the tray.

What can be inferred?
o: He was expecting someone who did not come.
hard.why: The second cup and empty chair show he waited for a guest who did not arrive.

easy.q: A diary entry is written in the ___ person.
easy.why: A diary records your own thoughts, so it uses I.

easy.q: A diary entry usually begins with
easy.why: A diary entry starts with the date and day.

easy.q: A formal letter that begins "Dear Sir" should end with
easy.why: Dear Sir pairs with Yours faithfully.

easy.q: Which salutation suits a formal letter to the Principal?
easy.why: A formal letter uses a respectful salutation.

easy.q: Which complimentary close suits a letter to a close friend?
easy.why: An informal letter can close warmly with Yours lovingly.

easy.q: Which close goes with the salutation "Dear Sir/Madam"?
easy.why: Yours faithfully pairs with Dear Sir or Madam.

medium.q: A byline in an article is
o: the writer's name below the title
medium.why: A byline names the writer.

medium.q: Which part belongs in a formal letter but not in a diary entry?
medium.why: A formal letter has a subject line. A diary does not.

medium.q: Which is NOT part of the format of a formal letter?
o: A pet name for the receiver
medium.why: Formal letters stay impersonal and have no pet names.

medium.q: A paragraph on "Our School Library" should
o: have a salutation and a subject line
stick to one idea with supporting details
medium.why: A paragraph develops one main idea.

medium.q: A paragraph on "The Importance of Sleep" should begin with
o: a topic sentence stating the main idea
medium.why: A good paragraph opens with a sentence that states its central idea.

medium.q: Which tone best suits a letter to the Editor?
medium.why: A letter to the Editor is formal and respectful.

hard.q: Which opening suits a diary entry after losing a match?
o: Dear Sir, With due respect, I wish to state that we lost.
Title: Losing a Match. By: Rohan.
Once upon a time a team lost a match.
Friday, 12 March, 9 p.m. Dear Diary, I still feel the sting of today's loss.
hard.why: A diary has a date and day, speaks to the diary and shares feelings.

hard.q: Which is the best ending for an article on saving water?
o: A clear call to action for readers
hard.why: A good article ends with a conclusion or a call to action.

hard.q: Which sentence suits a leave letter to a Principal?
o: Hey, give me a day off, na?
I request you to grant me leave for two days as I am unwell.
I am not coming, deal with it.
Leave is my right so sign it.
hard.why: A formal request is polite, clear and gives the reason.

hard.q: Which opening best suits a 150-word school magazine article on a plastic ban?
o: A catchy title, a byline and a strong first line
hard.why: Articles carry a title and byline and open with a hook.

hard.q: What should the middle of a short story do?
o: Give the address of the writer
Build the problem and the action
hard.why: The middle develops the conflict that leads to the ending.

hard.q: In a letter to the Editor, the subject line comes
o: after the salutation and before the body
hard.why: The usual order is address, date, receiver, salutation, subject, body, closing.

easy.q: In which quadrant does the point (−4, 7) lie?
easy.why: x is negative and y is positive, which is the top-left quadrant, Quadrant II.

easy.q: A point lies on the x-axis, 5 units to the left of the origin. What are its coordinates?
easy.why: On the x-axis y = 0. Left of the origin means x is negative, so (−5, 0).

easy.q: How far is the point (−6, 9) from the y-axis?
easy.why: Distance from the y-axis is the size of the x-coordinate, so |−6| = 6. Distance is never negative.

easy.q: Which of these points lies on the y-axis?
easy.why: Every point on the y-axis has x = 0, so only (0, −3) fits.

easy.q: Find the midpoint of the segment joining A(2, 8) and B(10, 4).
easy.why: Average the x-values and the y-values: (2+10)/2 = 6 and (8+4)/2 = 6.

easy.q: What is the distance of the point (6, 8) from the origin?
easy.why: Distance = √(6² + 8²) = √100 = 10. Adding 6 and 8 gives 14, which is a common mistake.

medium.q: A point has x-coordinate −7. In which of these places can it NOT lie?
medium.why: A negative x puts the point left of the y-axis, so it can never be in Quadrant I.

medium.q: In triangle PQR, P = (2, 1), Q = (6, 1) and R = (6, 4). How long is side PR?
medium.why: PQ = 4 and QR = 3 meet at a right angle at Q, so PR = √(16+9) = 5.

medium.q: Find the distance between A(−3, 2) and B(5, −4).
medium.why: Differences are 8 and 6, so distance = √(64+36) = 10. Adding 8 + 6 = 14 is wrong.

medium.q: The midpoint of AB is M(4, −1). If A is (2, 5), what are the coordinates of B?
medium.why: Midpoint rule: 4 = (2+x)/2 gives x = 6; −1 = (5+y)/2 gives y = −7.

medium.q: Which set of three points lies on one straight line?
medium.why: For (1,1),(3,4),(5,7) both steps rise 3 for a run of 2, so the slope is the same. The other sets change slope.

medium.q: a is negative and b is positive. In which quadrant does the point (−a, −b) lie?
medium.why: −a is positive and −b is negative, so the point has x > 0 and y < 0, which is Quadrant IV.

hard.q: For what value of k are the points (1, 2), (3, 5) and (7, k) on one straight line?
OPQR is a square with O at the origin and P(3, 1) as the next vertex. What is its area?
hard.why: Side OP = √(9+1) = √10, so area = (√10)² = 10. Using 3 + 1 as the side gives 16.

hard.q: A circle with centre at the origin passes through (5, 12). Which point lies strictly inside it?
hard.why: Radius² = 25 + 144 = 169. For (9,9): 162 < 169, so inside. (12,5) lies on it; (13,1) gives 170 and (10,10) gives 200, both outside.

hard.q: Triangle ABC has A(−2, 1), B(1, 5) and C(4, 1). Which statement is true?
o: It is isosceles, with AB = BC
hard.why: AB² = 9+16 = 25 and BC² = 9+16 = 25, but AC² = 36. Two sides are equal, and 25 + 25 ≠ 36, so it is not right-angled.

hard.q: A circle has its centre at the origin and radius 10. Which pair lists all its points with x-coordinate −6?
hard.why: x² + y² = 100 gives y² = 64, so y = 8 or −8. Both signs count.

hard.q: Find the point P on the x-axis that is equally far from A(2, 3) and B(6, 5).
hard.why: Let P = (x, 0): (x−2)² + 9 = (x−6)² + 25 gives 8x = 48, x = 6. Then PA = PB = 5.

easy.q: What is the degree of the polynomial 5x³ − 2x + 9?
easy.why: Degree is the highest power of the variable. Here the highest power of x is 3.

easy.q: What is the coefficient of x in 7x³ − 4x² + 6x − 1?
easy.why: The coefficient of x is the number multiplying x¹, which is 6.

easy.q: Which of these is a linear polynomial?
easy.why: A linear polynomial has degree 1. 3x + 2 has highest power 1; 7 is a constant (degree 0).

easy.q: Find the value of 4x − 7 when x = −2.
Find the value of t² − 3t + 2 when t = 3.
Rohan has ₹50 and saves ₹30 every week. How much will he have after n weeks?
easy.why: He starts with 50 and adds 30 for each of the n weeks, so 50 + 30n.

medium.q: Which line is the steepest?
medium.why: Steepness depends on the size of a, ignoring sign. |−5| is the largest.

medium.q: A father is 4 times as old as his son. In 6 years their ages will add up to 62. How old is the father now?
medium.why: Son s, father 4s: (s+6) + (4s+6) = 62 gives s = 10, so father = 40.

medium.q: A 180 m rope is cut into two pieces. The longer is 5 times the shorter. How long is the longer piece?
medium.why: Shorter s: s + 5s = 180 gives s = 30, so the longer is 150 m.

medium.q: An auto fare is y = 15x + 40 rupees for x km. How many km can you travel for ₹280?
Where does the graph of y = −3x + 6 cut the axes?
medium.why: Put x = 0: y = 6. Put y = 0: −3x + 6 = 0 gives x = 2.

medium.q: A line y = ax + b passes through (0, 4) and (2, 10). What is its equation?
medium.why: At x = 0, y = b = 4. Then 2a + 4 = 10 gives a = 3.

hard.q: A phone bought at ₹48,000 loses ₹4,000 in value every year. After how many years is it worth ₹12,000?
Meera has ₹800 and adds ₹250 each month. After how many months will she first have more than ₹5,000?
hard.why: 800 + 250n > 5000 gives n > 16.8. n = 16 gives exactly 4800, so 17 is the first.

hard.q: A mobile plan bill is y = ax + b rupees for x minutes. 100 minutes cost ₹340 and 250 minutes cost ₹640. What is the bill for 400 minutes?
hard.why: a = (640−340)/150 = 2 and b = 340 − 200 = 140. Then 2 × 400 + 140 = 940. Plain proportion gives the wrong 1360.

hard.q: Matchsticks make stages: 5, 9, 13, … (each stage adds 4). Which stage uses exactly 101 sticks?
hard.why: Stage n uses 4n + 1. 4n + 1 = 101 gives n = 25.

hard.q: A linear polynomial p(x) has p(1) = 5 and p(3) = 11. Where does its graph cut the x-axis?
hard.why: Slope a = 6/2 = 3, b = 5 − 3 = 2, so p(x) = 3x + 2. It is zero at x = −2/3.

hard.q: A positive number is 4 times another. If 18 is added to both, the larger becomes twice the smaller. What is the larger number?
hard.why: Smaller x, larger 4x: 4x + 18 = 2(x + 18) gives x = 9, so the larger is 36.

easy.q: Using Brahmagupta’s rule (debt × debt = fortune), find (−9) × (−4).
easy.why: Negative times negative is positive: 9 × 4 = 36.

easy.q: The temperature at Leh is 3°C at noon and falls by 11°C by night. What is the night temperature?
Which of these is an irrational number?
easy.why: √49 = 7 and 0.25 = 1/4 are rational. √17 is not a perfect square root, so it cannot be a fraction.

easy.q: Which fraction is equal to 3/5?
easy.why: 12/20 divides by 4 to give 3/5. The others simplify to different values.

easy.q: Which decimal is rational?
easy.why: A repeating decimal is a fraction (0.4545… = 5/11). A non-repeating, non-terminating decimal is irrational.

easy.q: Are the natural numbers closed under subtraction? Choose the correct reason.
o: Yes, since subtraction always gives a smaller number
No, since 3 − 7 = −4 is not a natural number
easy.why: Closure needs every result to stay in the set. 3 − 7 = −4 breaks it.

medium.why: Write 3/5 = 6/10, then 6/10 + 1/10 = 7/10. Adding tops and bottoms gives the wrong 4/15.

medium.q: Which of these gives a terminating decimal?
medium.why: A fraction terminates only if its denominator, in lowest form, has only 2s and 5s. 40 = 2³ × 5.

medium.q: Which of the following numbers is irrational?
Which is a rational number strictly between −1/2 and 1/4?
medium.why: −1/2 < 0 < 1/4. The others lie outside the interval.

medium.q: Which fraction has a repeating decimal?
medium.why: 18 = 2 × 3², and the factor 3 means the decimal never ends. The others have only 2s and 5s.

medium.q: How many rational numbers lie between 0.2 and 0.3?
medium.why: Between any two rationals there is another, so you can always keep going: 0.21, 0.211, 0.2111, …

hard.q: Write 0.272727… as a fraction in lowest terms.
hard.why: Let x = 0.2727…; 100x − x = 27 so x = 27/99, which reduces to 3/11.

hard.q: For which values of x is (2/5)(x + 5/4) = (2/5)x + 1/2 true?
hard.why: Expand the left side: (2/5)x + (2/5)(5/4) = (2/5)x + 1/2. Both sides are identical, so it holds for every x.

hard.q: Which statement is correct?
o: The sum of two irrational numbers is always irrational
The sum of √2 and −√2 is rational
The product of √2 and √8 is irrational
hard.why: √2 + (−√2) = 0. The product √2 × √8 = 4, so it is rational. Sums of irrationals can be rational.

hard.q: Which of these is a rational number strictly between 3.1415 and 3.1416?
hard.why: The value must be bigger than 3.1415 and smaller than 3.1416. 3.14155 fits; 3.1416 is the end point itself.

hard.q: To prove √7 is irrational we assume √7 = p/q in lowest terms. What do we find from 7q² = p²?
o: p and q are both odd
7 divides p, so 7 divides q too, which contradicts lowest terms
hard.why: 7q² = p² makes 7 divide p; write p = 7k, then q² = 7k² makes 7 divide q. Both share the factor 7, the contradiction.

easy.q: Expand (x + 5)².
easy.why: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² with a = x, b = 5: x² + 10x + 25. Leaving out the middle term is the usual slip.

easy.q: Expand (p − 4)².
easy.why: (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²: p² − 2(4)p + 16.

easy.q: Find (x + 7)(x − 7).
easy.why: (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b² = x² − 49.

easy.q: Use an identity to find 52².
Factorise x² + 6x + 9.
easy.why: x² + 2(x)(3) + 3² is a perfect square of (x + 3).

easy.q: Find 98² using an identity.

medium.q: Expand (3x − 2y)².
medium.why: a = 3x, b = 2y: a² − 2ab + b² = 9x² − 12xy + 4y².

medium.q: Expand (x + 3)(x + 8).
medium.why: Add 3 + 8 = 11 for the middle term and multiply 3 × 8 = 24.

medium.q: Factorise 25p² + 40pq + 16q².
medium.why: 25p² = (5p)², 16q² = (4q)² and 40pq = 2(5p)(4q), so it is (5p + 4q)².

medium.q: Find 103 × 97 using an identity.
Factorise x² − 49y².
medium.why: Difference of squares: a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b) with a = x, b = 7y.

medium.q: Simplify (a + b)² − (a − b)².
medium.why: Expanding, the a² and b² terms cancel and the cross terms give 2ab + 2ab = 4ab.

hard.q: Find 299 × 301 using an identity.
Evaluate 6.4² − 3.6² using an identity.
Simplify (a + 2b)² + (a − 2b)².
hard.why: The 4ab cross terms cancel; a² + a² = 2a² and 4b² + 4b² = 8b².

hard.q: Factorise 6x² + 17x + 12.
Simplify (2x − 3)² − (2x + 3)².
hard.why: Cross terms: −12x − 12x = −24x. The squares 4x² and 9 cancel.

hard.q: If x − y = 4 and xy = 21, what is x² + y²?

easy.q: Which is the longest chord of a circle?
o: A chord of length equal to the radius
Any chord through the arc’s midpoint
easy.why: Every chord is at most the diameter, which passes through the centre. A radius is not a chord.

easy.q: What is the angle subtended by a diameter at any point on the circle?
easy.why: The angle in a semicircle is a right angle.

easy.q: An arc subtends 80° at the centre. What angle does it subtend at a point on the remaining part of the circle?
easy.why: The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre: 80° ÷ 2 = 40°.

easy.q: ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral and ∠A = 95°. What is ∠C?
easy.why: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°: 180° − 95° = 85°.

easy.q: The perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to a chord does what?
o: It is parallel to the chord
easy.why: The perpendicular from the centre cuts the chord into two equal halves.

easy.q: A circle has radius 10 cm. A chord is 6 cm from the centre. How long is the chord?
easy.why: Half chord = √(10² − 6²) = 8, so the chord is 2 × 8 = 16 cm.

medium.q: The angle at the centre standing on an arc is 130°. What is the angle at a point on the major arc?
medium.why: The angle at the circumference is half the central angle: 65°.

medium.q: A circle has radius 17 cm and a chord of length 30 cm. How far is the chord from the centre?
medium.why: Half chord is 15, so distance = √(17² − 15²) = √64 = 8.

medium.q: A circle has diameter 50 cm and a chord of 48 cm. How far is the chord from the centre?
medium.why: Radius 25, half chord 24, so distance = √(625 − 576) = 7.

medium.q: A chord of length 24 cm is 9 cm from the centre. What is the radius?
medium.why: r = √(12² + 9²) = √225 = 15. Adding 12 + 9 gives the wrong 21.

medium.q: A chord AB makes an angle of 40° at a point C on the major arc. What angle does AB make at the centre?
medium.why: The centre angle is double the angle at the circumference: 2 × 40° = 80°.

medium.q: In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, ∠A = 110° and ∠B = 70°. Find ∠C and ∠D.
medium.why: A + C = 180° gives C = 70°, and B + D = 180° gives D = 110°.

hard.q: A triangle has sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm. What is the radius of its circumcircle?
hard.why: 6² + 8² = 10², so it is right-angled and the circumcentre is the midpoint of the hypotenuse. Radius = 10 ÷ 2 = 5.

hard.q: AB is a diameter of a circle and C lies on the circle with ∠BAC = 35°. What is ∠ABC?
hard.why: ∠ACB = 90° (semicircle), so ∠ABC = 180° − 90° − 35° = 55°.

hard.q: ABCD is cyclic with ∠A = (6x − 4)° and ∠C = (3x + 4)°. What is ∠A?
hard.why: Opposite angles add to 180°: 9x = 180, x = 20. So ∠A = 6(20) − 4 = 116°.

hard.q: In a circle of radius 6 cm, a chord subtends 90° at the centre. What is its length?
hard.why: The chord is the hypotenuse of a right isosceles triangle with legs 6: √(36+36) = 6√2.

hard.q: A chord of length 10 cm is in a circle with radius 13 cm. What is the area of the triangle formed by the chord and the centre?
hard.why: Height from the centre = √(169 − 25) = 12. Area = ½ × 10 × 12 = 60.

hard.q: ABCD is cyclic with ∠ADC = 100°. Side AB is extended to E. What is ∠CBE?
hard.why: ∠ABC + ∠ADC = 180°, so ∠ABC = 80°. ∠CBE is the exterior angle, 180° − 80° = 100°.

easy.q: Find the area of a triangle with base 12 cm and height 9 cm.
easy.why: Area = ½ × 12 × 9 = 54. Leaving out the ½ gives 108.

easy.q: Find the circumference of a circle of radius 21 cm. (Use π = 22/7.)
The circumference of a circle is 88 cm. What is its radius? (π = 22/7)
easy.why: 2πr = 88, so r = 88 ÷ 44/7 = 14. 28 is the diameter.

easy.q: Find the area of a circle of radius 7 cm. (π = 22/7)
easy.why: A = πr² = 22/7 × 49 = 154. 44 is the circumference.

easy.q: A rhombus has diagonals 10 cm and 24 cm. What is its area?
easy.why: Area = ½ × d₁ × d₂ = ½ × 10 × 24 = 120.

easy.q: A trapezium has parallel sides 8 cm and 12 cm and height 5 cm. Find its area.

medium.q: A diagonal splits a parallelogram with base 15 cm and height 8 cm into two triangles. What is the area of each?
medium.why: Parallelogram area = 15 × 8 = 120, and a diagonal halves it: 60.

medium.q: Find the area of a triangle with sides 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm.
Find the area of a sector of radius 21 cm with angle 60°. (π = 22/7)
A right-angled triangle has area 96 cm² and one leg 12 cm. What is its perimeter?
medium.why: Other leg = 2 × 96 ÷ 12 = 16. Hypotenuse = 20. Perimeter = 12 + 16 + 20 = 48.

medium.q: The minute hand of a clock is 21 cm long. What area does it sweep in 20 minutes? (π = 22/7)
medium.why: 20 minutes is one-third of a turn (120°): ⅓ × 22/7 × 441 = 462.

medium.q: Find the perimeter of a sector of radius 14 cm and angle 90°. (π = 22/7)
medium.why: Arc = ¼ × 2π × 14 = 22. Add the two radii: 22 + 28 = 50.

hard.q: One diagonal of a rhombus is twice the other, and its area is 81 cm². What is the length of the shorter diagonal?
hard.why: Shorter d, longer 2d: ½ × d × 2d = d² = 81, so d = 9.

hard.q: A bicycle wheel has diameter 70 cm. How far does it travel in 100 full turns? (π = 22/7)
hard.why: One turn = πd = 220 cm. 100 turns = 22000 cm = 220 m.

hard.q: A triangle has sides 26 cm, 28 cm and 30 cm. What is its area?
hard.why: s = 42; area = √(42 × 16 × 14 × 12) = 336. It is the 13-14-15 triangle doubled, so 84 × 4 = 336.

hard.q: A sector has radius 14 cm and arc length 11 cm. What is its area?
hard.why: Sector area = ½ × arc × radius = ½ × 11 × 14 = 77.

hard.q: A square is inscribed in a circle of radius 7 cm. What is the area of the circle outside the square? (π = 22/7)
hard.why: Diagonal = 14, square area = ½ × 14 × 14 = 98. Circle = 154, so the leftover is 154 − 98 = 56.

hard.q: A trapezium has parallel sides 30 cm and 14 cm and equal slant sides of 10 cm. What is its area?
hard.why: Overhang each side = (30−14)/2 = 8, so height = √(100 − 64) = 6. Area = ½ × 44 × 6 = 132.

easy.q: A fair die is rolled once. What is the probability of getting a 5?
easy.why: One favourable outcome out of 6 equally likely outcomes.

easy.q: A coin is tossed and a die is rolled together. How many outcomes are possible?
easy.why: 2 outcomes for the coin × 6 for the die = 12.

easy.q: A bag has 4 red and 6 blue marbles. One is picked at random. What is the probability it is red?
easy.why: 4 red out of 10 marbles: 4/10 = 2/5. Comparing red to blue (4:6) is a common slip.

easy.q: What is the probability of getting a 7 when a normal die is rolled?
easy.why: No face shows 7, so it is an impossible event with probability 0.

easy.q: A card is picked from cards numbered 1 to 20. What is the probability that it shows a multiple of 5?
easy.why: Multiples of 5: 5, 10, 15, 20 — that is 4. So 4/20 = 1/5.

easy.q: A die is rolled. What is the probability of getting a prime number?
easy.why: Primes on a die: 2, 3, 5. So 3/6 = 1/2. (1 is not prime.)

medium.q: A spinner has 8 equal sectors numbered 1 to 8. What is the probability that it stops on a number greater than 5?
medium.why: Numbers greater than 5: 6, 7, 8 — three of 8 sectors.

medium.q: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of exactly one head?
medium.why: Sample space: HH, HT, TH, TT. Exactly one head is HT or TH, so 2/4 = 1/2.

medium.q: A box has 5 red, 3 green and 2 white balls. What is the probability that a ball picked at random is not green?
medium.why: Not green = 5 + 2 = 7 balls out of 10.

medium.q: A number is picked at random from 1 to 12. What is the probability it is prime?
medium.why: Primes up to 12: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 — five numbers.

medium.q: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is 8?
Three fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of at least two heads?
medium.why: Favourable: HHH, HHT, HTH, THH = 4 of 8 outcomes.

hard.q: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum is at most 4?
hard.why: Sum 2: 1 way, sum 3: 2 ways, sum 4: 3 ways = 6 of 36 outcomes = 1/6.

hard.q: Two fair dice are rolled. What is the probability that the product of the numbers is 12?
In a test of 100 batteries, 12 lasted under 200 hours, 48 lasted 200 to 400 hours and 40 lasted over 400 hours. What is the probability a battery lasts at least 200 hours?
hard.why: 48 + 40 = 88 batteries out of 100, so 0.88.

hard.q: A fair coin is tossed 4 times. What is the probability of at least one tail?
hard.why: The only outcome with no tail is HHHH, probability 1/16. So 1 − 1/16 = 15/16.

hard.q: A bag has 5 red and 3 blue balls. Two are drawn one after another without replacement. What is the probability that both are red?
hard.why: 5/8 × 4/7 = 20/56 = 5/14. With replacement it would be 25/64.

hard.q: A bag has 5 red and 3 blue balls. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability that they are different colours?
hard.why: RB: 5/8 × 3/7 = 15/56, and BR is the same. Total = 30/56 = 15/28.

easy.q: What is the next term of 4, 9, 14, 19, …?
easy.why: The pattern adds 5 each time: 19 + 5 = 24.

easy.q: What is the common difference of the AP 100, 92, 84, …?
easy.why: 92 − 100 = −8. The sequence goes down, so d is negative.

easy.q: What is the next term of the GP 3, 6, 12, …?
easy.why: Each term is double the one before: 12 × 2 = 24.

easy.q: What is the common ratio of the GP 2, 6, 18, …?
easy.why: Divide any term by the one before: 6 ÷ 2 = 3.

easy.q: Find the 10th term of the AP 5, 8, 11, …
easy.why: a = 5, d = 3: 5 + 9 × 3 = 32. Using 10 × 3 gives the wrong 35.

easy.q: What is the nth term of the AP 2, 5, 8, 11, …?
easy.why: a + (n−1)d = 2 + 3(n−1) = 3n − 1. Check n = 1 gives 2.

medium.q: Which term of the AP 7, 13, 19, … is 151?
Asha earns ₹6,00,000 a year and gets a rise of ₹15,000 every year. After how many rises does she earn ₹7,50,000?
Which term of the AP 40, 36, 32, … is −8?
What is the nth term of the GP 3, 12, 48, …?
medium.why: a = 3, r = 4, and the nth term is arⁿ⁻¹ = 3 × 4ⁿ⁻¹.

medium.q: The 5th term of a GP is 48 and its common ratio is 2. What is the first term?
In an AP the 3rd term is 14 and the 8th term is 39. What is the 10th term?

hard.q: The 5th term of a GP is 162 and the common ratio is 3. What is its 8th term?
hard.why: Go on three more steps: 162 × 3³ = 162 × 27 = 4374.

hard.q: What is the smallest n for which 1 + 2 + … + n is greater than 500?
hard.why: n = 31 gives 496, which is not enough. n = 32 gives 528.

hard.q: What is the sum of all two-digit multiples of 7?
hard.why: They run from 14 to 98: 13 terms. Sum = 13 × (14 + 98) ÷ 2 = 728.

hard.q: Which term of the GP 3, 12, 48, … is 12288?
A ball dropped from 80 m bounces back to ¾ of its previous height each time. How high does it rise after the third bounce?
hard.why: Heights follow a GP: 80 × (¾)³ = 80 × 27/64 = 33.75 m.

hard.q: What is the sum of the first 20 terms of the AP 5, 9, 13, …?

easy.q: In “If it rains, the match is cancelled”, what is the hypothesis?
easy.why: The hypothesis is the “if” part: it rains.

easy.q: Which number is a counterexample to “All odd numbers are prime”?
easy.why: 9 is odd but equals 3 × 3, so it is not prime. 3, 7 and 11 are prime.

easy.q: What is the converse of “If a number is divisible by 6, then it is divisible by 3”?
o: If a number is not divisible by 6, then it is not divisible by 3
If a number is divisible by 3, then it is divisible by 6
If a number is not divisible by 3, then it is not divisible by 6
If a number is divisible by 3, then it is divisible by 2
easy.why: The converse swaps the hypothesis and the conclusion.

easy.q: Which value of n is a counterexample to “n² > n for every natural number n”?
easy.why: 1² = 1 is not greater than 1. All larger n satisfy the claim.

easy.q: The converse of “If x = 3, then x² = 9” is “If x² = 9, then x = 3”. Is the converse true?
o: No, because x² = 9 has no solution
easy.why: x² = 9 has two solutions, 3 and −3, so x = 3 does not always follow.

easy.q: The statement is “If a quadrilateral is a rectangle, then it is a parallelogram”. Is its converse true?
o: Yes, every parallelogram has a right angle
Yes, since both have four sides
No, a rhombus is a parallelogram that is not a rectangle
No, since a rectangle has no parallel sides
easy.why: A rhombus with no right angle is a parallelogram but not a rectangle.

medium.q: Which value of n shows that “6n + 1 is prime for every natural number n” is false?
medium.why: 6 × 4 + 1 = 25 = 5 × 5. The values for n = 3, 5, 6 are 19, 31, 37, all prime.

medium.q: Which number is a counterexample to “If n is prime, then n is odd”?
medium.why: 2 is prime and even. 9 is odd but not prime, so it does not test the claim.

medium.q: Which value of n shows that “n² + n + 17 is prime for every natural n” is false?
Which if-then sentence expresses “A number is a multiple of 9 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 9”?
o: If a number is a multiple of 9, then its digits are all 9
If a number is odd, then the sum of its digits is 9
If the digits of a number are 9, then it is a multiple of 3
If the sum of the digits of a number is a multiple of 9, then the number is a multiple of 9
medium.why: The part after “if” is the hypothesis: the digit sum is a multiple of 9.

medium.q: The converse of “If a and b are both even, then a + b is even” is false. Which pair shows this?
medium.why: 3 + 5 = 8 is even but 3 and 5 are not even. The other pairs are both even, so they do not break the converse.

medium.q: “If a number is divisible by 10, then it is divisible by 5.” Which number shows its converse is false?
medium.why: 15 is divisible by 5 but not by 10. The others are divisible by both.

hard.q: Which natural number n shows that “n² + 3n + 1 is prime for every n” is false?
hard.why: 6² + 18 + 1 = 55 = 5 × 11. For n = 3, 4, 5 the values are 19, 29, 41, all prime.

hard.q: Why is checking n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 not enough to prove that “n² + n is even for every natural n”?
o: Five examples are too few, but ten would be a proof
A finite list of examples cannot cover all natural numbers; a general argument is needed
Examples can never support a statement
hard.why: Examples can support a claim or break it, but only a general reason covers every case, such as n(n + 1) being a product with an even factor.

hard.q: Which value of n shows that “n² − n + 41 is prime for every natural n” is false?
hard.why: 41² − 41 + 41 = 41², which is not prime. For n = 10, 20, 40 the values 131, 421, 1601 are prime.

hard.q: Consider “If n² is odd, then n is odd” and its converse. Which is correct?
o: Both the statement and its converse are true
The statement is true and its converse is false
The statement is false and its converse is true
hard.why: If n is even, n² is even, so n² odd forces n odd. If n is odd, n² is odd too (odd × odd), so the converse also holds.

hard.q: Which odd number n is a counterexample to “If n is odd, then n² + 2 is prime”?
hard.why: 7² + 2 = 51 = 3 × 17. For 1, 3 and 9 the values 3, 11 and 83 are prime.

hard.q: Which number a is a counterexample to “If a² is divisible by 4, then a is divisible by 4”?
hard.why: 6² = 36 is divisible by 4, but 6 is not. 4, 8 and 12 are divisible by 4, so they follow the rule.

easy.q: Find the mean of 12, 15, 18, 20 and 25.
The marks of a student in three tests are 70, 80 and 90. What is the mean mark?
A team scores 90 runs in 15 overs. What is its run rate per over?
easy.why: Run rate = runs ÷ overs = 90 ÷ 15 = 6.

easy.q: A school has 500 students and 60% travel by bus. How many travel by bus?
Find the mean of 55, 65, 75 and 85.
The mean of 4 numbers is 12. What is their sum?
easy.why: Sum = mean × number of values = 12 × 4 = 48.

medium.q: A student scores 40 in a test of weight 1 and 80 in a test of weight 3. What is the weighted average?
medium.why: (40 × 1 + 80 × 3) ÷ 4 = 280 ÷ 4 = 70. The simple mean 60 ignores the weights.

medium.q: The mean of 5 numbers is 14. A sixth number, 20, is added. What is the new mean?
medium.why: Old total 70, new total 90, and 90 ÷ 6 = 15.

medium.q: A cafe is rated food 8, ambience 6 and service 5, with weights 5 : 3 : 2. What is the weighted rating?
A pond is dug in three sections of lengths 2, 3 and 5 m and depths 10, 6 and 4 m. What is its mean depth?
medium.why: Weight each depth by length: (20 + 18 + 20) ÷ 10 = 5.8.

medium.q: Eight players weigh 480 kg in total. A player of 53 kg leaves. What is the mean weight of the remaining 7?
medium.why: Remaining total = 480 − 53 = 427, and 427 ÷ 7 = 61.

medium.q: Class A has 30 students with mean marks 60 and class B has 20 students with mean 80. What is the mean of all 50?
medium.why: Total = 1800 + 1600 = 3400, and 3400 ÷ 50 = 68. The simple mean 70 ignores class sizes.

hard.q: In a weighted average every weight is doubled. What happens to the answer?
hard.why: Doubling weights doubles both the weighted sum and the total weight, so the ratio is unchanged.

hard.q: A final grade is 30% homework and 70% exam. A student gets 90 in homework and 60 in the exam. What is the grade?
A shop sells 12 shuttlecocks at ₹20 each and 8 at ₹30 each. What is the average price per shuttlecock?
hard.why: Total = 240 + 240 = 480 for 20 pieces, so ₹24.

hard.q: In one class 8 of 40 students wear spectacles. In another 36 of 60 do. What percentage of all 100 students wear spectacles?
hard.why: Total = 8 + 36 = 44 out of 100. Averaging 20% and 60% gives the wrong 40%.

hard.q: The mean of 10 numbers is 25. One number was copied as 42 instead of 24. What is the correct mean?
Five workers earn a mean of ₹400 a day. When a manager joins, the mean of all six is ₹500. What does the manager earn?
hard.why: Total of six = 3000, total of five = 2000, so the manager earns 3000 − 2000 = 1000.

easy.q: What is the gcd of 24 and 36?
easy.why: Common divisors of 24 and 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. The greatest is 12.

easy.q: What is 100 mod 7, that is, the remainder when 100 is divided by 7?
In column addition of 478 + 356, the units column gives 8 + 6 = 14. What does the algorithm write and carry?
easy.why: Only a single digit goes in the column. The ten of 14 is carried to the next column.

easy.q: What is the lcm of 4 and 6?
easy.why: The smallest number that both 4 and 6 divide is 12.

easy.q: Use Euclid’s method to find gcd(48, 18).
easy.why: 48 mod 18 = 12; 18 mod 12 = 6; 12 mod 6 = 0. The last non-zero remainder is 6.

easy.q: Use Euclid’s method to find gcd(17, 5).
easy.why: 17 mod 5 = 2; 5 mod 2 = 1; 2 mod 1 = 0. The last non-zero remainder is 1.

medium.q: What is gcd(4620, 2310)?
medium.why: 4620 = 2 × 2310, so 2310 divides both and is the largest such number.

medium.q: Find gcd(1071, 462) using Euclid’s method.
To add 12345 and 678 column by column, what must the algorithm do when 678 runs out of digits?
medium.why: Missing digits count as 0, so the carry still moves through the left columns.

medium.q: What is the lcm of 18 and 24?
Which pair has the same gcd as (91, 35)?
medium.why: Euclid’s step: gcd(m, n) = gcd(n, m mod n), and 91 mod 35 = 21.

medium.q: How many division steps does Euclid’s method need for gcd(120, 84)?
medium.why: 120 mod 84 = 36; 84 mod 36 = 12; 36 mod 12 = 0. That is 3 divisions.

hard.q: What is gcd(2024, 2025)?
hard.why: 2025 mod 2024 = 1, so the gcd is 1. Consecutive numbers share no factor.

hard.q: What is gcd(5040, 120)?
hard.why: 5040 = 42 × 120, so 120 divides both and nothing larger divides 120.

hard.q: To find gcd(48, 36) a student checks numbers from 36 down to 1 and stops at the first common divisor. How many numbers are checked?
hard.why: The first common divisor from the top is 12, so numbers 36, 35, …, 12 are checked: 25 numbers.

hard.q: Three numbers are added column by column. What is the largest carry that can move to the next column?
hard.why: The biggest column total is 9 + 9 + 9 + 2 = 29 (with a carry of 2 coming in), which carries 2 again.

hard.q: Using prime-factor records, 180 = 2² × 3² × 5 and 150 = 2 × 3 × 5². What is their gcd?
hard.why: Take the smaller power of each prime: 2¹ × 3¹ × 5¹ = 30.

easy.q: What is the sum of the four angles of any quadrilateral?
easy.why: A diagonal splits a quadrilateral into two triangles, each with 180°.

easy.q: What is true about the diagonals of every parallelogram?
easy.why: The diagonals cut each other into equal halves at their meeting point.

easy.q: In a parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 70°. What is ∠B?
easy.why: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram add up to 180°: 180° − 70° = 110°.

easy.q: A parallelogram has sides 8 cm and 5 cm. What is its perimeter?
easy.why: Opposite sides are equal: 2 × (8 + 5) = 26.

easy.q: A rhombus has a perimeter of 40 cm. How long is each side?
easy.why: All four sides are equal: 40 ÷ 4 = 10.

easy.q: Which quadrilateral always has equal diagonals that bisect each other at right angles?
easy.why: A rectangle has equal diagonals, a rhombus has perpendicular ones. A square has both.

medium.q: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = (3x + 10)° and ∠B = (2x + 10)°. What is ∠A?
The diagonals of parallelogram ABCD meet at O. AC = 14 cm and BD = 10 cm. What is OA + OB?
medium.why: The diagonals bisect each other, so OA = 7 and OB = 5. Sum = 12.

medium.q: ABCD is a rhombus with ∠A = 70°. What is ∠BAC, where AC is a diagonal?
medium.why: A rhombus’s diagonal bisects its angles, so ∠BAC = 70° ÷ 2 = 35°.

medium.q: A parallelogram has perimeter 56 cm and one side is 4 cm longer than the adjacent side. What is the longer side?
medium.why: Half the perimeter is 28, so s + (s + 4) = 28, s = 12 and the longer side is 16.

medium.q: A triangle has perimeter 30 cm. A new triangle is formed by joining the midpoints of its sides. What is its perimeter?
medium.why: Each new side is half of the side it faces, so the perimeter is half: 15 cm.

medium.q: A parallelogram has one right angle. What must it be?
medium.why: If one angle is 90°, the opposite angle is 90° and the adjacent ones are also 90°, so all angles are right angles.

hard.q: Which property is NOT always true for a rhombus?
hard.why: Diagonals of a rhombus are equal only when it is a square.

hard.q: The diagonals of rectangle ABCD meet at O and ∠AOB = 100°. What is ∠OAB?
hard.why: OA = OB, so the base angles of triangle AOB are equal: (180° − 100°) ÷ 2 = 40°.

hard.q: P is any point on side DC of parallelogram ABCD, whose area is 80 cm². What is the area of triangle APB?
hard.why: Triangle APB has the same base AB and the same height as the parallelogram, so its area is half: 40.

hard.q: In triangle ABC, D, E and F are midpoints of the sides. If the area of ABC is 48 cm², what is the area of triangle DEF?
hard.why: The midpoint triangle splits ABC into four congruent triangles, so DEF has ¼ of the area: 12.

hard.q: A rhombus has side 13 cm and one diagonal 10 cm. What is its area?
hard.why: Half of the other diagonal = √(169 − 25) = 12, so it is 24. Area = ½ × 10 × 24 = 120.

hard.q: P, Q, R and S are the midpoints of the sides of quadrilateral ABCD, with diagonals AC = 10 cm and BD = 6 cm. What is the perimeter of PQRS?
hard.why: Each side of PQRS is half a diagonal: two sides of 5 and two of 3, so 2(5 + 3) = 16.

easy.q: Write 3y = 4x − 9 in the form ax + by + c = 0.
easy.why: Move 3y to the right side: 0 = 4x − 3y − 9. Keep the signs of every term.

easy.q: Which pair (x, y) is a solution of x + 2y = 7?
easy.why: 1 + 2(3) = 7. The others give 8, 9 and 11.

easy.q: What is the slope of the line through (0, 0) and (2, 6)?
easy.why: Slope = rise ÷ run = 6 ÷ 2 = 3.

easy.q: What is the y-intercept of the line y = 2x − 5?
easy.why: At x = 0, y = −5, so the line cuts the y-axis at (0, −5).

easy.q: What is the equation of the x-axis?
easy.why: Every point on the x-axis has y-coordinate 0.

easy.q: How many solutions does a linear equation in two variables have?
easy.why: For every value of x we can find a matching y, so there are infinitely many solutions.

medium.q: The sum of two numbers is 54 and one is five times the other. What is the larger?
medium.why: x + 5x = 54 gives x = 9, so the larger is 45.

medium.q: If (3, 2) is a solution of 4x + ky = 20, what is k?
A ramp rises 3 m over a horizontal run of 12 m. What is its slope?
medium.why: Slope = rise ÷ run = 3 ÷ 12 = 1/4.

medium.q: Which line passes through the origin?
medium.why: Putting (0, 0) into 2x − 5y = 0 gives 0 = 0. The others give 0 ≠ 3, 0 ≠ 1 and 0 ≠ 1.

medium.q: A line passes through (1, 3) and (4, 12). What is its equation?
medium.why: Slope = 9 ÷ 3 = 3. Then y = 3x fits both points. The others fit only (1, 3).

medium.q: Where does the line 3x + 4y = 24 meet the x-axis?
medium.why: Put y = 0: 3x = 24, x = 8. The point is (8, 0).

hard.q: Half the perimeter of a field is 40 m, and its length is 6 m more than its width. What is the width?
hard.why: l + w = 40 and l − w = 6 give w = 17, l = 23.

hard.q: Where do the lines 2x + y = 11 and x − y = 1 meet?
hard.why: Adding the equations gives 3x = 12, so x = 4 and y = 3.

hard.q: Which ski hill is the steepest?
o: Rises 7 m over a run of 14 m
Rises 15 m over a run of 40 m
Rises 12 m over a run of 30 m
Rises 9 m over a run of 20 m
hard.why: Slopes are 0.5, 0.375, 0.4 and 0.45. A bigger rise does not always mean steeper; check rise ÷ run.

hard.q: A two-digit number’s digits add up to 9, and the number is 9 more than the number with digits reversed. What is the number?
hard.why: x + y = 9 and 9(x − y) = 9 give x − y = 1, so x = 5, y = 4. Check: 54 − 45 = 9.

hard.q: Where does the line y = (2/3)x − 4 cross the x-axis?
Four years ago A was thrice as old as B. Six years from now A will be twice as old as B. How old is A today?
hard.why: a − 4 = 3(b − 4) and a + 6 = 2(b + 6) give b = 14 and a = 34.

easy.q: Find the total surface area of a cube of side 5 cm.
easy.why: A cube has 6 faces of area 25 each: 6 × 25 = 150. 125 is the volume.

easy.q: Find the volume of a cuboid measuring 8 cm × 5 cm × 3 cm.
easy.why: Volume = l × b × h = 8 × 5 × 3 = 120. 158 is the surface area.

easy.q: Find the curved surface area of a cone with radius 7 cm and slant height 10 cm. (π = 22/7)
Find the surface area of a sphere of radius 7 cm. (π = 22/7)
easy.why: Surface area = 4πr² = 4 × 22/7 × 49 = 616.

easy.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 10 cm. (π = 22/7)
easy.why: Volume = πr²h = 22/7 × 49 × 10 = 1540. 440 is the curved surface area.

easy.q: How many cubes of side 2 cm fit in a cube of side 10 cm?
easy.why: Each edge holds 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cubes, so 5 × 5 × 5 = 125.

medium.q: A cone has radius 7 cm and height 24 cm. What is its total surface area? (π = 22/7)
Find the volume of a sphere of radius 21 cm. (π = 22/7)
Find the total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 7 cm. (π = 22/7)
medium.why: Total = curved 2πr² + flat base πr² = 3πr² = 3 × 154 = 462.

medium.q: A godown measures 20 m × 15 m × 10 m. How many boxes of 2 m × 1.5 m × 1 m can be packed in it?
medium.why: Godown volume 3000 m³; one box is 3 m³; 3000 ÷ 3 = 1000.

medium.q: Two cubes of side 4 cm are joined face to face to form a cuboid. What is the surface area of the cuboid?
medium.why: The cuboid is 8 × 4 × 4: 2(32 + 32 + 16) = 160. Two separate cubes would give 192, but the joined faces vanish.

medium.q: The surface area of a sphere is 5544 cm². What is its radius? (π = 22/7)
medium.why: 4πr² = 5544 gives r² = 441, so r = 21.

hard.q: The radii of two spheres are in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the ratio of their volumes?
hard.why: Volume is proportional to r³: 2³ : 3³ = 8 : 27. 4 : 9 would be the surface area ratio.

hard.q: A solid metal sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into small spheres of radius 2 cm. How many are made?
hard.why: The number is the ratio of volumes: (6/2)³ = 27.

hard.q: A hemispherical bowl has radius 21 cm. How many litres of water can it hold? (π = 22/7; 1000 cm³ = 1 L)
The radius of a sphere is increased by 30%. By about what percentage does its volume increase?
hard.why: New volume = 1.3³ = 2.197 times the old, an increase of 119.7%.

hard.q: A right triangle with legs 7 cm and 24 cm is rotated about the 24 cm leg. What is the volume of the solid formed? (π = 22/7)
hard.why: The solid is a cone with r = 7 and h = 24: ⅓ × 22/7 × 49 × 24 = 1232.

hard.q: What is the volume of the largest cylinder that can be cut from a cube of edge 14 cm? (π = 22/7)
hard.why: The cylinder has diameter 14 and height 14: 22/7 × 49 × 14 = 2156.

easy.q: A scientific model is best described as:
o: an exact full-size copy of the real object
a simplified picture of something that keeps the important features and leaves out minor details
a guess that no one has tested
a law that can never change
easy.why: A model keeps what matters for the question and drops the rest, so the problem becomes easier to study.

easy.q: In physics, the symbol c stands for:
o: the speed of sound in air
the speed of light in vacuum
easy.why: The symbol c stands for the speed of light, about 3 x 10^8 m/s.

easy.q: The SI unit of mass is the:
easy.why: The SI base unit of mass is the kilogram.

easy.q: How many minutes are there in 2 days?
easy.why: 1 day = 24 x 60 = 1440 minutes, so 2 days = 2880 minutes.

easy.q: A statement about what will happen under given conditions, which can later be checked, is called a:
easy.why: Predictions can be tested against what is later observed.

easy.q: A statement that describes a regular pattern in nature, often written as an equation, is called a:
easy.why: A law describes what happens in nature in a regular way.

medium.q: To estimate how long a cricket ball takes to fall from a 20 m high roof, which detail can be safely ignored in a simple model?
o: the logo printed on the ball
the starting speed of the ball
medium.why: Height, gravity and starting speed affect the fall time; a printed logo does not.

medium.q: Anita breathes 15 times a minute, taking in about 0.5 L each time. How many litres of air does she breathe in one hour?
medium.why: 15 x 60 = 900 breaths; 900 x 0.5 L = 450 L. 900 L forgets the 0.5 L per breath.

medium.q: Which statement correctly contrasts a law and a theory?
o: A law describes what happens; a theory explains why it happens
A law is a guess; a theory is a proven fact
A theory is always simpler than a law
A law and a theory mean exactly the same
medium.why: Laws describe patterns; theories are tested explanations of why they occur.

medium.q: Speed = distance / time. If a bus covers twice the distance in the same time, its speed:
medium.why: Speed is proportional to distance when time is fixed, so doubling distance doubles speed.

medium.q: Which of these is a testable prediction?
o: This plant is a happy plant
If I water this plant with 100 mL daily, it will grow at least 2 cm in a week
medium.why: A testable prediction states a measurable result under stated conditions.

medium.q: A model predicts that a pendulum swings once in 2.0 s, but you measure 2.3 s. What should you do first?
o: Change the measured value to 2.0 s
Decide that science does not work
Recheck the measurement and the assumptions, such as ignoring air drag
medium.why: Mismatches are clues: check data and assumptions, then improve the model.

hard.q: A person breathes 16 times a minute, about 0.5 L per breath. About how many litres of air is that in one day?
A heart beats 72 times a minute. How many beats are there in one day?
hard.why: 72 x 60 x 24 = 103,680. 4,320 is beats in an hour.

hard.q: A classmate says, "A theory is just a guess." The best reply is:
o: Yes, theories are guesses that no one tests
A scientific theory is a well-tested explanation backed by a lot of evidence
A theory is a law that has been proven wrong
A theory is a number with units
hard.why: In science a theory explains many observations and has survived many tests.

hard.q: Light travels 3 x 10^8 m/s. The Sun is 1.5 x 10^11 m away. About how long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
hard.why: Time = 1.5 x 10^11 / 3 x 10^8 = 500 s, which is about 8.3 minutes.

hard.q: Scientists may treat a cow as a sphere to estimate heat loss. Why is this acceptable?
o: Models must include every detail to be valid
It proves that shape never matters
It keeps only the features that matter for that question, and answers hold within those assumptions
hard.why: A simple model gives useful estimates if its limits are remembered.

hard.q: Someone says food cooked during a solar eclipse is poisonous. What is the most scientific way to check?
o: Compare food cooked during and outside an eclipse under the same conditions and look at the evidence
Believe it because elders say so
Reject it without looking at any evidence
Count how many people believe it
hard.why: Claims are tested with controlled comparisons and evidence.

easy.q: Who first observed cells, using a thin slice of cork?
easy.why: Hooke saw the box-like compartments of cork in 1665 and named them cells.

easy.q: Which organelle is called the powerhouse of the cell?
easy.why: Mitochondria release energy as ATP.

easy.q: The main material of the plant cell wall is:
easy.why: Plant cell walls are made mainly of cellulose.
easy.topic: Cell membrane, cell wall and osmosis

easy.q: Protein synthesis takes place on:
easy.why: Ribosomes build proteins.

easy.q: Osmosis is the movement of:
o: salt across a membrane from concentrated to dilute solution
water across a selectively permeable membrane from dilute to concentrated solution
water from concentrated to dilute solution
easy.why: Water moves toward the region with more dissolved substances.
easy.topic: Cell membrane, cell wall and osmosis

easy.q: A bacterium differs from an onion cell because it does not have a:
easy.why: Prokaryotes have DNA but no membrane-bound nucleus.

medium.q: Dry raisins soaked in plain water swell up because:
o: the raisin cells make more water
the cell wall pumps in sugar
water enters the raisin cells by osmosis
medium.why: The cell sap is more concentrated than plain water, so water moves in.
medium.topic: Cell membrane, cell wall and osmosis

medium.q: Which statement about endoplasmic reticulum is correct?
o: SER has no ribosomes and helps make lipids; RER has ribosomes and helps make proteins
SER is studded with ribosomes and makes proteins
medium.why: Ribosomes give RER its rough look.

medium.q: A plant cell kept in strong salt solution loses water and its membrane pulls away from the wall. This is called:
medium.why: Plasmolysis is shrinking of the protoplast in a hypertonic solution.
medium.topic: Cell membrane, cell wall and osmosis

medium.q: Mature human red blood cells have no nucleus. A result of this is that they:
o: make their own proteins in the nucleus
cannot divide or repair themselves but have more room for haemoglobin
medium.why: Losing the nucleus makes space for haemoglobin.

medium.q: If all mitochondria are removed from an animal cell, the cell would:
o: make much less ATP and soon run short of energy
medium.why: Mitochondria are the main source of ATP.

medium.q: The correct path of a protein made for secretion is:
o: ribosome on RER, then Golgi apparatus, then vesicle to the membrane
medium.why: Proteins are made, modified and packed in that order.

hard.q: Amla pieces kept in salt and sugar do not spoil. The main reason is that:
o: salt and sugar draw water out of microbes by osmosis, so they cannot grow
salt and sugar kill all cells by heat
salt makes the amla acidic only
hard.why: Strongly concentrated surroundings dehydrate microbes.
hard.topic: Cell membrane, cell wall and osmosis

hard.q: A human body cell has 46 chromosomes. If gametes were made by mitosis, a zygote would have:
hard.why: Each gamete would have 46, so the zygote would have 92. Meiosis prevents this.

hard.q: Which statement is true of both mitochondria and chloroplasts?
o: Both make glucose from carbon dioxide
Both are found in every cell
Both have a double membrane and their own DNA
hard.why: They are double-membraned organelles with their own DNA.

hard.q: In a potato-cup experiment, a boiled potato cup with sugar in it shows no rise in water level. The reason is that boiling:
o: turned water into gas inside the cup
destroyed the selectively permeable membrane of the cells
hard.why: Dead cells lose selective permeability, so osmosis stops.

hard.q: A cell with 8 chromosomes undergoes meiosis. The result is:
hard.why: Meiosis gives four haploid cells.

hard.q: In a culture, normal cells stop dividing when they touch each other, but some cells keep piling up. These cells have most likely lost:
hard.why: Loss of contact inhibition leads to uncontrolled growth, as in tumours.

easy.q: Growth in the length of a root or shoot tip is due to:

easy.q: The tissue that carries food from leaves to other parts of a plant is:
easy.why: Phloem carries prepared food; xylem carries water.

easy.q: The tissue that lines the mouth and the inside of the gut is:
easy.why: Epithelia cover surfaces and line cavities.

easy.q: A tendon joins:
easy.why: Ligaments join bone to bone; tendons join muscle to bone.

easy.q: The knee is an example of a:

easy.q: Messages are carried through the body by:

thick walls and a large vacuole
medium.why: These features suit rapidly dividing cells.

intercalary meristem at the base of leaves

medium.q: A ring of bark is cut all around a tree trunk. Soon the roots below the cut starve because:

water cannot go up through the bark

hard.why: Xylem lies deeper than bark.

hard.q: Which pairing of tissue and function is correct?

hard.q: Landing on stiff legs hurts more than landing with bent knees because:

easy.q: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius.

hard.q: I would have helped you if you ___ me earlier.

easy.q:
Read the passage and answer.

Every evening, Kamla ran the tiny tea stall outside Nashik railway station. For years she measured her success by the cups she sold. Then a college student suggested keeping a notebook of what customers asked for. Within a month the notebook showed that many travellers wanted something to eat, not just tea, and that most of them left the platform within ten minutes. Kamla began selling small packets of roasted peanuts and poha prepared in the morning. Her income rose by a third. She did not need new machines or loans; she needed to observe what was already in front of her. Kamla still jokes that the best business course she took was a thirty-rupee notebook. The student, meanwhile, wrote his project on her stall and secured top marks.

Question: What did Kamla's notebook first reveal?
o: Many travellers wanted food as well as tea
easy.why: The notebook showed that travellers wanted something to eat and left quickly.

Students often claim that they study better while listening to music, chatting online and checking notifications. Psychologists, however, point out that the brain does not truly do several tasks at once; it switches rapidly between them, and each switch costs a little time and attention. A student who answers a message in the middle of a chemistry problem may need several minutes to regain the same depth of focus. Over an evening, these small losses add up to a serious waste. In one classroom experiment, two groups were given the same reading task. The group that worked without interruptions finished earlier and answered more questions correctly. Yet the members of the second group were convinced that they had worked well. This false confidence is, perhaps, the most worrying finding. It suggests that the problem is not only distraction but also our poor judgement of how distracted we are.

In a drought-prone block of Rajasthan, the administration repaired old stepwells instead of laying a costly pipeline from a distant river. Critics called the decision backward-looking. They argued that a pipeline was modern, visible and politically impressive, while stepwells belonged to the past. The officer in charge, Ms Rathore, replied that the pipeline would take six years to complete and would depend on a river that was itself shrinking. The stepwells, on the other hand, could be restored within a season, were cheaper to maintain and were already known to the villagers, who understood when and how they filled. Two monsoons later, the repaired stepwells held water through the summer for the first time in thirty years. Ms Rathore does not claim that pipelines have no place in planning. Her point is narrower: a solution should be judged by whether it fits local conditions and can be delivered in time, not by how modern it appears.

easy.q: What is the LCM of 12 and 18?
easy.why: 12 = 2^2 x 3 and 18 = 2 x 3^2. Take the highest powers: 2^2 x 3^2 = 36.

easy.q: What is the HCF of 72 and 120?
easy.why: 72 = 2^3 x 3^2 and 120 = 2^3 x 3 x 5. Common part is 2^3 x 3 = 24.

easy.q: Which is the prime factorisation of 360?
easy.why: 360 = 8 x 9 x 5 = 2^3 x 3^2 x 5. The other products give 600, 540 and 240.

easy.q: The sum of the rational number 3 and the irrational number root 2 is
easy.why: A rational plus an irrational is always irrational. If 3 + root 2 were rational, root 2 would be rational too.

easy.q: What is the smallest prime that divides 7 x 11 x 13 + 13?
easy.why: The number is 13 x (77 + 1) = 13 x 78, which is even. So 2 divides it and no smaller prime exists.

easy.q: Which fraction has a terminating decimal expansion?
easy.why: 80 = 2^4 x 5 has only 2 and 5 as prime factors. 12, 15 and 18 each have a factor 3.

medium.q: What is the smallest number that leaves remainder 5 when divided by 12, 15 and 20?
medium.why: LCM(12, 15, 20) = 60, so the number is 60 + 5 = 65.

medium.q: Three temple bells ring every 18, 24 and 30 minutes. They ring together at 8:00 a.m. When will they next ring together?
medium.why: LCM of 18, 24, 30 is 360 minutes, which is 6 hours. 8:00 a.m. + 6 hours = 2:00 p.m.

medium.why: The denominator has the prime factor 7, so it is not of the form 2^m x 5^n. A rational number then repeats forever.

medium.why: Subtract the remainder first: 240 and 1024. HCF(240, 1024) = 16.

Which of these numbers is irrational?
medium.why: (root 5 + root 2)^2 = 7 + 2 root 10, which is irrational. The other three work out to 3, 2 and 2.

hard.why: LCM = 60. 9999 = 60 x 166 + 39, so the largest multiple is 9999 - 39 = 9960.

hard.q: What is the smallest 3-digit number that leaves remainder 3 when divided by 8, 12 and 18?
hard.why: LCM = 72. The smallest 3-digit multiple of 72 is 144, so the number is 144 + 3 = 147.

hard.q: The decimal expansion of 29 / (2^3 x 5^5) terminates after how many decimal places?
hard.why: Multiply top and bottom to make the denominator a power of 10: the larger of the two powers, 5, decides the number of places.

hard.q: In proving that root 3 is irrational, we assume root 3 = p/q in lowest terms and reach 3 divides p and 3 divides q. Why is this a contradiction?
o: p and q then share a common factor 3
p and q are both even
q turns out to be zero
hard.why: Lowest terms means p and q have no common factor other than 1. Both being multiples of 3 contradicts that.

hard.q: Which of the following is a rational number?
hard.why: Adding 2 + root 3 and 2 - root 3 cancels the surds and gives 4. The other three expressions still contain an irrational part.

hard.q: What is the largest number that divides 398, 436 and 542 leaving remainders 7, 11 and 15 respectively?
hard.why: Subtract remainders to get 391, 425, 527. HCF of these is 17 (391 = 17 x 23, 425 = 17 x 25, 527 = 17 x 31).

medium.why: Adding the equations gives 3x = 12, so x = 4. Then y = x + 1 = 5.
