easy.q: We ___ to the museum yesterday.
easy.why: Yesterday marks a finished time in the past, so use the simple past.

easy.q: I ___ him since 2019.
easy.why: Since with a state that continues to now takes the present perfect.

easy.q: She ___ in Chennai since 2020.
easy.why: Since with a state that continues to now takes the present perfect.

easy.q: Look! The children ___ cricket in the park.
easy.why: Look! points to an action happening now, so use the present continuous.

easy.q: ___ I borrow your pen, please?
easy.why: May is used for asking permission politely.

easy.q: You ___ wear a helmet while riding a scooter; it is the law.
easy.why: Must expresses a rule or strong obligation.

medium.q: When I called her, she ___ dinner.
medium.why: An action in progress at a past moment takes the past continuous.

medium.q: If it ___ tomorrow, we will cancel the picnic.
medium.why: In a first conditional, the if-clause takes the simple present.

medium.q: By the time the police arrived, the thief ___.
medium.why: The escape was completed before another past event, so use the past perfect.

medium.q: My brother ___ in Bengaluru for five years now.
medium.why: For five years now links the past to the present, so use the present perfect continuous.

medium.q: You ___ told me earlier; I would have helped.
medium.why: Should have plus a past participle shows a missed duty or advice.

medium.q: I ___ for the bus for twenty minutes when it finally came.
medium.why: An action lasting up to a past moment takes the past perfect continuous.

hard.q: If she had left earlier, she ___ the train.
hard.why: A past unreal condition gives would have plus a past participle.

hard.q: I wish I ___ the answer yesterday.
hard.why: A wish about the past uses the past perfect.

hard.q: The lights are on, so they ___ at home.
hard.why: Must expresses a firm guess from evidence.

hard.q: Had I known about the strike, I ___ at home.
hard.why: Had I known is an inverted if I had known, so the result is would have plus participle.

hard.q: By next March, Aarav ___ in this company for ten years.
hard.why: A future point with for ten years needs the future perfect.

hard.q: It is high time we ___ the project.
hard.why: After it is high time, a past form is used for a present need.

easy.q: ___ honest man never lies.
easy.why: Honest starts with a vowel sound, so an is used.

easy.q: She bought ___ umbrella yesterday.
easy.why: Umbrella starts with a vowel sound, so use an.

easy.q: Mumbai is ___ biggest city in Maharashtra.
easy.why: A superlative takes the.

easy.q: He has two cars, but ___ of them is new.
easy.why: Neither means not one and not the other of two.

easy.q: How ___ water is left in the bottle?
easy.why: Water is uncountable, so use much.

easy.q: There is hardly ___ milk left.
easy.why: Hardly takes any; milk is uncountable so many and few do not fit.

medium.q: The girl ___ won the quiz is my cousin.
medium.why: Who is the subject relative pronoun for a person.

medium.q: I will wait here ___ you return.
medium.why: Until introduces a time clause for how long.

medium.q: Every student ___ a library card.
medium.why: Every takes a singular verb.

medium.q: In "I know that he is honest", the clause "that he is honest" is a
medium.why: It is the object of know, so it works as a noun.

medium.q: The book ___ I borrowed from the library is very old.
medium.why: Which refers to things; book is a thing.

medium.q: I have ___ time left, so I cannot help you.
medium.why: Little means almost none and gives a negative sense.

hard.q: This is the man ___ car was stolen.
hard.why: Whose shows possession.

hard.q: He asked me ___ I had finished the work.
hard.why: Whether introduces an indirect yes or no question.

hard.q: We went out to play ___ the rain had stopped.
hard.why: After gives the time order: rain stopped, then play.

hard.q: In "The house where I was born is now a museum", the clause "where I was born" is a
hard.why: It describes the noun house.

hard.q: Which sentence has an adverb clause of reason?
o: She stayed at home because she had a fever.
She asked why he was late.
The boy who is tall is my brother.
I think that he is right.
hard.why: Because gives the reason for an action, so it is an adverb clause.

hard.q: Which is the correct way to join "He is rich. He is unhappy." using although?
o: Although he is rich but he is unhappy.
Although he is rich, he is unhappy.
Though rich, but unhappy he is.
hard.why: Although already shows contrast; do not add but.

easy.q: Passive of "The peon rang the bell."
o: The bell was rung by the peon.
The bell is rung by the peon.
The bell was ringing by the peon.
The bell rang by the peon.
easy.why: Simple past becomes was plus the past participle.

easy.q: Passive of "The cook prepares lunch daily."
o: Lunch prepared by the cook daily.
Lunch was prepared by the cook daily.
Lunch is prepared by the cook daily.
Lunch is preparing by the cook daily.
easy.why: Simple present passive is is or are plus the past participle.

easy.q: Passive of "Farmers grow rice in Punjab."
o: Rice grows by farmers in Punjab.
Rice is grew by farmers in Punjab.
Rice was growing by farmers in Punjab.
Rice is grown by farmers in Punjab.
easy.why: Use is plus the past participle grown.

easy.q: They said, "We have won." They said that they ___.
easy.why: The present perfect changes to the past perfect after a past reporting verb.

easy.q: She said, "I am tired." Reported:
o: She said that she was tired.
She said that I am tired.
She said that she were tired.
She said that she will be tired.
easy.why: The pronoun changes to she and the tense moves back to was.

easy.q: Rohit said to Mina, "I will help you." Reported:
o: Rohit told Mina that I would help her.
Rohit told Mina that he would help her.
Rohit told Mina that he will help you.
Rohit told Mina that he would help you.
easy.why: Will becomes would; I becomes he and you becomes her.

medium.q: Passive of "They are building a new bridge."
o: A new bridge is being built by them.
A new bridge has been built by them.
A new bridge was being built by them.
A new bridge is built by them.
medium.why: Present continuous passive is is or are being plus the past participle.

medium.q: Passive of "The manager will announce the results."
o: The results will be announcing by the manager.
The results will be announced by the manager.
The results would announced by the manager.
The results are announced by the manager.
medium.why: Future passive is will be plus the past participle.

medium.q: He said, "I have finished my homework." Reported:
o: He said that he has finished his homework.
He said that I had finished his homework.
He said that he had finished his homework.
He said that he will finish his homework.
medium.why: Present perfect becomes past perfect in reported speech.

medium.q: She asked me, "Where do you live?" Reported:
o: She asked me where did I live.
She asked me where do I live.
She asked me where had I lived.
She asked me where I lived.
medium.why: Reported questions use statement order and shift the tense back.

medium.q: The teacher said to the boys, "Stand in line." Reported:
o: The teacher ordered the boys to stand in line.
The teacher said the boys that stand in line.
The teacher asked if the boys stood in line.
The teacher ordered the boys that they stood in line.
medium.why: A command is reported with ordered plus to and the infinitive.

medium.q: Passive of "Who wrote this poem?"
o: By whom was this poem written?
By whom this poem was written?
Who is this poem written by?
medium.why: Wh-questions in the passive keep question order with was and the past participle.

hard.q: Passive of "Why did the committee reject the proposal?"
o: Why the proposal was rejected by the committee?
Why was the committee rejected the proposal?
Why was the proposal rejected by the committee?
Why is the proposal rejected by the committee?
hard.why: Past simple becomes was plus the past participle, with question order kept.

hard.q: Passive of "Nobody has ever seen such a sight."
o: Such a sight had never been seen.
Such a sight has never been seen.
Such a sight was never seen by nobody.
Such a sight never has seen.
hard.why: Nobody ever becomes never, and present perfect passive is has been plus participle.

hard.q: "Please lend me your pen," said Anil to Rita. Reported:
o: Anil told Rita please lend him her pen.
Anil asked Rita that she lends him her pen.
Anil requested Rita that lend me your pen.
Anil requested Rita to lend him her pen.
hard.why: A polite request is reported with requested plus to and the pronouns change.

hard.q: She said to me, "Will you attend the meeting tomorrow?" Reported:
o: She asked me if I will attend the meeting tomorrow.
She asked me that I would attend the meeting the next day.
She asked me whether would I attend the meeting the next day.
She asked me whether I would attend the meeting the next day.
hard.why: Yes or no questions take whether or if; will becomes would and tomorrow becomes the next day.

hard.q: He said, "I met her here yesterday." Reported:
o: He said that he had met her there the day before.
He said that he had met her here the previous day.
He said that he would meet her there the day before.
He said that he has met her there the next day.
hard.why: Past becomes past perfect; here becomes there; yesterday becomes the day before.

hard.q: Passive of "The principal gave Ravi a medal."
o: A medal is given to Ravi by the principal.
Ravi was given to a medal by the principal.
A medal was given to Ravi by the principal.
A medal gave Ravi by the principal.
hard.why: The object medal becomes the subject; the verb is was given.

easy.q: The word closest in meaning to "abundant" is
easy.why: Abundant means present in large amounts.

easy.q: The word closest in meaning to "rapid" is
easy.why: Rapid and swift both mean very fast.

easy.q: The opposite of "increase" is
easy.why: Increase means to go up; decrease means to go down.

easy.q: The opposite of "generous" is
easy.why: Generous means giving freely; stingy means unwilling to give.

easy.q: Find the wrong word in "He don't like tea."
easy.why: With he, use doesn't, not don't.

easy.q: "A piece of cake" means
easy.why: The idiom means a task that is very easy.

medium.q: "Once in a blue moon" means
medium.why: The idiom means something that happens very seldom.

medium.q: The word closest in meaning to "reluctant" is
medium.why: Reluctant means not wanting to do something.

medium.q: Find the error in "Each of the boys have finished the work."
medium.why: Each is singular, so the verb should be has.

medium.q: Fill the blank: He was punished ___ coming late.
medium.why: Punished for gives the reason for the punishment.

medium.q: Arrange: always / success / hard / brings / work
medium.why: Subject hard work, adverb always, verb brings, object success.

medium.q: The speaker's talk was so ___ that half the audience fell asleep.
medium.why: Monotonous means dull and unchanging, which puts people to sleep.

hard.q: "To burn the midnight oil" means to
o: work or study late into the night
hard.why: The idiom refers to working late, when lamps burned oil.

hard.q: Choose the correct spelling.
hard.why: Accommodate has double c and double m.

hard.q: Find the error in "Neither the teacher nor the students was present."
hard.why: With neither or nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, students, so were.

hard.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: She is more senior than me.
hard.why: Senior, junior and superior take to, not than.

hard.q: In "The minister's reply was evasive", evasive means
hard.why: An evasive reply dodges the question.

hard.q: Order the sentences. P: Wash the rice thoroughly in cold water. Q: Then soak it for half an hour. R: Add it to boiling water. S: Finally, let it simmer until soft.
hard.why: The steps follow the logic of the recipe; Then and Finally mark the order.

easy.q:
Passage: India's stepwells, built a thousand years ago, were not mere sources of water. Villagers gathered at them to rest, trade news and celebrate festivals. Their deep, cool chambers kept the air several degrees below the heat outside. With piped water, most fell into neglect, though a few are now being restored as heritage sites.

According to the passage, the deep chambers of stepwells
o: kept the air cooler than outside
were built in the last decade
easy.why: The passage says the air was several degrees below the heat outside.

easy.q:
Passage: The Sundarbans, shared by India and Bangladesh, is the world's largest mangrove forest. Its tangled roots trap silt and slow the waves that strike the coast, so villages behind the forest suffer less damage in cyclones. The forest is also home to the Bengal tiger, which swims between its islands. Yet rising seas and salty water are killing the trees, and scientists warn that thousands of families may lose both their protection and their livelihood from fishing and honey collection.

According to the passage, the Sundarbans is
o: a tiger reserve found only in Bangladesh
easy.why: The first sentence states it is the world's largest mangrove forest.

easy.q:
Passage: The Sundarbans, shared by India and Bangladesh, is the world's largest mangrove forest. Its tangled roots trap silt and slow the waves that strike the coast, so villages behind the forest suffer less damage in cyclones. The forest is also home to the Bengal tiger, which swims between its islands. easy.q: Which of these is the empty set?
o: {x : x is a natural number and 3 < x < 4}
{x : x is an even prime number}
{x : x is a natural number and x < 2}
easy.why: No natural number lies strictly between 3 and 4. {0} has one element, 2 is an even prime, and 1 is a natural number below 2.

easy.q: A set has 5 elements. How many subsets does it have?
easy.why: A set with n elements has 2^n subsets, so 2^5 = 32.

easy.q: A set has 64 subsets. How many elements does the set have?

medium.why: Either drink: 70 + 55 - 20 = 105. Neither = 120 - 105 = 15.

medium.why: Only tennis = total - those who like cricket = 65 - 40 = 25.

medium.q: Of 30 teachers who teach Maths or Physics, 18 teach Maths and 7 teach both. How many teach only Physics?
medium.why: n(Physics) = 30 - 18 + 7 = 19. Physics only = 19 - 7 = 12.

medium.q: n(A U B) = 50, n(A) = 30 and n(B) = 35. How many elements are in exactly one of A and B?
U = {1, 2, ..., 20}, A is the set of multiples of 4 and B is the set of multiples of 5. What is n(A' and B')?
medium.why: n(A) = 5, n(B) = 4, n(A and B) = 1 (only 20). So n(A U B) = 8 and the complement has 20 - 8 = 12.

medium.q: How many subsets of {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} contain both 1 and 2?
medium.why: 1 and 2 are fixed inside. Each of 3, 4, 5 may be in or out, giving 2^3 = 8 subsets.

hard.q: In a group, n(A) = 40, n(B) = 35, n(C) = 30, n(A and B) = 12, n(B and C) = 10, n(A and C) = 8 and n(A and B and C) = 5. How many belong to exactly one of the three sets?
hard.why: Only A = 25, only B = 18, only C = 17, total 60. The union (80) counts members of two or three sets as well.

hard.q: How many subsets of {1, 2, 3, 4} contain at least one even number?
hard.why: Subsets with no even number are the subsets of {1, 3}: 4 of them. So 16 - 4 = 12.

hard.q: In a class of 100, 70 play cricket and 55 play football. What is the least possible number who play both?
hard.why: n(both) >= 70 + 55 - 100 = 25, since the union cannot exceed 100.

hard.q: Among 80 people, n(A) = 25, n(B) = 30, n(C) = 20, n(A and B) = 10, n(B and C) = 8, n(A and C) = 6 and n(A and B and C) = 4. How many belong to exactly two of the sets?
hard.why: Add the pair counts: 10 + 8 + 6 = 24. Each triple member was counted 3 times, so subtract 3 x 4 = 12, giving 12.

hard.q: From 1 to 30, how many numbers are divisible by 3 or 5 but not by both?
hard.why: Multiples of 3: 10, of 5: 6, of both (15): 2. Exactly one = 10 + 6 - 2 x 2 = 12.

hard.q: In a survey of 200 people, 120 read paper A, 90 read B, 70 read C, 50 read A and B, 40 read B and C, 30 read A and C, and 20 read all three. How many read none of them?

easy.q: If n(A) = 4 and n(B) = 3, how many elements does A x B have?
easy.why: n(A x B) = n(A) x n(B) = 4 x 3 = 12.

easy.q: If n(A) = 4 and n(A x B) = 28, how many elements does B have?
easy.why: n(A x B) = n(A) x n(B), so n(B) = 28 / 4 = 7.

easy.why: f(-3) = 2 x 9 - 5 = 13. Squaring -3 gives +9, not -9.

easy.why: The first coordinates of the ordered pairs make up A: 1, 2 and 3.

easy.q: How many relations are there from a set with 2 elements to a set with 3 elements?
easy.why: A x B has 6 elements and every subset of it is a relation, so there are 2^6 = 64.

medium.q: f(x) = x^2 - 4x + 7 is defined on A = {0, 1, 2, 3, 4}. What is its range?
medium.why: f takes the values 7, 4, 3, 4, 7. The range lists each distinct value once: {3, 4, 7}.

medium.q: What is the domain of f(x) = sqrt(16 - x^2)?
medium.why: We need 16 - x^2 >= 0, that is x^2 <= 16, so -4 <= x <= 4.

medium.q: f(x) = ax + b with f(1) = 5 and f(3) = 11. What is f(5)?
medium.why: Subtracting: 2a = 6, so a = 3 and b = 2. Then f(5) = 15 + 2 = 17.

medium.q: How many relations are there from a set with 3 elements to a set with 4 elements?
medium.why: A x B has 12 elements, and every subset is a relation: 2^12 = 4096.

medium.q: What is the domain of f(x) = sqrt(x - 3) + 1/(x^2 - 25)?
medium.why: sqrt needs x >= 3. The denominator vanishes at 5 and -5, but only 5 lies in [3, infinity), so remove only 5.

medium.q: What is the range of f(x) = (x^2 - 9)/(x - 3)?
medium.why: For x != 3 the function equals x + 3, which takes every value except 3 + 3 = 6.

hard.q: What is the range of f(x) = x / (1 + x^2)?
hard.why: Put y = x/(1 + x^2): yx^2 - x + y = 0 needs 1 - 4y^2 >= 0, so |y| <= 1/2. The ends are reached at x = 1 and x = -1.

hard.q: On A = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}, R = {(a, b) : a divides b}. How many ordered pairs are in R?
hard.why: Counting b for each a: 6, 3, 2, 1, 1, 1 gives 14 pairs.

hard.q: How many one-one functions are there from a set with 3 elements to a set with 4 elements?
hard.why: The three elements pick distinct images in order: 4 x 3 x 2 = 24.

hard.q: How many onto functions are there from a set with 4 elements onto a set with 2 elements?
hard.why: There are 2^4 = 16 functions, and 2 of them (all to one element) are not onto. So 14.

hard.q: f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c has f(0) = 4, f(1) = 9 and f(2) = 18. What is f(3)?
What is the domain of f(x) = sqrt((x - 1)/(x - 4))?
hard.why: We need (x - 1)/(x - 4) >= 0 with x != 4. That holds for x <= 1 and x > 4.

hard.why: cos 36 = (sqrt5 + 1)/4 and cos 72 = (sqrt5 - 1)/4. Their difference is 2/4 = 1/2.

medium.q: What is the modulus of (2 + i)(1 - 3i)?
medium.why: |z1 z2| = |z1||z2| = sqrt5 x sqrt10 = sqrt50 = 5 sqrt2.

hard.why: (1 + i)^2 = 2i, so the top is 16. (1 - i)^2 = -2i, so the bottom is (-2i)^3 = 8i. 16/(8i) = -2i.

hard.q: What is the least positive integer n for which ((1 + i)/(1 - i))^n = 1?
hard.why: (1 + i)/(1 - i) = i. i^n = 1 first when n = 4.

hard.q: A quadratic with real coefficients has 3 - 2i as a root and leading coefficient 1. What is it?
hard.why: The other root is 3 + 2i. Sum = 6 and product = 9 + 4 = 13, so x^2 - 6x + 13 = 0.

hard.q: Which of these is a square root of -5 + 12i?
hard.why: (2 + 3i)^2 = 4 + 12i - 9 = -5 + 12i. The others square to 5 + 12i, -5 - 12i and 5 - 12i.
Every block of 4 consecutive powers sums to 0. 2027 terms leave the last three powers: 1 + i - 1 = i.

hard.q: On the Argand plane, what is the locus of z with |z - 3| = |z + 3i|?
hard.why: With z = x + iy: (x - 3)^2 + y^2 = x^2 + (y + 3)^2 simplifies to -6x = 6y, so y = -x.

easy.q: Solve 3x - 5 < 7 for real x.
Solve 2x + 7 > 3x - 1 for real x.
easy.why: Move terms: 7 + 1 > 3x - 2x, so 8 > x, which means x < 8.

easy.q: Solve x/3 - 2 >= 1 for real x.
easy.why: Add 2: x/3 >= 3, then multiply by 3: x >= 9.

easy.q: Which interval is the solution of |x| <= 2?
easy.why: |x| <= 2 means -2 <= x <= 2, with both ends included.

easy.q: Solve 5 - 2x >= 11 for real x.
easy.why: Subtract 5: -2x >= 6. Dividing by -2 reverses the sign: x <= -3.

easy.q: How many integers x satisfy -2 <= x < 3?
easy.why: The integers are -2, -1, 0, 1 and 2: five of them.

medium.q: Solve 3 <= 2x - 5 <= 9 for real x.
medium.why: Add 5 to all parts: 8 <= 2x <= 14. Divide by 2: 4 <= x <= 7.

medium.q: Meena scored 62 and 71 in two tests. What is the least score in the third test that gives her an average of at least 70?
medium.why: She needs a total of at least 3 x 70 = 210. After 133 marks she needs 210 - 133 = 77.

medium.q: Solve the system 2x - 1 > 3 and 4 - x >= 1.
medium.why: The first gives x > 2 and the second gives x <= 3. Both hold for 2 < x <= 3.

medium.q: Rohan has Rs 500. A geometry box costs Rs 80 and a pen costs Rs 12. What is the greatest number of pens he can buy along with the box?
medium.why: 80 + 12p <= 500 gives p <= 35. He cannot buy part of a pen, so the greatest is 35.

medium.q: How many integers x satisfy -3 < 2x + 1 <= 9?
medium.why: Subtract 1 and divide by 2: -2 < x <= 4. The integers are -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4: six.

medium.q: Solve |3x + 2| >= 7.

hard.why: Sign changes at 1, 2 and 3. The expression is positive on (1, 2) and beyond 3, zero at 1 and 3, and undefined at 2.

hard.q: The length of a rectangle is 4 cm more than its breadth. Its perimeter is less than 48 cm and the breadth is at least 5 cm. How many whole-number breadths are possible?
hard.why: Perimeter 2(2b + 4) < 48 gives b < 10. With b >= 5 the breadths are 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.
Write it as -5/(x + 3) < 0. That holds exactly when x + 3 > 0. Cross-multiplying without checking the sign of x + 3 is the trap.

hard.q: How many integers satisfy both |2x - 3| <= 9 and x^2 > 4?
hard.why: The first gives -3 <= x <= 6. The second removes -2 to 2. The integers left are -3, 3, 4, 5, 6.

hard.q: The sum of three consecutive odd positive integers is more than 20 but less than 40. How many such triples exist?
hard.why: With smallest x: 20 < 3x + 6 < 40, so 14/3 < x < 34/3. The odd x are 5, 7, 9, 11, so 4 triples.

hard.q: Solve x^2 - 4x - 5 <= 0 and |x - 1| > 2 together.
hard.why: The first gives -1 <= x <= 5. The second gives x > 3 or x < -1. The overlap is 3 < x <= 5.

easy.q: In how many ways can 6 friends sit on a bench in a row?
What is the value of 7!/5!?
easy.why: 7!/5! = 7 x 6 = 42, since the 5! cancels.

easy.q: In how many ways can the letters of the word TRAIN be arranged?
easy.why: All 5 letters are different, so 5! = 120.

easy.q: In how many ways can 3 students be chosen from 8?
easy.why: C(8,3) = 8x7x6/(3x2x1) = 56. Using 8P3 = 336 would count the order.

easy.q: If nP2 = 56, what is n?
What is the value of 10C8?
easy.why: 10C8 = 10C2 = (10 x 9)/2 = 45. Choosing 8 to take is the same as choosing 2 to leave.

medium.q: A group of 5 girls and 6 boys must pick a team of 2 girls and 3 boys. How many teams are possible?
medium.why: 5C2 x 6C3 = 10 x 20 = 200. Girls and boys are chosen separately and multiplied.

medium.q: How many different arrangements of the letters of the word BANANA are there?
medium.why: 6 letters with A repeated 3 times and N twice: 6!/(3! x 2!) = 60.

medium.q: A team of 4 is to be chosen from 7 boys and 5 girls with exactly 2 girls. How many ways?
How many 4-digit even numbers can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 with no digit repeated?
medium.why: The last digit is 2, 4 or 6 (3 ways). The other places: 5 x 4 x 3 = 60. Total 3 x 60 = 180.

medium.q: In how many ways can 6 people sit in a row if two particular people must sit together?
medium.why: Treat the pair as one unit: 5! = 120 arrangements, and the pair can swap in 2 ways. 240.

medium.q: How many 3-digit numbers have all three digits different?
medium.why: The hundreds digit has 9 choices (not 0), the tens 9 (not the first), the units 8. 9 x 9 x 8 = 648.

hard.q: A polygon has 44 diagonals. How many sides does it have?
In how many arrangements of the letters of the word LEADER do the vowels stay together?
hard.why: Vowels E, A, E form one block with 3!/2! = 3 internal orders. The block and 3 consonants make 4 units: 4! x 3 = 72.

hard.q: How many 5-digit numbers divisible by 4 can be formed from digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 with no digit repeated?
hard.why: The last two digits must form 12, 24, 32 or 52 (4 ways). The other three digits fill the rest in 3! = 6 ways. 4 x 6 = 24.

hard.q: In how many ways can 4 cards be chosen from a pack of 52 so that all four are from different suits?
hard.why: Pick one card from each suit: 13 x 13 x 13 x 13 = 28561.

hard.q: In how many ways can 5 boys and 3 girls stand in a row so that no two girls are together?
hard.why: Boys can stand in 5! = 120 ways, leaving 6 gaps. Girls take 3 of them in order: 6P3 = 120. 120 x 120 = 14400.

hard.q: In how many ways can 3 different numbers be chosen from 1 to 20 so that their sum is even?
hard.why: All even: 10C3 = 120. One even and two odd: 10 x 45 = 450. Total 570.

easy.q: How many terms are there in the expansion of (x + y)^12?
easy.why: (x + y)^n has n + 1 terms.

easy.q: The expansion of (a + b)^14 has how many terms?
easy.why: (a + b)^n always has n + 1 terms, so n = 14 gives 15.

easy.q: What is the last term in the expansion of (x - y)^5?
easy.why: The last term is (-y)^5 = -y^5, because an odd power keeps the minus sign.

easy.q: What is the coefficient of x^2 in the expansion of (1 + x)^6?
easy.why: The coefficient is C(6,2) = 15.

easy.q: What is the sum of the binomial coefficients in the expansion of (1 + x)^9?
easy.why: Putting x = 1 gives the sum 2^9 = 512.

easy.q: What is the coefficient of x^2 in the expansion of (x + 2)^4?
easy.why: The x^2 term is 4C2 x^2 x 2^2 = 6 x 4 x^2 = 24x^2.

medium.q: What is the sum of all the coefficients in the expansion of (2x + 1)^5?
What is the coefficient of x^3 in the expansion of (3 + 2x)^6?
medium.why: The x^3 term is 6C3 x 3^3 x (2x)^3 = 20 x 27 x 8 = 4320.

medium.q: What is the middle term in the expansion of (1 + x)^10?
medium.why: There are 11 terms, so the middle one is the 6th: 10C5 x^5 = 252 x^5.

medium.q: Using the first three terms of the binomial expansion, what is the approximate value of (1.02)^6?
What is the constant term in the expansion of (x - 2/x)^6?
What is the coefficient of x^5 in (1 + x)^2 (1 + x)^6?
medium.why: The product is (1 + x)^8, so the coefficient of x^5 is 8C5 = 56.

hard.q: Which is larger, (1.2)^4000 or 800?
hard.why: By the binomial theorem (1 + 0.2)^4000 > 1 + 4000 x 0.2 = 801, which is more than 800.

hard.q: What is the remainder when 7^103 is divided by 25?
What is the remainder when 5^99 is divided by 13?
What is the coefficient of x^3 in the expansion of (1 + x + x^2)^4?
hard.why: Ways to make x^3: one x^2 and one x with two 1s (4!/(1!1!2!) = 12), or three x with one 1 (4). Total 16.

hard.q: What is the value of 1 x 10C1 + 2 x 10C2 + 3 x 10C3 + ... + 10 x 10C10?
hard.why: r x nCr = n x (n-1)C(r-1), so the sum is n x 2^(n-1) = 10 x 512 = 5120.

hard.q: What is the term independent of x in the expansion of (2x^2 - 3/x)^9?

easy.q: What is the 10th term of the AP 3, 7, 11, ...?
What is the sum of the first 20 natural numbers?
What is the 15th term of the AP 5, 9, 13, ...?
What is the geometric mean of 4 and 25?
easy.why: GM = sqrt(4 x 25) = sqrt(100) = 10. The 14.5 is their arithmetic mean.

easy.q: What is the sum of the first 12 natural numbers?
What is the sum of the first 15 terms of the AP 2, 5, 8, ...?

medium.q: Three arithmetic means are inserted between 4 and 20. What is the sum of the three means?
medium.why: d = (20 - 4)/4 = 4, so the means are 8, 12 and 16. Their sum is 36.

medium.q: In a GP the 3rd term is 12 and the 6th term is 96. What is the sum of the first 6 terms?
What is the value of 1^2 + 2^2 + ... + 12^2?
Three numbers in AP have sum 21 and product 315. What is the largest of them?
medium.why: Take 7 - d, 7, 7 + d. (49 - d^2) x 7 = 315 gives d^2 = 4, so the numbers are 5, 7, 9.

medium.q: How many terms of the AP 9, 17, 25, ... give a sum of 636?
medium.why: n/2 x (18 + 8(n - 1)) = 636 gives 4n^2 + 5n - 636 = 0, so n = 12 (the other root is negative).

medium.q: An infinite GP has first term 3 and sum 9. What is its second term?
medium.why: 3/(1 - r) = 9 gives r = 2/3. The second term is 3 x 2/3 = 2.

hard.q: What is the sum of 3 + 33 + 333 + 3333?
The nth term of a series is n(n + 2). What is the sum of the first 10 terms?
hard.why: Sum of n^2 is 385 and sum of 2n is 110. Total 495.

hard.q: The AM of two positive numbers is 25 and their GM is 15. What is the larger number?
hard.why: a + b = 50 and ab = 225, so a and b are roots of t^2 - 50t + 225 = 0: 45 and 5.

hard.q: The sum of the first n terms of an AP is 3n^2 + 5n. What is its 20th term?
Three numbers in GP have sum 39 and product 729. What is the largest?
hard.why: The middle term is the cube root of 729 = 9. Then r + 1/r = 10/3, so r = 3 or 1/3, giving 3, 9, 27.

hard.q: What is the sum of the first 8 terms of 1 + 3 + 7 + 15 + 31 + ...?
hard.why: The kth term is 2^k - 1. The sum is (2^9 - 2) - 8 = 502.

easy.q: What is the slope of the line through (2, 3) and (5, 9)?
What is the slope of the line 3x - 4y + 12 = 0?
easy.why: Rewrite as y = (3/4)x + 3. The coefficient of x is the slope.

easy.q: What is the equation of the line through (2, -3) parallel to the x-axis?
easy.why: A line parallel to the x-axis has the same y at every point, here y = -3.

easy.q: What is the distance of (3, 4) from the line 3x + 4y - 5 = 0?
easy.topic: Distance of a point from a line

easy.q: What are the x-intercept and y-intercept of 2x + 3y = 12?
easy.why: Put y = 0: x = 6. Put x = 0: y = 4.

easy.q: What is the distance of the point (1, 2) from the line 3x + 4y - 10 = 0?
easy.topic: Distance of a point from a line

medium.q: Which is the equation of the line through (-2, 3) with slope -4?
Which is the equation of the line through (1, -1) and (3, 5)?
medium.why: The slope is 6/2 = 3, so y + 1 = 3(x - 1), which gives 3x - y - 4 = 0.

medium.q: What is the equation of the line through (2, 1) perpendicular to 3x - 2y + 5 = 0?
medium.why: The given slope is 3/2, so the required slope is -2/3. y - 1 = -(2/3)(x - 2) gives 2x + 3y - 7 = 0.

medium.q: For which value of k are the lines kx + 3y = 7 and 2x - y = 4 perpendicular?
medium.why: Slopes are -k/3 and 2. Perpendicular means (-k/3)(2) = -1, so k = 3/2.

medium.q: What is the acute angle between two lines with slopes 2 and 1/3?
What is the distance between the parallel lines 5x - 12y + 10 = 0 and 5x - 12y - 3 = 0?
medium.topic: Distance of a point from a line

hard.q: What is the distance between the parallel lines 3x + 4y = 10 and 6x + 8y + 5 = 0?
hard.why: Write the second as 3x + 4y + 5/2 = 0. Distance = |-10 - 5/2|/5 = 2.5.
hard.topic: Distance of a point from a line

hard.q: How far is the origin from the line passing through (3, 0) and (0, 4)?
hard.why: The line is x/3 + y/4 = 1, i.e. 4x + 3y - 12 = 0. The distance from the origin is 12/5.

hard.q: What is the image (reflection) of the point (1, 2) in the line x - y - 1 = 0?
hard.why: The mirror line is y = x - 1. Reflection swaps the roles: (a, b) goes to (b + 1, a - 1) = (3, 0). The midpoint (2, 1) lies on the line.
hard.topic: Distance of a point from a line

hard.q: What is the area of the triangle formed by the lines y = x, y = 2x and x + y = 6?
hard.why: The vertices are (0, 0), (3, 3) and (2, 4). Area = 1/2 |3 x 4 - 2 x 3| = 3.

hard.q: Two opposite sides of a square lie on 3x - 4y + 5 = 0 and 3x - 4y - 15 = 0. What is its area?
hard.why: The side equals the distance between the lines: |5 + 15|/5 = 4. Area = 4^2 = 16.
hard.topic: Distance of a point from a line

hard.q: What is the orthocentre of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0) and (1, 3)?
hard.why: The altitude from (1, 3) is x = 1. The side from (4, 0) to (1, 3) has slope -1, so the altitude from the origin is y = x. They meet at (1, 1).

easy.q: What is the equation of the circle with centre at the origin and radius 7?
easy.why: With centre (0, 0) and radius r the equation is x^2 + y^2 = r^2 = 49.

easy.q: What is the radius of the circle x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 8y - 11 = 0?
What are the coordinates of the focus of y^2 = 16x?
easy.why: y^2 = 4ax with 4a = 16 gives a = 4, so the focus is (4, 0).

easy.q: What is the length of the major axis of x^2/49 + y^2/25 = 1?
easy.why: a^2 = 49, so a = 7 and the major axis is 2a = 14.

easy.q: What is the centre of the circle x^2 + y^2 - 8x + 6y = 0?
easy.why: Complete the squares: (x - 4)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = 25. The centre is (4, -3).

easy.q: What are the coordinates of the focus of x^2 = 12y?
easy.why: x^2 = 4ay with 4a = 12 gives a = 3. The focus is (0, a) = (0, 3).

medium.q: What is the equation of the parabola with vertex at the origin and focus at (0, -3)?
medium.why: The focus is below the vertex, so the parabola opens downward: x^2 = -4ay with a = 3.

medium.q: A circle has a diameter with end points (2, 3) and (6, 7). What is its equation?
medium.why: The centre is the midpoint (4, 5). The radius is half of sqrt(16 + 16) = sqrt8, so r^2 = 8.

medium.q: What is the eccentricity of the ellipse 9x^2 + 16y^2 = 144?
A point on y^2 = 12x is at a distance 7 from the focus. What is its x-coordinate?
medium.why: For y^2 = 4ax with a = 3, the focal distance is x + a = x + 3. So x = 7 - 3 = 4.

medium.q: What is the eccentricity of the hyperbola x^2/9 - y^2/16 = 1?
An ellipse has foci (+3, 0) and (-3, 0) and eccentricity 3/5. What is its equation?
medium.why: e = c/a gives a = 5. Then b^2 = a^2 - c^2 = 25 - 9 = 16.

hard.q: A circle passes through (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 6). What is its equation?
hard.why: Passing through the origin gives c = 0. Putting in (4, 0) and (0, 6) gives g = -2 and f = -3.

hard.q: An ellipse has foci (+4, 0) and (-4, 0) and passes through (0, 3). What is its equation?
hard.why: The point (0, 3) is on the minor axis, so b = 3. a^2 = b^2 + c^2 = 9 + 16 = 25.

hard.q: A hyperbola has foci (0, +13) and (0, -13) and conjugate axis of length 24. What is its equation?
hard.why: The foci are on the y-axis, c = 13. 2b = 24 gives b = 12, so a^2 = 169 - 144 = 25.

hard.q: A circle passes through (1, 2) and (3, 4) and its centre lies on the x-axis. What is its equation?
hard.why: Let the centre be (h, 0). (h - 1)^2 + 4 = (h - 3)^2 + 16 gives h = 5, and r^2 = 16 + 4 = 20.

hard.q: A point on y^2 = 8x is at distance 6 from the focus. What is the absolute value of its y-coordinate?
hard.why: Here a = 2, so the focal distance is x + 2 = 6 and x = 4. Then y^2 = 32, |y| = 4 sqrt2.

hard.q: A circle with centre (2, -1) touches the line 3x + 4y - 5 = 0. What is its equation?
hard.why: The radius is the distance to the line: |6 - 4 - 5|/5 = 3/5. So r^2 = 9/25.

easy.q: A point lies on the z-axis at height 5. What are its coordinates?
easy.why: On the z-axis, x and y are both 0, so the point is (0, 0, 5).

easy.q: What is the distance between (1, 2, 3) and (4, 6, 15)?
What is the image of (2, 3, -4) in the yz-plane?
easy.why: Reflection in the yz-plane changes only the x-coordinate.

easy.q: What is the distance of (2, 3, 6) from the origin?
easy.why: Distance = sqrt(4 + 9 + 36) = sqrt(49) = 7.

easy.q: What is the perpendicular distance of (3, -4, 5) from the xz-plane?
easy.why: The distance from the xz-plane is the absolute value of the y-coordinate, |-4| = 4.

easy.q: A point lies in the yz-plane. What is its x-coordinate?
easy.why: Every point of the yz-plane has x = 0.

medium.q: What is the midpoint of the segment joining (2, -4, 6) and (8, 2, -2)?
medium.why: Average each coordinate: (10/2, -2/2, 4/2).

medium.q: What is the distance between (2, -1, 3) and (-2, 3, -1)?
medium.why: Differences are 4, 4 and 4, so the distance is sqrt(16 + 16 + 16) = sqrt48 = 4 sqrt3.

medium.q: What is the foot of the perpendicular from (3, 7, 9) to the y-axis?
medium.why: The foot on the y-axis keeps the y-coordinate and sets x and z to 0.

medium.q: Which point divides the segment from (1, -2, 3) to (6, 3, -2) internally in the ratio 2 : 3?
What is the centroid of the triangle with vertices (1, 2, 3), (4, 5, 6) and (-2, 2, 0)?
The distance between (a, 0, 1) and (2, 2, -1) is 3. What is the sum of all possible values of a?
medium.why: (a - 2)^2 + 4 + 4 = 9 gives (a - 2)^2 = 1, so a = 3 or 1. The sum is 4.

hard.q: A point on the y-axis is equidistant from (3, 1, 2) and (5, 5, 6). What is its y-coordinate?
In what ratio does the xy-plane divide the segment joining (2, -3, 4) and (5, 6, -2)?
hard.why: z = 0 needs (-2k + 4)/(k + 1) = 0, so k = 2, and k is positive, so the division is internal.

hard.q: The vertices of a triangle are A(1, 1, 0), B(3, 1, 2) and C(1, 3, 2). What type of triangle is it?
hard.why: AB^2 = 4 + 0 + 4 = 8, BC^2 = 4 + 4 + 0 = 8 and AC^2 = 0 + 4 + 4 = 8. All sides are equal.

hard.q: Planes parallel to the coordinate planes are drawn through (1, 2, 3) and (3, 6, 7). What is the length of the diagonal of the box formed?
hard.why: The edges are 2, 4 and 4. The diagonal is sqrt(4 + 16 + 16) = 6.

hard.q: In what ratio does the xz-plane divide the segment joining (2, -4, 5) and (-1, 2, 7)?
hard.why: On the xz-plane y = 0. If the ratio is m : n, then 2m - 4n = 0, so m : n = 2 : 1, positive so internal.

hard.q: ABCD is a parallelogram with A(1, 0, 2), B(3, 1, 5) and C(4, 3, 3). What are the coordinates of D?
hard.why: The diagonals bisect each other, so D = A + C - B = (1 + 4 - 3, 0 + 3 - 1, 2 + 3 - 5) = (2, 2, 0).

easy.q: What is the limit of (x^2 + 2x) as x tends to 3?
easy.why: The function is continuous, so substitute x = 3: 9 + 6 = 15.
easy.topic: Limits of algebraic and trig functions

easy.q: What is the limit of (x^2 - 4)/(x - 2) as x tends to 2?
easy.why: Cancel x - 2 to get x + 2, which tends to 4.
easy.topic: Limits of algebraic and trig functions

easy.q: What is the limit of sin 5x / x as x tends to 0?
easy.why: sin 5x / x = 5 x (sin 5x)/(5x), and (sin t)/t tends to 1. The limit is 5.

easy.q: What is the derivative of 3x^4 - 2x + 7?
easy.why: Differentiate term by term: 12x^3 - 2 + 0.

easy.q: What is the limit of sin 3x / x as x tends to 0?
easy.why: sin 3x / x = 3 x (sin 3x / 3x), which tends to 3 x 1.

easy.q: What is the limit of (x^2 - 9)/(x - 3) as x tends to 3?
easy.why: Factor: (x - 3)(x + 3)/(x - 3) = x + 3, which tends to 6.
easy.topic: Limits of algebraic and trig functions

medium.q: What is the limit of (x^3 - 8)/(x - 2) as x tends to 2?
medium.why: x^3 - 8 = (x - 2)(x^2 + 2x + 4). After cancelling, put x = 2: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
medium.topic: Limits of algebraic and trig functions

medium.q: What is the derivative of (x + 1)(x^2 - 2) at x = 1?
medium.why: Product rule: (x^2 - 2) + (x + 1)(2x) = -1 + 4 = 3 at x = 1.

medium.q: What is the derivative of x/(x + 1) at x = 1?
medium.why: Quotient rule: ((x + 1) - x)/(x + 1)^2 = 1/(x + 1)^2, which is 1/4 at x = 1.

medium.q: What is the limit of (sqrt(x + 4) - 2)/x as x tends to 0?
medium.why: Multiply by the conjugate: x/(x(sqrt(x+4) + 2)) = 1/(sqrt(x+4) + 2), which tends to 1/4.
medium.topic: Limits of algebraic and trig functions

medium.q: What is the limit of (1 - cos 2x)/x^2 as x tends to 0?
medium.why: 1 - cos 2x = 2 sin^2 x, so the ratio is 2 (sin x / x)^2, which tends to 2.

medium.q: What is the derivative of tan x at x = pi/4?
medium.why: d/dx tan x = sec^2 x. At pi/4, sec^2 = 1/cos^2 = 1/(1/2) = 2.

hard.q: What is the limit of (x^7 - 128)/(x - 2) as x tends to 2?
hard.why: This is the derivative of x^7 at 2 (using the formula for (x^n - a^n)/(x - a)): 7 x 2^6 = 448.
hard.topic: Limits of algebraic and trig functions

hard.q: What is the limit of (tan 2x - sin 2x)/x^3 as x tends to 0?
hard.why: tan 2x - sin 2x = tan 2x (1 - cos 2x), which behaves like 2x times 2x^2. The ratio tends to 4.

hard.q: What is the limit of (sqrt(1 + x) - sqrt(1 - x))/x as x tends to 0?
hard.why: Multiply by the conjugate: 2x/(x(sqrt(1+x) + sqrt(1-x))) = 2/(sqrt(1+x) + sqrt(1-x)), which tends to 1.
hard.topic: Limits of algebraic and trig functions

hard.q: What is the derivative of (x^2 + 1)(x^3 - x) at x = 2?
If y = (x^2 + 1)/(x - 2), what is dy/dx at x = 3?
What is the limit of (cos x - cos 3x)/x^2 as x tends to 0?
hard.why: cos x - cos 3x = 2 sin 2x sin x. Divided by x^2, it tends to 2 x 2 x 1 = 4.

easy.q: The standard deviation of a data set is 7. What is its variance?
easy.why: Variance is the square of the standard deviation: 7^2 = 49.

easy.q: A data set has mean 40 and standard deviation 6. What is its coefficient of variation?
What is the mean deviation about the mean of 4, 8, 12, 16, 20?
easy.why: Mean = 12. Absolute deviations 8, 4, 0, 4, 8 add to 24, and 24/5 = 4.8.

easy.q: What is the variance of 2, 4, 6, 8, 10?
easy.why: Mean = 6; squared deviations 16, 4, 0, 4, 16 add to 40; 40/5 = 8.

easy.q: What is the mean deviation about the mean of 3, 5, 7, 9, 11?
easy.why: The mean is 7. The absolute deviations are 4, 2, 0, 2, 4, which add to 12. 12/5 = 2.4.

easy.q: What is the variance of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5?
easy.why: The mean is 3. Squared deviations 4, 1, 0, 1, 4 add to 10, and 10/5 = 2.

medium.q: Group A has mean 60 and SD 9. Group B has mean 40 and SD 8. Which is more consistent?
o: A, because its CV is 15% against 20%
B, because its SD is smaller
medium.why: CV compares spread relative to the mean: A has 9/60 = 15% and B has 8/40 = 20%. The lower CV is more consistent.

medium.q: What is the mean deviation about the median of 3, 6, 7, 11, 14?
medium.why: The median is 7. Absolute deviations: 4, 1, 0, 4, 7, which add to 16. 16/5 = 3.2.

medium.q: Five observations have mean 12. When one observation, 20, is removed, what is the mean of the other four?
medium.why: The total was 60. Removing 20 leaves 40 over 4 observations, a mean of 10.

medium.q: Eight observations have mean 10 and variance 9. What is the sum of their squares?
medium.why: Variance = (sum of squares)/n - mean^2, so sum of squares = 8 x (9 + 100) = 872.

medium.q: Data x have mean 25 and standard deviation 5. What is the variance of the data 2x + 3?
medium.why: Multiplying by 2 doubles the SD to 10; adding 3 does not change it. The variance is 100.

medium.q: Two groups have coefficients of variation 15% and 20%. The second group has mean 40. What is its standard deviation?
medium.why: CV = SD/mean x 100, so SD = 20% of 40 = 8.

hard.q: What is the variance of the first 11 natural numbers?
A data set has five values equal to 7 and five values equal to 13. What is its standard deviation?
hard.why: The mean is 10, and every value is exactly 3 away from it. So the SD is 3.

hard.q: Ten observations have mean 15 and variance 9. An observation 12 is replaced by 18. What is the new variance?
hard.why: The sum of squares was 10 x 234 = 2340; now 2340 - 144 + 324 = 2520. New mean = 15.6, so variance = 252 - 243.36 = 8.64.

hard.q: Five observations have mean 6 and variance 9.2. Three of them are 2, 4 and 7. What is the larger of the other two?
hard.why: Sum 30 gives a + b = 17. Sum of squares 5(9.2 + 36) = 226, so a^2 + b^2 = 226 - 69 = 157. Then a, b = 6 and 11.

hard.q: A group of 20 has mean 10 and variance 4. Another group of 30 has mean 20 and variance 9. What is the variance of the combined 50?
Ten observations have mean 8 and standard deviation 3. Each is multiplied by 5 and then 2 is subtracted. What is the sum of the squares of the new values?
hard.why: New mean 38 and new SD 15, so the sum of squares is n(variance + mean^2) = 10(225 + 1444) = 16690.

easy.q: Two dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum is 7?
Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of at least one head?
A fair die is thrown once. What is the probability of getting a prime number?
easy.why: The primes on a die are 2, 3 and 5: 3 outcomes out of 6.

easy.q: One card is drawn from a well-shuffled pack of 52. What is the probability that it is an ace?
easy.why: There are 4 aces among 52 cards, so 4/52 = 1/13.

easy.q: P(E) = 0.35. What is the probability that E does not happen?
A number is chosen at random from 1 to 20. What is the probability that it is a multiple of 5?
easy.why: The multiples of 5 are 5, 10, 15 and 20: 4 out of 20 = 1/5.

medium.q: In a class of 40, 22 play chess, 18 play carrom and 7 play both. What is the probability that a random student plays at least one of the two games?
medium.why: n(chess or carrom) = 22 + 18 - 7 = 33, so the probability is 33/40.

medium.q: P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.5 and P(A or B) = 0.8. What is the probability that exactly one of A and B happens?
medium.why: P(A and B) = 0.6 + 0.5 - 0.8 = 0.3. Exactly one = P(A or B) - P(A and B) = 0.8 - 0.3 = 0.5.

medium.q: Two dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum is a multiple of 5?
medium.why: Sum 5 can occur in 4 ways and sum 10 in 3 ways: 7 favourable outcomes out of 36.

medium.q: Two cards are drawn together from a pack of 52. What is the probability that both are aces?
medium.why: 4C2/52C2 = 6/1326 = 1/221. Using 1/13 x 1/13 would wrongly assume replacement.

medium.q: A bag has 4 red, 3 blue and 2 yellow balls. Two balls are drawn together. What is the probability that both are red?
A number is chosen from 1 to 50. What is the probability that it is a multiple of 4 or of 6?

hard.q: Out of 10 points in a plane, 6 are collinear. Three points are chosen at random. What is the probability that they form a triangle?
hard.why: Total choices 10C3 = 120. Choosing all three from the 6 collinear points gives 6C3 = 20 non-triangles. (120 - 20)/120 = 5/6.

hard.q: Two different numbers are chosen from 1 to 10. What is the probability that their sum is even?
hard.why: The sum is even when both are odd or both even: 5C2 + 5C2 = 20 out of 10C2 = 45, i.e. 4/9.

hard.q: In a leap year, what is the probability of 53 Mondays or 53 Tuesdays?
hard.why: A leap year has 52 weeks and 2 extra days, one of 7 equally likely pairs. Pairs containing Monday or Tuesday are Sun-Mon, Mon-Tue, Tue-Wed: 3 of 7.

hard.q: The letters of BANANA are arranged at random. What is the probability that all three A's are together?
hard.why: There are 6!/(3!2!) = 60 arrangements. With AAA as a block: 4!/2! = 12. So 12/60 = 1/5.

hard.q: Three dice are thrown. What is the probability that the sum is 10?
hard.why: 27 of the 216 outcomes have sum 10, and 27/216 = 1/8.

hard.q: P(A) = 3/5 and P(B) = 1/2. What is the least possible value of P(A and B)?
hard.why: P(A and B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A or B) >= 3/5 + 1/2 - 1 = 1/10, since P(A or B) cannot exceed 1.
