easy.q: Each of two point charges is doubled while their distance stays the same. What happens to the force between them?
easy.why: F is proportional to q1 q2, so doubling both gives 2 x 2 = 4 times the force.

easy.q: The distance between two point charges is doubled. What happens to the electrostatic force between them?
easy.why: Coulomb's force is proportional to 1/r^2, so doubling r divides it by 4.

easy.q: Why can two electric field lines never cross each other?
o: Field lines repel each other like charges
At a point the field has only one direction
Field is zero at every point on a line
easy.why: If lines crossed, the field at the crossing would have two directions, which is impossible.

easy.q: A charge of 3 microcoulomb is placed at a point where the electric field is 200 N/C. What force acts on it?
How many electrons together carry a charge of 1 coulomb? (e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C)
A body has 3 x 10^13 extra electrons (e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C). What charge does it carry?
easy.why: q = n e = 3 x 10^13 x 1.6 x 10^-19 = 4.8 x 10^-6 C, and it is negative because the body has extra electrons.

medium.q: Charges +4 microcoulomb and -4 microcoulomb are 10 cm apart in air. What is the electric field at the midpoint? (k = 9 x 10^9)
o: 2.88 x 10^7 N/C, towards the negative charge
1.44 x 10^7 N/C, towards the negative charge
2.88 x 10^7 N/C, towards the positive charge
medium.why: Each charge gives k q / r^2 = 9 x 10^9 x 4 x 10^-6 / 0.0025 = 1.44 x 10^7 N/C in the same direction, so the total is 2.88 x 10^7 N/C.

medium.q: Two identical metal spheres carry +6 microcoulomb and -2 microcoulomb. They touch and are then placed 20 cm apart. What is the force between them? (k = 9 x 10^9)
medium.why: After touching, the total +4 microcoulomb is shared equally: +2 microcoulomb each. F = 9 x 10^9 x 4 x 10^-12 / 0.04 = 0.9 N, repulsive.

medium.q: A thin spherical shell of radius 0.2 m carries a charge of 8 microcoulomb. What is the field at 0.4 m from its centre? (k = 9 x 10^9)
medium.why: Outside a shell the field equals that of a point charge at the centre: 9 x 10^9 x 8 x 10^-6 / 0.16 = 4.5 x 10^5 N/C.

medium.q: A dipole has charges +/-1 microcoulomb separated by 2 cm. What is the electric field on its axis at 0.5 m from the centre (r much larger than the dipole length)? (k = 9 x 10^9)
What is the electric field at 0.5 m from a point charge of 5 nanocoulomb in air? (k = 9 x 10^9 N m^2/C^2)
Charges +q and +4q are 0.3 m apart. At what point on the line between them is the electric field zero?
medium.why: Set kq/x^2 = k(4q)/(0.3 - x)^2, so (0.3 - x) = 2x and x = 0.1 m from the smaller charge.

hard.q: Three charges of +2 microcoulomb each sit at the corners of an equilateral triangle of side 0.1 m. What is the net force on one of them? (k = 9 x 10^9)
hard.why: Each of the other two pushes with 3.6 N, 60 degrees apart. The resultant is 2 x 3.6 x cos 30 = 3.6 x sqrt3 = 6.2 N.

hard.q: A dipole has charges +2 microcoulomb and -2 microcoulomb separated by 3 cm. It sits at 30 degrees to a uniform field of 5 x 10^4 N/C. What torque acts on it?
A very long straight wire has a uniform charge of 2 microcoulomb per metre. What is the field at 0.5 m from it? (k = 9 x 10^9)
hard.why: For a line charge E = 2k lambda / r = 2 x 9 x 10^9 x 2 x 10^-6 / 0.5 = 7.2 x 10^4 N/C.

hard.q: An oil drop of mass 3.2 x 10^-15 kg carries two extra electrons and hangs still in a vertical field. What is the field strength? (g = 10 m/s^2, e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C)
hard.why: qE = mg gives E = 3.2 x 10^-14 / 3.2 x 10^-19 = 1 x 10^5 N/C. The drop is negative and the force must be upward, so the field points down.

hard.q: A point charge of 17.7 nanocoulomb sits at one corner of a cube. What is the total electric flux through the cube? (epsilon_0 = 8.85 x 10^-12)
hard.why: Eight identical cubes meet at that corner, so the cube gets 1/8 of q/epsilon_0 = 2000/8 = 250 N m^2/C.

hard.q: Two charges 0.3 m apart in air exert a force F. They are then placed in oil of dielectric constant 4. At what distance is the force again F?
hard.why: Force in a medium falls by K, so to keep F the distance must shrink by sqrt K: 0.3 / 2 = 0.15 m.

easy.q: What is the potential at 0.36 m from a point charge of 4 nanocoulomb in air? (k = 9 x 10^9 N m^2/C^2)
What is the SI unit of capacitance, the farad, equal to?
easy.why: C = Q / V, so one farad is one coulomb per volt.

easy.q: The electric field in a region is uniform at 50 V/m. What is the potential difference between two points 2 m apart along the field?
Three capacitors of 6 microfarad each are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent capacitance?
easy.why: In parallel capacitances add: 6 + 6 + 6 = 18 microfarad.

easy.q: How much work is done in moving a 2 microcoulomb charge through a potential difference of 150 V?
How much work is done in moving a charge along an equipotential surface?
o: Equal to q times the potential
easy.why: There is no potential difference between the points, so W = qV = 0.

medium.q: A parallel plate capacitor has plate area 0.02 m^2 and plate gap 1 mm in air. What is its capacitance? (epsilon_0 = 8.85 x 10^-12)
Capacitors of 3 microfarad and 6 microfarad are connected in series. What is the equivalent capacitance?
medium.why: 1/C = 1/3 + 1/6 = 1/2, so C = 2 microfarad.

medium.q: Capacitors of 4 microfarad and 12 microfarad are connected in series across 24 V. What is the voltage across the 4 microfarad capacitor?
medium.why: C = 4 x 12 / 16 = 3 microfarad, Q = 72 microcoulomb, and V = Q / 4 = 18 V. The smaller capacitor takes the larger voltage.

medium.q: A 20 microfarad capacitor is charged to 50 V and disconnected. It is then joined across an uncharged 20 microfarad capacitor. What is the common voltage?
medium.why: Charge 1000 microcoulomb is conserved and now sits on 40 microfarad: V = 1000 / 40 = 25 V.

medium.q: Charges +3 microcoulomb and -2 microcoulomb are 0.3 m apart. What is the electrostatic potential energy of the pair? (k = 9 x 10^9)
medium.why: U = k q1 q2 / r = 9 x 10^9 x (3 x 10^-6)(-2 x 10^-6) / 0.3 = -0.18 J. It is negative because the charges attract.

medium.q: Four charges of +1 microcoulomb sit at the corners of a square whose diagonal is 0.2 m. What is the potential at the centre? (k = 9 x 10^9)
medium.why: Each corner is 0.1 m from the centre. V = 4 x 9 x 10^9 x 10^-6 / 0.1 = 3.6 x 10^5 V. Potential is a scalar, so contributions add.

hard.q: A 6 microfarad capacitor charged to 100 V is joined across an uncharged 3 microfarad capacitor. How much energy is lost?
hard.why: Initial energy 0.03 J. Common voltage = 600/9 = 66.7 V, so final energy = 0.02 J. Loss = 0.01 J.

hard.q: A 4 microfarad capacitor is in series with a parallel pair of 2 microfarad and 4 microfarad capacitors. What is the equivalent capacitance?
hard.why: The parallel pair gives 6 microfarad. In series with 4: (4 x 6)/(4 + 6) = 2.4 microfarad.

hard.q: An electron starts from rest and is accelerated through 200 V. What is its final speed? (e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C, m = 9.1 x 10^-31 kg)
A parallel plate capacitor of 4 microfarad has a dielectric slab (constant 3) of half the gap thickness inserted, filling the whole plate area. What is the new capacitance?
hard.why: C = epsilon_0 A / (d - t + t/K) = C0 / (1 - 0.5 + 0.5/3) = C0 / (2/3) = 6 microfarad.

hard.q: A 6 microfarad air capacitor has a thin metal slab, one-quarter of the gap thick, slipped between its plates (not touching). What is the new capacitance?
hard.why: C = epsilon_0 A / (d - t) = C0 / (1 - 1/4) = 6 x 4/3 = 8 microfarad.

hard.q: Three charges of 1 microcoulomb each are brought from far away to the corners of an equilateral triangle of side 0.1 m. How much work is done? (k = 9 x 10^9)
hard.why: There are three pairs, each with energy k q^2 / a = 0.09 J. Total = 0.27 J.

easy.q: A charge of 3 coulomb flows through a wire in 0.5 s. What is the current?
A potential difference of 12 V is applied across a 4 ohm resistor. What current flows?
A wire is replaced by another of the same material and area but twice the length. What happens to its resistance?
easy.why: R = rho L / A, so R is proportional to L.

easy.q: Resistors of 6 ohm and 3 ohm are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance?
How does the resistivity of a metal change when it is heated?
easy.why: More ion vibrations make electrons collide more often, so resistivity of a metal rises with temperature.

easy.q: Resistors of 2, 3 and 5 ohm are connected in series. What is the total resistance?
easy.why: In series resistances add: 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 ohm.

medium.q: A wire has resistance 10 ohm. It is drawn uniformly so that its length doubles (volume constant). What is its new resistance?
medium.why: Length doubles and area halves, so R = rho L / A becomes 4 times, 40 ohm.

medium.q: A cell of emf 6 V and internal resistance 1 ohm delivers a current of 2 A. What is its terminal voltage?
A wire has resistance 50 ohm at 20 degrees C. Its temperature coefficient is 0.004 per degree C. What is its resistance at 70 degrees C?
Cells of 10 V and 4 V are joined in series with opposite polarity through a total resistance of 3 ohm. What current flows?
A potentiometer wire has a potential gradient of 0.2 V per metre. A cell is balanced at 6.0 m. What is its emf?
medium.why: Emf = gradient x balancing length = 0.2 x 6.0 = 1.2 V.

medium.q: In a metre bridge the unknown resistance is in the right gap and a 6 ohm resistor in the left gap. The null point is at 40 cm from the left end. What is the unknown resistance?

hard.q: A cell of emf 12 V and internal resistance 2 ohm is connected to a variable load. What is the maximum power the load can receive?
hard.why: Power is greatest when R equals r = 2 ohm. P = E^2 / 4r = 144 / 8 = 18 W.

hard.q: A 4 ohm and 12 ohm resistor in parallel are joined in series with 2 ohm across 10 V. What current flows through the 12 ohm resistor?
hard.why: Parallel part = 3 ohm; total 5 ohm; I = 2 A. Voltage across the parallel part = 6 V, so the 12 ohm carries 6/12 = 0.5 A.

hard.q: A wire of resistance 27 ohm is cut into three equal pieces which are joined in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance?
hard.why: Each piece is 9 ohm. Three 9 ohm in parallel give 9/3 = 3 ohm.

hard.q: A cell drives 1.0 A through an external 2 ohm resistor, and 0.5 A through 5 ohm. What is its emf?
hard.why: E = I(R + r): 1(2 + r) = 0.5(5 + r) gives r = 1 ohm, so E = 3 V.

hard.q: Three identical cells, each of emf 2 V and internal resistance 1.5 ohm, are joined in parallel across a 3.5 ohm resistor. What current flows through the resistor?
hard.why: Parallel cells: emf 2 V, internal resistance 1.5/3 = 0.5 ohm. I = 2 / (3.5 + 0.5) = 0.5 A.

hard.q: A cell of emf 2 V and internal resistance 1 ohm is connected in parallel with a cell of emf 1 V and internal resistance 1 ohm, positive terminal to positive terminal. What is the voltage across the combination?
hard.why: Equivalent emf = (2/1 + 1/1) / (1/1 + 1/1) = 1.5 V. The circulating current is 0.5 A and V = 2 - 0.5 x 1 = 1.5 V.

easy.q: An electron moves at 2 x 10^6 m/s perpendicular to a magnetic field of 0.5 T. What is the magnitude of the force on it? (e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C)
A 0.5 m wire carries 4 A perpendicular to a field of 0.2 T. What force acts on it?
A charged particle moves parallel to a uniform magnetic field. What is the magnetic force on it?
easy.why: F = q v B sin(theta) and theta = 0, so the force is zero.

easy.q: Why does a magnetic field do no work on a moving charge?
o: The force is always perpendicular to the velocity
The force is always along the velocity
The force is zero for all charges
The charge loses speed but gains mass
easy.why: Work = F . v . dt and F is perpendicular to v, so no energy is transferred and speed stays constant.

easy.q: What is the magnetic field at the centre of a single circular loop of radius 0.1 m carrying 5 A? (mu_0 = 4 pi x 10^-7)
A long solenoid has 1000 turns per metre and carries 2 A. What is the field inside it? (mu_0 = 4 pi x 10^-7)

medium.q: A proton moves at 2 x 10^5 m/s perpendicular to a field of 0.1 T. What is the radius of its path? (m = 1.67 x 10^-27 kg, e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C)
A coil of 50 turns and area 0.02 m^2 carries 3 A. Its plane is parallel to a field of 0.4 T. What torque acts on it?
medium.why: With the plane parallel to the field, the normal is perpendicular to B, so torque = N I A B = 50 x 3 x 0.02 x 0.4 = 1.2 N m.

medium.q: Two long parallel wires 5 cm apart carry 2 A and 3 A in the same direction. What is the force per metre between them? (mu_0/4pi = 10^-7)
medium.why: F/L = mu_0 I1 I2 / 2 pi d = 2 x 10^-7 x 6 / 0.05 = 2.4 x 10^-5 N/m. Parallel currents attract.

medium.q: In a velocity selector the electric field is 2000 V/m and the magnetic field 0.01 T. Which speed passes undeflected?
medium.why: Undeflected when qE = qvB, so v = E/B = 2000 / 0.01 = 2 x 10^5 m/s.

medium.q: A 0.4 m wire carrying 5 A makes 30 degrees with a field of 0.5 T. What force acts on it?
medium.why: F = B I L sin(theta) = 0.5 x 5 x 0.4 x 0.5 = 0.5 N.

medium.q: An electron circulates in a field of 0.01 T. What is the frequency of revolution? (e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C, m = 9.1 x 10^-31 kg)

hard.q: A galvanometer of resistance 50 ohm gives full scale deflection for 1 mA. What shunt must be connected to convert it into an ammeter reading 0 to 1 A?
hard.why: S = Ig G / (I - Ig) = 0.001 x 50 / 0.999 = 0.05 ohm, connected in parallel.

hard.q: A galvanometer of resistance 100 ohm gives full scale at 2 mA. What series resistance converts it into a voltmeter of range 0 to 10 V?
hard.why: Total resistance needed = 10 / 0.002 = 5000 ohm. Series resistor = 5000 - 100 = 4900 ohm.

hard.q: A proton and an alpha particle enter the same uniform field perpendicular to it, both with the same kinetic energy. What is the ratio of radii r(alpha) : r(proton)?
hard.why: r = sqrt(2 m K) / (q B). For the alpha, m is 4 times and q is 2 times, so sqrt4 / 2 = 1. The radii are equal.

hard.q: In a simple model, an electron moves in a circle of radius 5.3 x 10^-11 m at 2.2 x 10^6 m/s. What is the magnetic moment of this orbit? (e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C)
An electron passes undeflected through crossed fields of 3000 V/m and 0.02 T. If the electric field is switched off, what radius circle does it follow? (e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C, m = 9.1 x 10^-31 kg)
An electron enters a field of 0.01 T at 60 degrees to the field with speed 2 x 10^6 m/s. What is the pitch of its helical path? (e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C, m = 9.1 x 10^-31 kg)
hard.why: Parallel speed = 2 x 10^6 cos60 = 10^6 m/s. Period = 2 pi m / eB = 3.57 x 10^-9 s. Pitch = 10^6 x 3.57 x 10^-9 = 3.6 mm.

easy.q: Which statement about magnetic field lines of a bar magnet is correct?
o: They start at the north pole and end at infinity
They cross each other near the poles
They always start at the south pole inside the magnet and stop at the surface
easy.why: There are no magnetic monopoles, so field lines are continuous closed loops passing through the magnet.

easy.q: A single-turn loop of area 0.05 m^2 carries 2 A. What is its magnetic moment?
A bar magnet is cut into two equal pieces across its middle. What do you get?
o: One north-pole piece and one south-pole piece
Two smaller magnets, each with a north and south pole
A pole strength of double the value on each piece
easy.why: Isolated magnetic poles do not exist, so each piece becomes a magnet with both poles.

easy.q: What is the net magnetic flux through any closed surface?
o: Equal to mu_0 times enclosed current
Equal to the enclosed pole strength
easy.why: Gauss's law for magnetism: field lines form closed loops, so as many enter as leave.

easy.q: A magnet of moment 3 A m^2 is at 30 degrees to a field of 0.2 T. What torque acts on it?
easy.why: tau = m B sin(theta) = 3 x 0.2 x 0.5 = 0.3 N m.

easy.q: What is the angle of dip at a magnetic pole of the Earth?
easy.why: At the poles the field is vertical, so the needle points straight down: dip is 90 degrees.

medium.q: A magnet of moment 0.5 J/T is held at 60 degrees to a field of 0.2 T. What is its potential energy?
A bar magnet of magnetic moment 2 A m^2 is placed at 90 degrees to a field of 0.5 T. What torque acts on it?
medium.why: Torque = m B sin(90) = 2 x 0.5 = 1 N m.

medium.q: A short bar magnet has moment 1.2 A m^2. What is its field on the equatorial line at 0.2 m from the centre? (mu_0/4pi = 10^-7)
medium.why: B(equatorial) = (mu_0/4pi) m / r^3 = 10^-7 x 1.2 / 0.008 = 1.5 x 10^-5 T. The axial value would be double.

medium.q: A bar magnet of moment 4 A m^2 is cut into four equal pieces by cuts perpendicular to its length. What is the moment of each piece?
medium.why: Pole strength stays the same but the length becomes a quarter, so each moment is 4/4 = 1 A m^2.

medium.q: A solenoid with 800 turns per metre carries 1 A and has an iron core of relative permeability 1000. What is the field in the core? (mu_0 = 4 pi x 10^-7)
A paramagnetic sample has susceptibility 6 x 10^-4 at 300 K. Assuming Curie's law, what is it at 150 K?
medium.why: Curie's law: chi is proportional to 1/T. Halving T doubles chi.

hard.q: A magnet of moment 0.3 J/T lies in a field of 0.4 T. How much work turns it from 60 degrees to 120 degrees from the field?
A circular coil of 100 turns and radius 5 cm carries 2 A. What is the maximum torque on it in a field of 0.3 T?
hard.why: Moment = N I pi r^2 = 100 x 2 x pi x 0.0025 = 1.57 A m^2. Maximum torque = m B = 1.57 x 0.3 = 0.47 N m.

hard.q: At a place the Earth's total field is 5 x 10^-5 T and its vertical component is 3 x 10^-5 T. What is the angle of dip?
hard.why: sin(delta) = V / B = 0.6, so delta = 37 degrees. (53 degrees would come from using cosine.)

hard.q: A magnet of moment 0.4 J/T is initially along a field of 0.25 T. How much work is done in turning it through 180 degrees?
hard.why: W = U_final - U_initial = (+mB) - (-mB) = 2 m B = 2 x 0.4 x 0.25 = 0.2 J.

hard.q: In Bohr's model the orbital angular momentum of the ground-state electron is h / 2 pi. What is the magnetic moment of the orbit, e L / 2m? (h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J s, e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C, m = 9.1 x 10^-31 kg)
At a place the horizontal component of Earth's field is 0.3 gauss and the angle of dip is 60 degrees. What is the total field there?
hard.why: B_H = B cos(dip), so B = 0.3 / 0.5 = 0.6 gauss.

easy.q: A loop of area 0.5 m^2 lies perpendicular to a field of 0.4 T. What is the magnetic flux through it?
easy.why: Flux = B A cos(0) = 0.4 x 0.5 = 0.2 Wb.

easy.q: The flux through a 200-turn coil changes by 0.01 Wb in 0.05 s. What emf is induced?
The current in a coil changes at 3 A/s and induces an emf of 6 V. What is the coil's self-inductance?
easy.why: emf = L dI/dt, so L = 6 / 3 = 2 H.

easy.q: How much energy is stored in a 4 H inductor carrying 2 A?
Which of these devices makes use of eddy currents?
easy.why: Changing flux in a metal block drives eddy currents whose heating melts the metal in an induction furnace.

easy.q: The north pole of a bar magnet is pushed towards a coil. What is the face of the coil nearest the magnet?
o: A north pole, to oppose the approach
A south pole, to attract the magnet
A north pole only after the magnet stops
easy.why: By Lenz's law the induced current opposes the change, so it repels the approaching north pole with a north face.

medium.q: A 0.5 m rod moves at 4 m/s perpendicular to a uniform field of 0.2 T, with its length perpendicular to both. What emf is induced across its ends?
An aeroplane with a 30 m wingspan flies at 250 m/s where the vertical field component is 4 x 10^-5 T. What emf appears across its wing tips?
A 0.8 m rod slides at 5 m/s on rails in a perpendicular field of 0.3 T. The circuit resistance is 2 ohm. What current flows?
When the current in a primary coil changes by 5 A in 0.1 s, an emf of 25 V appears in a nearby secondary. What is the mutual inductance?
A 100-turn coil of area 0.05 m^2 faces a field that rises from 0.2 T to 0.8 T in 0.1 s. What emf is induced?
A solenoid has 1000 turns per metre, cross-section 10^-3 m^2 and length 0.5 m. What is its self-inductance? (mu_0 = 4 pi x 10^-7)

hard.q: A coil has 100 turns, area 0.01 m^2 and resistance 10 ohm. The field through it (perpendicular to its plane) drops from 0.5 T to 0 uniformly. How much charge flows through the coil?
hard.why: Charge = N x change in flux / R = 100 x 0.005 / 10 = 0.05 C.

hard.q: A 50-turn coil of area 0.04 m^2 rotates at 50 Hz in a field of 0.5 T. What is the peak emf?
hard.why: emf_max = N B A omega = 50 x 0.5 x 0.04 x (2 pi x 50) = 314 V.

hard.q: A coil of 500 turns has a flux of 4 x 10^-4 Wb through each turn when it carries 2 A. How much energy is stored in it?
The flux through a single loop of resistance 5 ohm is 4t^2 - 3t webers, with t in seconds. What current flows at t = 2 s?
hard.why: emf = d(phi)/dt = 8t - 3 = 13 V at t = 2 s. I = 13 / 5 = 2.6 A.

hard.q: A square loop of side 0.2 m and resistance 0.4 ohm is being pulled out of a field of 0.5 T at a steady 2 m/s. What power is dissipated as heat in it?
A 0.5 m metal rod rotates about one end at 20 rad/s in a uniform field of 0.4 T perpendicular to its plane. What is the emf between its ends?

easy.q: An alternating voltage is v = 311 sin(100 pi t). What is its frequency?
easy.why: Comparing with sin(2 pi f t) gives 2 pi f = 100 pi, so f = 50 Hz.

easy.q: An ideal transformer has 100 primary and 1000 secondary turns. If the primary gets 220 V, what is the secondary voltage?
easy.why: Vs / Vp = Ns / Np, so Vs = 220 x 10 = 2200 V.

easy.q: What is the impedance of a series LCR circuit at resonance?
o: It equals R and is minimum
easy.why: At resonance X_L = X_C so they cancel and Z = R, the minimum value.

easy.q: What is the average power consumed by an ideal capacitor in an AC circuit over a full cycle?
o: Equal to V rms x I rms
easy.why: Voltage and current are 90 degrees apart, so the capacitor stores and returns energy and uses none on average.

easy.q: What is the power factor of a circuit containing a pure inductor?
easy.why: Current lags the voltage by 90 degrees, so cos(90) = 0 and no net power is used.

easy.q: In an AC circuit containing only a resistor, how are the voltage and current related in phase?
easy.why: For a pure resistor, V = I R at every instant, so they rise and fall together.

medium.q: A step-down transformer has 1000 primary turns, 100 secondary turns, 2200 V input and delivers 10 A. If it is ideal, what is the primary current?
medium.why: Output power = 220 x 10 = 2200 W, so Ip = 2200 / 2200 = 1 A. Current steps up as voltage steps down.

medium.q: A series circuit has R = 6 ohm, X_L = 14 ohm and X_C = 6 ohm on a 120 V rms supply. What is the rms current?
A series circuit has L = 5 mH and C = 2 microfarad. What is its resonant frequency?
A 50 microfarad capacitor is connected to a 220 V, 50 Hz supply. What is the rms current?
An AC voltage is v = 311 sin(100 pi t) volt. What is its value at t = 1/300 s?
A series circuit has R = 12 ohm and impedance 20 ohm on a 200 V rms supply. What average power does it use?
medium.why: I = 200 / 20 = 10 A. P = I^2 R = 100 x 12 = 1200 W (equivalently V I cos(phi) with cos(phi) = 0.6).

hard.q: A series circuit has R = 30 ohm, inductive reactance 60 ohm and capacitive reactance 20 ohm. It is connected to a 100 V rms supply. What is the rms current?
A series circuit has R = 5 ohm, L = 0.5 H and C = 8 microfarad. What is its quality factor at resonance?
hard.why: omega_0 = 1 / sqrt(LC) = 500 rad/s. Q = omega_0 L / R = 500 x 0.5 / 5 = 50.

hard.q: A resistor of 60 ohm is in series with a capacitor of reactance 80 ohm on a 200 V rms supply. What is the rms voltage across the capacitor?
A series circuit has R = 15 ohm, X_L = 35 ohm and X_C = 15 ohm. What is the phase angle between the supply voltage and the current?
hard.why: tan(phi) = (X_L - X_C) / R = 20/15, so phi = 53 degrees. X_L is larger, so the circuit is inductive and voltage leads.

hard.q: A plant sends 20 kW over a line of total resistance 0.5 ohm. If power is stepped up to 2000 V before transmission, what is the heat loss in the line?
For the same series circuit (R = 30 ohm, X_L = 60 ohm, X_C = 20 ohm, 100 V rms supply), what is the average power consumed?
hard.why: I = 2 A and cos(phi) = R/Z = 30/50 = 0.6, so P = V I cos(phi) = 100 x 2 x 0.6 = 120 W (also I^2 R = 4 x 30).

easy.q: Which of these electromagnetic waves has the longest wavelength?
easy.why: Radio waves lie at the low-frequency, long-wavelength end of the electromagnetic spectrum.

easy.q: Which radiation is used in TV remote controls?
easy.why: Remote controls send pulses of infrared light.

easy.q: Which part of the atmosphere absorbs most of the harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun?
easy.why: Ozone in the stratosphere absorbs most of the Sun's ultraviolet.

easy.q: How are electromagnetic waves produced?
o: By charges moving at constant velocity
easy.why: Only an accelerating charge produces a changing electric and magnetic field that radiates.

easy.q: In an electromagnetic wave, how are the electric field, magnetic field and direction of travel related?
o: E and B are parallel to the direction of travel
E is along travel and B is perpendicular
E and B are parallel to each other
easy.why: EM waves are transverse: E, B and the propagation direction are at right angles to each other.

easy.q: What is the wavelength of an electromagnetic wave of frequency 3 x 10^9 Hz in vacuum? (c = 3 x 10^8 m/s)

medium.q: What is the frequency of light of wavelength 500 nm in vacuum? (c = 3 x 10^8 m/s)
What is the wavelength of light of frequency 6 x 10^14 Hz in vacuum? (c = 3 x 10^8 m/s)
A 0.5 microfarad capacitor is charged so that its voltage rises at 40 V/s. What is the displacement current between its plates?
medium.why: I_d = I_conduction = C dV/dt = 0.5 x 10^-6 x 40 = 20 microampere.

medium.q: In an EM wave the electric field points along +y and the magnetic field along +z. In which direction does the wave travel?
medium.why: Direction of travel is along E x B = y x z = +x.

medium.q: In a plane EM wave in vacuum the magnetic field amplitude is 2 x 10^-8 T. What is the electric field amplitude? (c = 3 x 10^8 m/s)
A plane EM wave in vacuum has electric field amplitude 30 V/m. What is its average energy density? (epsilon_0 = 8.85 x 10^-12)
medium.why: Average energy density = 1/2 epsilon_0 E0^2 = 0.5 x 8.85 x 10^-12 x 900 = 4.0 x 10^-9 J/m^3.

hard.q: The electric field amplitude of a plane EM wave in vacuum is 100 V/m. What is its average intensity? (epsilon_0 = 8.85 x 10^-12, c = 3 x 10^8 m/s)
The electric field between circular capacitor plates of radius 0.1 m rises at 10^12 V/m per second. What is the displacement current? (epsilon_0 = 8.85 x 10^-12)
hard.why: I_d = epsilon_0 A dE/dt = 8.85 x 10^-12 x pi x 0.01 x 10^12 = 0.28 A.

hard.q: A beam of intensity 900 W/m^2 falls on a perfectly reflecting surface at normal incidence. What is the radiation pressure? (c = 3 x 10^8 m/s)
hard.why: Pressure on a perfect absorber is I / c = 3 x 10^-6 Pa. A perfect reflector gets double, 6 x 10^-6 Pa.

hard.q: A surface absorbs 9 J of electromagnetic energy completely from a beam. What momentum is delivered to it? (c = 3 x 10^8 m/s)
hard.why: Momentum = energy / c = 9 / (3 x 10^8) = 3 x 10^-8 kg m/s.

hard.q: The magnetic field of a wave in vacuum is B = 2 x 10^-7 sin(500 x + 1.5 x 10^11 t) tesla in SI units. What are the wave speed's direction and the electric field amplitude?
hard.why: The sign between kx and omega t is +, so the wave moves towards -x. Speed = 1.5 x 10^11 / 500 = 3 x 10^8 m/s, and E0 = c B0 = 60 V/m.

hard.q: The voltage across a 2 microfarad capacitor rises at 5 V/s. What is the displacement current between its plates?
hard.why: I_d equals the conduction current C dV/dt = 2 x 10^-6 x 5 = 10^-5 A.

easy.q: What is the speed of light in glass of refractive index 1.5? (c = 3 x 10^8 m/s)
A convex lens has a focal length of 25 cm. What is its power?
Which mirror always gives a virtual, erect and diminished image of a real object?
easy.why: A convex mirror spreads rays so its image is always behind the mirror, upright and smaller.

easy.q: An object 2 cm tall forms an image 6 cm tall. What is the magnification magnitude?
easy.why: m = image height / object height = 6 / 2 = 3.

easy.q: When light passes from air into glass, which of these quantities stays the same?
easy.why: Frequency is set by the source. Speed and wavelength both fall in glass.

easy.q: Which pair of conditions is needed for total internal reflection?
o: Rarer to denser medium, angle above the critical angle
Denser to rarer medium, angle below the critical angle
Denser to rarer medium, angle above the critical angle
easy.why: TIR needs light going into a rarer medium at an incidence angle larger than the critical angle.

medium.q: An object is 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. Where is the image formed?
o: 30 cm in front of the mirror
7.5 cm in front of the mirror
15 cm in front of the mirror

medium.q: A magnifying glass of focal length 5 cm is used with the image at 25 cm from the eye. What is the angular magnification?
An object is 20 cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 20 cm. Where is the image?
o: 10 cm in front of the mirror
medium.why: With f = +20 and u = -20, 1/v = 1/20 + 1/20, so v = +10 cm: virtual, behind the mirror.

medium.q: A telescope has an objective of focal length 100 cm and an eyepiece of focal length 4 cm. What is its magnification in normal adjustment?
A prism of angle 60 degrees has refractive index sqrt3. What is its angle of minimum deviation?
medium.why: n = sin((A + D)/2) / sin(A/2): sin((60 + D)/2) = sqrt3 x 0.5, so (60 + D)/2 = 60 and D = 60 degrees.

medium.q: What is the critical angle for light going from glass of refractive index 1.5 to air?
medium.why: sin(c) = 1 / 1.5, so c = 41.8 degrees.

hard.q: An object is 30 cm from a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. Which describes the image?
o: Virtual, erect, 60 cm from the lens
Real, inverted, 60 cm from the lens
Real, inverted, 12 cm from the lens
Virtual, erect, 12 cm from the lens
hard.why: 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/20 - 1/30 = 1/60, so v = +60 cm (real). Magnification = v/u = -2 (inverted).

hard.q: A glass slab (n = 1.5) of thickness 9 cm lies on a printed page. By how much does the print appear raised when viewed from above?
Two convex lenses of focal length 20 cm each are 10 cm apart on a common axis. What is the focal length of the combination?
A glass lens (n = 1.5) has focal length 20 cm in air. What is its focal length when immersed in water (n = 4/3)?
A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 30 cm. What is the power of the combination?
A compound microscope has objective focal length 1 cm and eyepiece focal length 5 cm. An object is 1.2 cm from the objective and the final image is at 25 cm. What is the magnification?
hard.why: Objective: 1/v = 1 - 1/1.2 gives v = 6 cm, so m_o = 5. Eyepiece: m_e = 1 + 25/5 = 6. Total = 5 x 6 = 30.

easy.q: Which phenomenon proves that light waves are transverse?
easy.why: Only transverse waves can be polarised.

easy.q: What is the shape of the wavefront of light from a very distant source such as a star?
easy.why: Over a small region a distant source's spherical wavefront is nearly flat, so it is taken as plane.

easy.q: At a point the path difference of two coherent waves is 2 lambda. What do we see there?
easy.why: Constructive interference occurs for path differences n lambda, here n = 2.

easy.q: In Young's experiment the wavelength of light is doubled with everything else unchanged. What happens to the fringe width?
easy.why: Fringe width beta = lambda D / d is proportional to lambda.

easy.q: When is diffraction at a single slit most noticeable?
o: When the slit is much wider than the wavelength
When the slit width is comparable to the wavelength
When the screen is very close
easy.why: Bending is large only when the opening is of the same order as lambda.

easy.q: In Young's double slit experiment, the fringe width is given by lambda D / d. If the screen is moved to double the distance D, the fringe width:
easy.why: Fringe width is proportional to D.

medium.q: In a double slit experiment the slit separation is 0.3 mm, the screen is 1.2 m away and the wavelength is 500 nm. What is the fringe width?
In a double slit experiment lambda = 600 nm, slit separation 0.5 mm and screen distance 1.5 m. What is the fringe width?
Plane polarised light of intensity I0 falls on an analyser whose axis is at 60 degrees to its plane of polarisation. What intensity is transmitted?
medium.why: Malus's law: I = I0 cos^2(60) = I0 x (1/2)^2 = I0/4.

medium.q: Light of wavelength 600 nm in air enters glass of refractive index 1.5. What is its wavelength in the glass?
medium.why: Frequency stays fixed and speed falls by n, so lambda falls by n: 600 / 1.5 = 400 nm.

medium.q: A double slit experiment gives fringe width 1.2 mm in air. What is the fringe width if the whole set-up is placed in water of refractive index 4/3?
medium.why: Wavelength in water is lambda / n, so fringe width falls by the same factor: 1.2 x 3/4 = 0.9 mm.

medium.q: Light is polarised on reflection from glass of refractive index root 3. What is the polarising (Brewster) angle?
medium.why: tan(i_B) = n = root 3, so i_B = 60 degrees.

hard.q: Light of wavelength 600 nm falls on a single slit 0.2 mm wide. A screen is 2 m away. What is the width of the central maximum?
hard.why: Width = 2 lambda D / a = 2 x 6 x 10^-7 x 2 / 2 x 10^-4 = 0.012 m.

hard.q: Two coherent slits each give intensity I0 on the screen when alone. At a point where the path difference is lambda/6, what is the net intensity?
hard.why: Phase = 2 pi/6 = 60 degrees. I = 4 I0 cos^2(30) = 4 I0 x 0.75 = 3 I0.

hard.q: In a double slit experiment a thin sheet of refractive index 1.5 and thickness 6 micrometre covers one slit. The wavelength is 600 nm. By how many fringes does the pattern shift?
hard.why: Extra path = (n - 1) t = 0.5 x 6 x 10^-6 = 3 x 10^-6 m. Number of fringes = 3 x 10^-6 / 6 x 10^-7 = 5.

hard.q: Two coherent sources have intensities in the ratio 9 : 1. What is the ratio I(max) : I(min) in the interference pattern?
hard.why: Amplitudes are in the ratio 3 : 1. I(max)/I(min) = (3 + 1)^2 / (3 - 1)^2 = 16/4 = 4.

hard.q: Two coherent sources each give intensity I0 at a point when acting alone. At a point where the path difference is a quarter of the wavelength, what is the resultant intensity?
hard.why: Phase difference = 90 degrees. I = 4 I0 cos^2(45) = 2 I0.

hard.q: In a double slit experiment (visible light 400 to 700 nm) the 3rd bright fringe of 600 nm is at a certain point. Which other wavelength also has a bright fringe at the same point?
hard.why: The point has 3 x 600 = 1800 nm path. A wavelength must divide 1800 nm into a whole number: 1800/450 = 4. For 500, 550, 400 nm the ratios 3.6, 3.27, 4.5 are not whole numbers.

easy.q: What is the energy of a photon of wavelength 620 nm? (hc = 1240 eV nm)
What is the frequency of a photon of energy 4.14 eV? (h = 4.14 x 10^-15 eV s)
A metal has work function 4.5 eV. Light of photon energy 3.1 eV falls on it. What is observed?
o: Electrons are emitted after a delay
Emission starts if intensity is raised
easy.why: Photon energy is below the work function, so no emission occurs whatever the intensity.

easy.q: How does the de Broglie wavelength of a particle depend on its momentum?
easy.why: lambda = h / p.

easy.q: What is the momentum of a photon of wavelength 600 nm? (h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J s)
In the photoelectric effect, above the threshold frequency, how does the photoelectric current depend on the intensity of light?
easy.why: More photons per second free more electrons, so saturation current increases with intensity.

medium.q: A metal has work function 2.48 eV. What is its threshold wavelength? (hc = 1240 eV nm)
medium.why: lambda_0 = hc / phi = 1240 / 2.48 = 500 nm.

medium.q: Light of photon energy 5.0 eV falls on a metal of work function 2.0 eV. What is the stopping potential?
Light of wavelength 300 nm falls on a metal of work function 2.5 eV. What is the stopping potential? (hc = 1240 eV nm)
What is the de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through 600 V? (lambda = 12.27 / sqrt(V) angstrom)
medium.why: lambda = 12.27 / sqrt600 = 12.27 / 24.5 = 0.50 angstrom.

medium.q: What is the de Broglie wavelength of a 0.05 kg ball moving at 20 m/s? (h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J s)
medium.why: lambda = h / m v = 6.63 x 10^-34 / (0.05 x 20) = 6.6 x 10^-34 m, far too small to see.

medium.q: What is the de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through 150 V? (lambda = 12.27 / root V angstrom)

hard.q: Through what potential difference must an electron be accelerated to have a de Broglie wavelength of 0.5 angstrom? (lambda = 12.27 / sqrt(V) angstrom)
A metal has work function 2.48 eV. Light of wavelength 400 nm falls on it. What is the stopping potential? (hc = 1240 eV nm)
hard.why: Photon energy = 1240 / 400 = 3.1 eV. KE_max = 3.1 - 2.48 = 0.62 eV, so V_s = 0.62 V.

hard.q: Light of wavelength lambda gives photoelectrons of maximum kinetic energy 1.0 eV from a metal of work function 2.0 eV. What is the maximum kinetic energy if the wavelength is halved?
hard.why: Photon energy was 3 eV. Halving lambda doubles it to 6 eV, so KE = 6 - 2 = 4 eV (not double the old 1 eV).

hard.q: A 6 W light beam is completely absorbed by a surface. What force does it exert? (c = 3 x 10^8 m/s)
hard.why: Force = P / c = 6 / 3 x 10^8 = 2 x 10^-8 N. A perfect reflector would get double.

hard.q: A 0.1 W beam of 400 nm light hits a photocell where 1 photon in 1000 ejects an electron. What is the photocurrent? (h = 6.63 x 10^-34, c = 3 x 10^8, e = 1.6 x 10^-19)
hard.why: Photon energy = 4.97 x 10^-19 J, so photons per second = 0.1 / 4.97 x 10^-19 = 2 x 10^17. Electrons per second = 2 x 10^14, so I = 2 x 10^14 x 1.6 x 10^-19 = 3.2 x 10^-5 A.

hard.q: A proton and an alpha particle are accelerated through the same potential difference. What is lambda_proton / lambda_alpha?
hard.why: lambda = h / root(2 m q V). Alpha has m = 4 times and q = 2 times, so the ratio is root(8) = 2 root 2.

easy.q: What is the energy of the electron in the ground state of a hydrogen atom?
easy.why: The ground-state energy of hydrogen is -13.6 eV; the negative sign means the electron is bound.

easy.q: What minimum energy is needed to ionise a hydrogen atom from its ground state?
easy.why: The ground state energy is -13.6 eV, so 13.6 eV lifts the electron to zero energy.

easy.q: Which spectral series of hydrogen lies in the visible region?
easy.why: Balmer lines end on n = 2 and fall in the visible range. Lyman is ultraviolet; the others are infrared.

easy.q: According to Bohr, what is the angular momentum of the electron in the n = 2 orbit?
easy.why: L = n h / 2 pi, so for n = 2 it is h / pi.

easy.q: The first Bohr radius is 0.53 angstrom. What is the radius of the n = 3 orbit?
easy.why: r_n = n^2 r_1 = 9 x 0.53 = 4.8 angstrom.

easy.q: Some alpha particles in Rutherford's experiment bounced almost straight back. What did this show?
o: The positive charge is packed in a tiny nucleus
Electrons are heavier than alpha particles
easy.why: Only a small, dense, positive core could repel an alpha particle backwards.

medium.q: What is the energy of the n = 2 level of hydrogen?
What is the energy of the electron in the n = 4 level of hydrogen?
What is the kinetic energy of the electron in the n = 2 level of hydrogen?
medium.why: In a Bohr orbit KE = -E_total, so KE = +3.4 eV (total energy -3.4 eV).

medium.q: What is the wavelength of the photon emitted when a hydrogen electron falls from n = 4 to n = 2? (hc = 1240 eV nm)
Using R = 1.097 x 10^7 per metre, what is the shortest wavelength in the Balmer series?
medium.why: The series limit has n = infinity to 2: 1/lambda = R/4, so lambda = 4 / 1.097 x 10^7 = 365 nm.

medium.q: What is the ionisation energy of He+ (one electron, Z = 2), using E_n = -13.6 Z^2 / n^2 eV?
medium.why: Ground state energy = -13.6 x 4 = -54.4 eV, so 54.4 eV is needed to remove the electron.

hard.q: What is the wavelength of the first line of the Lyman series (n = 2 to n = 1)? (hc = 1240 eV nm)
Hydrogen atoms in n = 5 emit light in all possible ways while returning to the ground state. How many different lines can appear in total?
hard.why: Number of lines = n(n - 1)/2 = 5 x 4/2 = 10.

hard.q: What is the series limit wavelength of the Paschen series? (R = 1.097 x 10^7 per metre)
hard.why: Paschen lines end on n = 3. At the limit 1/lambda = R/9, so lambda = 9 / 1.097 x 10^7 = 820 nm.

hard.q: An electron in He+ falls from n = 2 to n = 1. What photon energy is emitted? (Use E_n = -13.6 Z^2 / n^2 eV)
Hydrogen atoms in the ground state are hit by electrons of kinetic energy 12.5 eV. How many different spectral lines can they emit?
hard.why: 12.5 eV can excite n = 3 (12.09 eV) but not n = 4 (12.75 eV). From n = 3 the lines are 3-2, 3-1, 2-1: three.

hard.q: The speed of the electron in the first Bohr orbit of hydrogen is 2.19 x 10^6 m/s. What is its speed in the n = 3 orbit?
hard.why: Speed in orbit n is v1 / n, so 2.19 x 10^6 / 3 = 7.3 x 10^5 m/s.

easy.q: How many nucleons are there in a chlorine-35 nucleus with 17 protons?
easy.why: The mass number 35 is the total number of protons and neutrons.

easy.q: Which force holds protons and neutrons together inside a nucleus?
easy.why: The strong force is attractive, short-ranged and much stronger than the proton-proton repulsion.

easy.q: How many neutrons are there in the nucleus of uranium-238 (atomic number 92)?
easy.why: Neutrons = mass number - atomic number = 238 - 92 = 146.

easy.q: Nuclear radius follows R = R0 A^(1/3) with R0 = 1.2 fm. What is the radius of a nucleus with A = 27?
What is the composition of an alpha particle?
easy.why: An alpha particle is a helium-4 nucleus: A = 4, Z = 2.

easy.q: Uranium-238 (Z = 92) emits one alpha particle. What are the mass number and atomic number of the daughter?
easy.why: An alpha carries away 4 nucleons and 2 protons: A = 234, Z = 90.

medium.q: A radioactive element has half-life 5 days. What is its decay constant? (ln 2 = 0.693)
Sodium-24 (Z = 11) undergoes beta-minus decay. What is the atomic number of the daughter?
medium.why: A neutron turns into a proton, so Z rises by 1 and A stays 24.

medium.q: What fraction of a radioactive sample has decayed after 3 half-lives?
medium.why: Undecayed fraction = (1/2)^3 = 1/8, so 7/8 has decayed.

medium.q: If the mass number of a nucleus doubles, how does its density change (approximately)?
medium.why: Mass is proportional to A and volume is proportional to R^3, which is proportional to A. Density is about 2.3 x 10^17 kg/m^3 for all nuclei.

medium.q: The mass defect of a helium-4 nucleus is 0.0304 u. What is its binding energy per nucleon? (1 u = 931.5 MeV)
medium.why: Total = 0.0304 x 931.5 = 28.3 MeV. Dividing by 4 nucleons gives 7.1 MeV.

medium.q: A nucleus has a mass defect of 0.03 u. What is its binding energy? (1 u = 931.5 MeV)

hard.q: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 6.93 hours. What is its mean life? (ln 2 = 0.693)
hard.why: Mean life = T / ln 2 = 6.93 / 0.693 = 10 hours.

hard.q: The activity of a sample falls from 800 Bq to 100 Bq in 6 hours. What is its half-life?
hard.why: 800 to 100 is a fall by 1/8, which is 3 half-lives. Half-life = 6 / 3 = 2 hours.

hard.q: Four hydrogen atoms (1.007825 u each) fuse into one helium atom (4.002603 u). What energy is released? (1 u = 931.5 MeV; ignore positron effects)
Radium-226 (226.0254 u) decays by alpha emission to radon-222 (222.0176 u). With the helium-4 mass 4.0026 u, what is the energy released? (1 u = 931.5 MeV)
Samples A and B start with equal numbers of nuclei. Their half-lives are 2 hours and 6 hours. After 6 hours, what is the ratio of activities A : B?
hard.why: A has (1/2)^3 = 1/8 left, B has 1/2. Activity = lambda N, with lambda inversely proportional to T: A : B = (1/2)(1/8) : (1/6)(1/2) = 1/16 : 1/12 = 3 : 4.

hard.q: The deuteron mass is 2.014102 u, the proton (hydrogen atom) 1.007825 u and the neutron 1.008665 u. What is the binding energy per nucleon? (1 u = 931.5 MeV)
hard.why: Mass defect = 0.002388 u, giving 2.22 MeV. Divide by 2 nucleons to get 1.11 MeV.

easy.q: What are the majority carriers in a p-type semiconductor?
easy.why: Trivalent dopants create holes, which are the majority carriers in p-type material.

easy.q: How does a pure semiconductor behave at absolute zero temperature?
easy.why: At 0 K all electrons are in the valence band, so there are no free carriers.

easy.q: An ideal full-wave rectifier is fed with a 50 Hz AC input. What is the frequency of its output ripple?
easy.why: A full-wave rectifier uses both half cycles, so ripple frequency is twice the input.

easy.q: What happens to the depletion region of a p-n junction under reverse bias?
easy.why: Reverse bias pulls carriers away from the junction, so the depletion layer grows and only a tiny leakage current flows.

easy.q: What is the output of an OR gate when inputs are A = 1 and B = 0?
easy.why: An OR gate gives 1 if at least one input is 1.

easy.q: Which element can be added to silicon to make a p-type semiconductor?
easy.why: Boron is trivalent (group 13), so it creates holes. The others are pentavalent donors.

medium.q: A transistor has current gain beta = 80 and base current 25 microampere. What is its collector current?
In a transistor the base current is 20 microampere and the collector current is 1.98 mA. What is the emitter current?
In a transistor the base current is 40 microampere and the collector current is 4 mA. What is the current gain beta?
medium.why: beta = I_C / I_B = 4 mA / 40 microampere = 100.

medium.q: A half-wave rectifier with an ideal diode is fed with a sine wave of peak 10 V. What is the average (dc) output voltage?
medium.why: For a half-wave rectifier V_dc = V_peak / pi = 10 / 3.14 = 3.18 V.

medium.q: The band gap of silicon is about 1.1 eV. What is the longest wavelength of light that can create an electron-hole pair? (hc = 1240 eV nm)
Silicon has intrinsic carrier density 1.5 x 10^16 per m^3. It is doped with 10^22 donors per m^3. What is the hole density?

hard.q: A 6 V battery is connected in series with a forward-biased silicon diode (drop 0.7 V) and a 530 ohm resistor. What current flows?
hard.why: The resistor gets 6 - 0.7 = 5.3 V. I = 5.3 / 530 = 10 mA.

hard.q: A common-emitter amplifier has beta = 100, collector resistor 5 kilo-ohm and input resistance 1 kilo-ohm. What is its voltage gain?
hard.why: A_v = beta R_C / R_in = 100 x 5000 / 1000 = 500. (50000 would be the power gain, beta x A_v.)

hard.q: The two inputs of a NAND gate are joined together. Which gate does it behave as?
hard.why: With A = B the output is NOT(A AND A) = NOT A.

hard.q: What is the least number of 2-input NAND gates needed to build one AND gate?
hard.why: AND = NAND followed by a NOT, and a NOT is a NAND with inputs tied. That is two gates.

hard.q: A 15 V supply feeds a 9 V Zener diode through a 500 ohm series resistor. A 1.5 kilo-ohm load is connected across the Zener. What current flows through the Zener?
hard.why: Current in series resistor = (15 - 9) / 500 = 12 mA. Load current = 9 / 1500 = 6 mA. Zener current = 12 - 6 = 6 mA.

hard.q: An n-type sample has 5 x 10^21 electrons per m^3 and electron mobility 0.1 m^2/(V s). Ignoring holes, what is its resistivity? (e = 1.6 x 10^-19 C)
hard.why: Conductivity = n e mu = 5 x 10^21 x 1.6 x 10^-19 x 0.1 = 80 S/m. Resistivity = 1/80 = 1.25 x 10^-2 ohm m.
